## File: .claude/skills/auth-patterns/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: name: auth-patterns
  2: description: Guidelines for authentication and authorization patterns covering OIDC, JWT, and BFF security in .NET Clean Architecture projects.
  3: type: domain
  4: enforcement: suggest
  5: priority: critical
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # Authentication & Authorization Patterns
  9: 
 10: > **Project-Agnostic Authentication & Authorization Guide**
 11: >
 12: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 13: 
 14: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 15: 
 16: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 17: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 18: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 19: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server (BFF) project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 20: | `{Project}.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM project | `Explore.Blazor.Client` |
 21: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `Explore.API` |
 22: 
 23: ---
 24: 
 25: ## 🎯 Purpose
 26: 
 27: This skill provides the standard patterns for implementing security in .NET Clean Architecture projects. It covers the OIDC/JWT authentication flow, the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) security model, and authorization conventions.
 28: 
 29: ## ⚡ When This Skill Activates
 30: 
 31: **Triggered by**:
 32: - Keywords: "auth", "security", "jwt", "oidc", "keycloak", "authorize", "claim"
 33: - File patterns: `*Controller.cs`, `*Program.cs` (for auth setup)
 34: 
 35: ## 📚 Resources
 36: 
 37: | Resource | Description |
 38: |----------|-------------|
 39: | [user-id-extraction.md](resources/user-id-extraction.md) | The critical fallback pattern for extracting user ID from JWT claims. |
 40: 
 41: ## 1. Authentication Architecture: BFF with OIDC & JWT
 42: 
 43: The project uses a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern to handle authentication, which provides a strong security posture by never exposing tokens to the browser.
 44: 
 45: ```mermaid
 46: sequenceDiagram
 47:     participant Browser (Blazor WASM)
 48:     participant BFF (Blazor Server)
 49:     participant Keycloak
 50:     participant API (Backend)
 51: 
 52:     Browser->>+BFF: User clicks "Login"
 53:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Initiates OIDC Authorization Code Flow
 54:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Redirects with Authorization Code
 55:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Exchanges Code for Tokens (Access + Refresh)
 56:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Returns JWTs
 57:     BFF-->>-Browser: Stores tokens in secure, HttpOnly cookie & redirects
 58: 
 59:     Browser->>+BFF: Makes API call (/api/v1/...)
 60:     BFF->>+API: YARP proxy reads token from cookie, attaches as "Authorization: Bearer" header
 61:     API->>API: Validates JWT signature & claims
 62:     API-->>-BFF: Returns data
 63:     BFF-->>-Browser: Returns data to client
 64: ```
 65: 
 66: *   **`{Project}.Blazor` (BFF)**: Is the OIDC client. It handles the redirect to the identity provider and manages the user's session via a cookie.
 67: *   **`{Project}.Blazor.Client` (WASM)**: Is not OIDC-aware. It simply includes credentials (the cookie) with every request to its backend (the BFF).
 68: *   **`{Project}.API`**: Is a stateless service that only trusts JWT Bearer tokens. It has no knowledge of the user's session cookie.
 69: 
 70: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 71: - **`Explore.Blazor`**: BFF using Keycloak as the identity provider
 72: - **`Explore.Blazor.Client`**: Blazor WASM client
 73: - **`Explore.API`**: Stateless API validating Keycloak-issued JWTs
 74: 
 75: ## 2. Authorization Conventions
 76: 
 77: ### Controller Endpoint Authorization
 78: 
 79: A simple and strict convention is followed for API endpoints:
 80: *   **`GET` requests are public**: Decorated with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
 81: *   **`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` requests are protected**: Decorated with `[Authorize]`.
 82: *   **Admin-only operations**: Decorated with `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`.
 83: 
 84: **Generic Template:**
 85: ```csharp
 86: // ✅ Public read access
 87: [HttpGet]
 88: [AllowAnonymous]
 89: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
 90: {
 91:     var {entities} = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest());
 92:     return Ok({entities});
 93: }
 94: 
 95: // ✅ Authenticated write access
 96: [HttpPost]
 97: [Authorize]
 98: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto {entity})
 99: {
100:     var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = {entity} };
101:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
102:     return Ok(response);
103: }
104: 
105: // ✅ Admin-only access
106: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
107: [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]
108: public async Task<ActionResult> DeletePermanent({IdType} id)
109: {
110:     var result = await _mediator.Send(new Delete{Entity}PermanentlyCommand { Id = id });
111:     return result ? NoContent() : NotFound();
112: }
113: ```
114: 
115: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
116: ```csharp
117: [HttpGet]
118: [AllowAnonymous]
119: public async Task<ActionResult<List<EventListDto>>> GetAll()
120: {
121:     var events = await _mediator.Send(new GetEventListRequest());
122:     return Ok(events);
123: }
124: 
125: [HttpPost]
126: [Authorize]
127: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto @event)
128: {
129:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = @event };
130:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
131:     return Ok(response);
132: }
133: ```
134: 
135: ### Resource-Level Authorization
136: 
137: Resource-level authorization (e.g., "can this user edit *this specific* event?") is the responsibility of the **MediatR handler** in the Application layer, not the controller.
138: 
139: ```csharp
140: // Example: DeleteEventCommandHandler
141: public async Task<bool> Handle(DeleteEventCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
142: {
143:     // The handler receives the UserId from the controller
144:     var @event = await _eventRepository.GetById(request.Id);
145: 
146:     if (@event == null)
147:         return false; // Not found
148: 
149:     // ✅ Handler enforces ownership logic
150:     var actor = await _actorRepository.GetById(@event.ActorId);
151:     if (actor == null || actor.UserId.ToString() != request.UserId)
152:     {
153:         // User does not own the event, deny deletion
154:         return false;
155:     }
156: 
157:     await _eventRepository.Delete(@event);
158:     return true;
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: ## 3. User ID Extraction from JWT Claims
163: 
164: For the **CRITICAL PATTERN** for safely and consistently extracting the user ID from JWT claims, including the fallback mechanism for `sub`, `nameidentifier`, and `sid`, refer to [user-id-extraction.md](resources/user-id-extraction.md).
165: 
166: ---
167: **Related Skills**:
168: - `clean-architecture-rules`
169: - `blazor-bff-patterns`
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/resources/auth-state-management.md
````markdown
  1: # Authentication State Management
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Authentication State Management**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: >
  7: > **Note**: Code examples use ISLAMU Event (Explore) implementation. Replace with your project names.
  8: 
  9: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 10: 
 11: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 12: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 13: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 14: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server (BFF) project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 15: | `{Project}.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM project | `Explore.Blazor.Client` |
 16: 
 17: ---
 18: 
 19: This document describes how authentication state is managed and shared across the Blazor Hybrid application, especially between the Blazor Server (BFF) and Blazor WebAssembly (WASM) components.
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## 1. Authentication State Serialization
 24: 
 25: To seamlessly transition user authentication from the server-rendered part to the client-rendered part of the Blazor Hybrid app, the authentication state is serialized.
 26: 
 27: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs` (Server-side Blazor)
 28: 
 29: ```csharp
 30: builder.Services.AddRazorComponents()
 31:     .AddInteractiveServerComponents()
 32:     .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents()
 33:     .AddAuthenticationStateSerialization(options => 
 34:         options.SerializeAllClaims = true);  // ✅ Serialize all claims for WASM
 35:                                             // This makes user claims available client-side
 36: builder.Services.AddCascadingAuthenticationState(); // Makes AuthenticationStateProvider injectable
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs` (Blazor WebAssembly)
 40: 
 41: ```csharp
 42: builder.Services.AddAuthorizationCore(); // Basic authorization services
 43: builder.Services.AddCascadingAuthenticationState(); // Enables CascadingAuthenticationState
 44: builder.Services.AddAuthenticationStateDeserialization(); // Deserializes the auth state from the server
 45: ```
 46: 
 47: ### Key Points
 48: 
 49: *   **`AddAuthenticationStateSerialization`**: On the server, this captures the authenticated user's claims and includes them in the rendered HTML output.
 50: *   **`AddAuthenticationStateDeserialization`**: On the client, this reads the serialized claims from the HTML and re-establishes the authentication state.
 51: *   **`AddCascadingAuthenticationState`**: Makes the `AuthenticationStateProvider` and `Task<AuthenticationState>` available via `CascadingParameter` in components.
 52: 
 53: ---
 54: 
 55: ## 2. Accessing Authentication State in Components
 56: 
 57: Once serialized, the authentication state can be accessed in any Blazor component.
 58: 
 59: ### Using `AuthorizeView` (Declarative)
 60: 
 61: The `AuthorizeView` component selectively displays UI content based on the user's authentication and authorization status.
 62: 
 63: ```razor
 64: <CascadingAuthenticationState>
 65:     <AuthorizeView>
 66:         <Authorized>
 67:             <MudText>Welcome, @context.User.Identity?.Name!</MudText>
 68:             <MudButton OnClick="CreateEvent">Create Event</MudButton>
 69:         </Authorized>
 70:         <NotAuthorized>
 71:             <MudButton Href="/login">Login to Create Events</MudButton>
 72:         </NotAuthorized>
 73:         <Authorizing>
 74:             <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" /> Loading authentication...
 75:         </Authorizing>
 76:     </AuthorizeView>
 77: </CascadingAuthenticationState>
 78: ```
 79: 
 80: ### Accessing Programmatically (Imperative)
 81: 
 82: For logic that depends on the authentication state, inject `AuthenticationStateProvider`.
 83: 
 84: ```csharp
 85: @inject AuthenticationStateProvider AuthenticationStateProvider
 86: 
 87: @code {
 88:     private string? _currentUserName;
 89:     private bool _isAuthenticated;
 90:     private Guid? _currentUserId;
 91: 
 92:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 93:     {
 94:         var authState = await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
 95:         var user = authState.User;
 96: 
 97:         _isAuthenticated = user.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
 98:         _currentUserName = user.Identity?.Name;
 99:         _currentUserId = Guid.TryParse(user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value, out var id) ? id : (Guid?)null;
100: 
101:         // You can also access specific claims:
102:         var emailClaim = user.FindFirst("email")?.Value;
103:         var roles = user.FindAll("realm_access.roles").Select(c => c.Value).ToList();
104:     }
105: }
106: ```
107: 
108: ### Key Claims
109: 
110: When accessing claims, be aware of the common types and the fallback pattern for User ID:
111: 
112: *   `context.User.Identity?.Name`: Typically the `preferred_username` or `name` claim.
113: *   `user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value`: The standard OIDC subject (user ID) claim.
114: *   `user.FindFirst("email")?.Value`: The user's email address.
115: *   `user.FindAll("realm_access.roles").Select(c => c.Value)`: Roles assigned to the user in Keycloak.
116: 
117: *For the critical User ID extraction fallback pattern, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill.*
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 3. WASM Message Handlers for Authentication
122: 
123: In the Blazor WASM client (`Explore.Blazor.Client`), custom `DelegatingHandler`s are used to manage credentials (cookies) and handle unauthorized responses.
124: 
125: ### `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler`
126: 
127: Ensures that credentials (the session cookie) are included with every HTTP request made by the WASM client to the BFF.
128: 
129: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler.cs`
130: 
131: ```csharp
132: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
133: 
134: using System.Net.Http;
135: using System.Threading;
136: using System.Threading.Tasks;
137: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Http;
138: 
139: public class BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler : DelegatingHandler
140: {
141:     protected override Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
142:         HttpRequestMessage request, 
143:         CancellationToken cancellationToken)
144:     {
145:         // ✅ CRITICAL: Include cookies with requests to the BFF
146:         request.SetBrowserRequestCredentials(BrowserRequestCredentials.Include);
147:         return base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
148:     }
149: }
150: ```
151: 
152: ### `BffUnauthorizedHandler`
153: 
154: Intercepts `401 Unauthorized` responses from the BFF and redirects the user to the login page.
155: 
156: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/BffUnauthorizedHandler.cs`
157: 
158: ```csharp
159: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
160: 
161: using System.Net;
162: using System.Net.Http;
163: using System.Threading;
164: using System.Threading.Tasks;
165: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components;
166: 
167: public class BffUnauthorizedHandler : DelegatingHandler
168: {
169:     private readonly NavigationManager _navigationManager;
170: 
171:     public BffUnauthorizedHandler(NavigationManager navigationManager)
172:     {
173:         _navigationManager = navigationManager;
174:     }
175: 
176:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
177:         HttpRequestMessage request, 
178:         CancellationToken cancellationToken)
179:     {
180:         var response = await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
181: 
182:         if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized)
183:         {
184:             // ✅ Redirect to login page if 401 Unauthorized is received
185:             _navigationManager.NavigateTo("/login?returnUrl=" + Uri.EscapeDataString(_navigationManager.Uri));
186:         }
187: 
188:         return response;
189:     }
190: }
191: ```
192: 
193: ### Registration of WASM Message Handlers
194: 
195: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs`
196: 
197: ```csharp
198: builder.Services.AddTransient<BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler>();
199: builder.Services.AddTransient<BffUnauthorizedHandler>();
200: 
201: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
202: {
203:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress);
204: })
205: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler>()  // Attaches cookies
206: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BffUnauthorizedHandler>();           // Handles 401 redirects
207: ```
208: 
209: ---
210: 
211: **Related Documentation**:
212: - [token-forwarding.md](token-forwarding.md) - Details on server-side token management.
213: - [`auth-patterns`](../../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - Comprehensive authentication patterns.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/resources/bff-configuration.md
````markdown
  1: # BFF Configuration
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic BFF Configuration with YARP**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: >
  7: > **Note**: All code examples use the ISLAMU Event (Explore) implementation. Replace project-specific names with your values.
  8: 
  9: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 10: 
 11: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 12: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 13: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 14: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server (BFF) project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 15: | `{Project}.API` | Backend API project | `Explore.API` |
 16: | `{project}` | camelCase project name | `explore` |
 17: 
 18: ---
 19: 
 20: This document details the configuration for the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern using YARP (Yet Another Reverse Proxy) in the `{Project}.Blazor` project.
 21: 
 22: ---
 23: 
 24: ## 1. YARP Reverse Proxy Setup
 25: 
 26: YARP is used to proxy API calls from the Blazor client to the `Explore.API` backend. This is crucial for the BFF pattern as it allows for server-side token management.
 27: 
 28: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`
 29: 
 30: ```csharp
 31: // Define the base URL for the backend API
 32: var exploreApiBaseUrl = builder.Configuration["ExploreApi:BaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:7039/";
 33: 
 34: // Configure proxy routes: requests matching this path will be forwarded
 35: var proxyRoutes = new[]
 36: {
 37:     new RouteConfig
 38:     {
 39:         RouteId = "explore-api", // Unique ID for this route
 40:         ClusterId = "explore-api", // ID of the cluster to forward to
 41:         Match = new RouteMatch
 42:         {
 43:             // All requests starting with /api/v1/ will be proxied
 44:             Path = "/api/v1/{**catchall}"
 45:         }
 46:     }
 47: };
 48: 
 49: // Configure proxy clusters: defines the actual backend services
 50: var proxyClusters = new[]
 51: {
 52:     new ClusterConfig
 53:     {
 54:         ClusterId = "explore-api", // Must match the ClusterId in RouteConfig
 55:         Destinations = new Dictionary<string, DestinationConfig>
 56:         {
 57:             // Define one or more destinations for the cluster
 58:             ["primary"] = new() { Address = exploreApiBaseUrl }
 59:         }
 60:     }
 61: };
 62: 
 63: // Add YARP to the service collection and load configuration
 64: builder.Services.AddReverseProxy()
 65:     .LoadFromMemory(proxyRoutes, proxyClusters)
 66:     .AddTransforms(context =>
 67:     {
 68:         // This transform is CRITICAL for forwarding the JWT
 69:         context.AddRequestTransform(async transformContext =>
 70:         {
 71:             var httpContext = transformContext.HttpContext;
 72:             // Get the access token from the secure cookie
 73:             var token = await httpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token");
 74:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
 75:             {
 76:                 // Attach the token as a Bearer header to the proxied request
 77:                 transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization =
 78:                     new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
 79:             }
 80:         });
 81:     });
 82: ```
 83: 
 84: ### Key Points
 85: 
 86: *   **`exploreApiBaseUrl`**: Should be configured in `appsettings.json` or environment variables.
 87: *   **`Path = "/api/v1/{**catchall}"`**: This route captures all requests intended for the backend API.
 88: *   **`AddTransforms`**: This is where the magic happens. It intercepts the outgoing request from the BFF to the API, extracts the JWT from the user's session cookie (which was obtained during OIDC login), and attaches it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header. This makes the backend API oblivious to the cookie-based authentication, only seeing standard JWTs.
 89: 
 90: ---
 91: 
 92: ## 2. Authentication Endpoint Mapping
 93: 
 94: These endpoints handle the login and logout flows, leveraging ASP.NET Core's built-in authentication handlers.
 95: 
 96: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`
 97: 
 98: ```csharp
 99: // Endpoint for initiating the login process
100: app.MapGet("/login", async ctx =>
101: {
102:     var returnUrl = ctx.Request.Query["returnUrl"].ToString();
103:     // Challenge the user with the OpenID Connect scheme, which redirects to Keycloak
104:     await ctx.ChallengeAsync(
105:         OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme,
106:         new AuthenticationProperties
107:         {
108:             // After successful login, redirect to the original URL or home
109:             RedirectUri = string.IsNullOrEmpty(returnUrl) ? "/" : returnUrl
110:         }
111:     );
112: });
113: 
114: // Endpoint for initiating the logout process
115: app.MapGet("/logout", async ctx =>
116: {
117:     // Sign out from cookie authentication
118:     await ctx.SignOutAsync(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme);
119:     // Sign out from OpenID Connect, which typically redirects to Keycloak's logout endpoint
120:     await ctx.SignOutAsync(
121:         OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme,
122:         new AuthenticationProperties { RedirectUri = "/" }
123:     );
124: });
125: 
126: // Optional: An endpoint to expose basic user information to the client
127: // This prevents the client from needing to parse claims from the cookie directly
128: app.MapGet("/bff/me", (HttpContext ctx) =>
129: {
130:     if (ctx.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated != true)
131:     {
132:         return Results.Unauthorized(); // Return 401 if not authenticated
133:     }
134: 
135:     // Return selected claims to the client
136:     return Results.Ok(new
137:     {
138:         Name = ctx.User.Identity?.Name,
139:         Claims = ctx.User.Claims.Select(c => new { c.Type, c.Value })
140:     });
141: });
142: ```
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## 3. NSwag API Client Configuration
147: 
148: NSwag generates C# clients for your OpenAPI/Swagger API. These clients need to be configured correctly in the BFF (`Explore.Blazor`) and the WASM client (`Explore.Blazor.Client`).
149: 
150: ### BFF (Blazor Server) Configuration
151: 
152: In the Blazor Server component of the hybrid app, the NSwag client can directly access the backend API because it's running on the server. The `AccessTokenForwardingHandler` ensures JWTs are sent.
153: 
154: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`
155: 
156: ```csharp
157: var exploreApiBaseUrl = builder.Configuration["ExploreApi:BaseUrl"] ?? "https://localhost:7039/";
158: 
159: // Register the NSwag generated API client
160: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
161: {
162:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(exploreApiBaseUrl); // Direct API base URL
163: })
164: .AddHttpMessageHandler<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>() // Custom handler to attach JWT
165: .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() =>
166: {
167:     // Custom HttpClientHandler to allow self-signed certs in development
168:     var handler = new HttpClientHandler();
169:     if (builder.Environment.IsDevelopment())
170:     {
171:         handler.ServerCertificateCustomValidationCallback = 
172:             (message, cert, chain, errors) =>
173:             {
174:                 var isLocalhost = message.RequestUri?.Host.Contains("localhost") ?? false;
175:                 return isLocalhost || errors == System.Net.Security.SslPolicyErrors.None;
176:             };
177:     }
178:     return handler;
179: });
180: ```
181: 
182: ### WASM Client (`Explore.Blazor.Client`) Configuration
183: 
184: In the Blazor WebAssembly client, the NSwag client should **NOT** directly call the backend API. Instead, it calls the **BFF itself**, and the BFF's YARP proxy then forwards the request.
185: 
186: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs`
187: 
188: ```csharp
189: // Register the NSwag generated API client for the WASM client
190: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
191: {
192:     // Base address is the WASM app's own base address, which routes to the BFF
193:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress);
194: })
195: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler>() // Attaches cookies to outgoing requests
196: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BffUnauthorizedHandler>();           // Handles 401 Unauthorized responses
197: ```
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: **Related Documentation**:
202: - [token-forwarding.md](token-forwarding.md) - Details on `AccessTokenForwardingHandler`.
203: - [auth-state-management.md](auth-state-management.md) - Context for `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler` and `BffUnauthorizedHandler`.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/resources/service-layer-patterns.md
````markdown
  1: # Service Layer Patterns
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Service Layer Patterns for Blazor**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: >
  7: > **Note**: All code examples in this document use the ISLAMU Event (Explore) implementation as a concrete reference. Replace `Explore`, `Event`, and related names with your project-specific values.
  8: 
  9: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 10: 
 11: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 12: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 13: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 14: | `{Project}.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM project | `Explore.Blazor.Client` |
 15: | `{Entity}` | Main entity (singular) | `Event` |
 16: | `{Entities}` | Entity plural | `Events` |
 17: | `{entity}` | camelCase entity | `event` |
 18: | `{IdType}` | Primary key type | `Guid` |
 19: 
 20: ---
 21: 
 22: This document describes the recommended pattern for creating a service layer that wraps the NSwag-generated API clients in the Blazor frontend.
 23: 
 24: ---
 25: 
 26: ## 1. Purpose of the Service Layer
 27: 
 28: The primary goal of this service layer is to provide an abstraction over the raw API client, offering several benefits:
 29: 
 30: *   **Error Handling**: Centralized and consistent error handling, preventing exceptions from bubbling up directly to UI components.
 31: *   **Logging**: Standardized logging for API calls and their outcomes.
 32: *   **Safe Defaults**: Returning empty collections or `null`s instead of throwing exceptions on expected API failures (e.g., 404 Not Found).
 33: *   **Decoupling**: Isolating UI components from direct knowledge of the API client's methods or specific HTTP status codes.
 34: *   **Reusability**: Encapsulating common API call logic.
 35: 
 36: ---
 37: 
 38: ## 2. Service Layer Structure
 39: 
 40: ### Service Interface (`I{Entity}Service.cs`)
 41: 
 42: Define an interface for each entity or domain area that exposes methods for common operations.
 43: 
 44: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/IEventService.cs`
 45: 
 46: ```csharp
 47: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
 48: 
 49: using Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients; // NSwag generated client
 50: using Explore.Application.DTOs.Event; // Shared DTOs
 51: using Explore.Application.Responses; // Shared command responses
 52: 
 53: public interface IEventService
 54: {
 55:     Task<ICollection<EventListDto>> GetAllEventsAsync();
 56:     Task<EventDto?> GetEventByIdAsync(Guid eventId);
 57:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> CreateEventAsync(CreateEventDto dto);
 58:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> UpdateEventAsync(Guid id, UpdateEventDto dto);
 59:     Task<bool> DeleteEventAsync(Guid eventId);
 60: }
 61: ```
 62: 
 63: ### Service Implementation (`{Entity}Service.cs`)
 64: 
 65: Implement the interface, injecting the NSwag-generated API client and `ILogger`. Each method should include `try-catch` blocks to handle `ApiException` (from NSwag) and general exceptions.
 66: 
 67: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/EventService.cs`
 68: 
 69: ```csharp
 70: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
 71: 
 72: using Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients; // NSwag generated client
 73: using Explore.Application.DTOs.Event; // Shared DTOs
 74: using Explore.Application.Responses; // Shared command responses
 75: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
 76: using System;
 77: using System.Collections.Generic;
 78: using System.Net.Http;
 79: using System.Threading.Tasks;
 80: 
 81: public class EventService : IEventService
 82: {
 83:     private readonly IEventApiClient _apiClient;
 84:     private readonly ILogger<EventService> _logger;
 85: 
 86:     public EventService(IEventApiClient apiClient, ILogger<EventService> logger)
 87:     {
 88:         _apiClient = apiClient ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(apiClient));
 89:         _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
 90:     }
 91: 
 92:     public async Task<ICollection<EventListDto>> GetAllEventsAsync()
 93:     {
 94:         try
 95:         {
 96:             _logger.LogInformation("[EVENT SERVICE] Fetching all events...");
 97:             var response = await _apiClient.EventAllAsync();
 98:             _logger.LogInformation("[EVENT SERVICE] Received {Count} events", response?.Count ?? 0);
 99:             return response ?? new List<EventListDto>(); // ✅ Return safe default
100:         }
101:         catch (ApiException ex)
102:         {
103:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[EVENT SERVICE] API error: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
104:             return new List<EventListDto>(); // ✅ Return safe default on API error
105:         }
106:         catch (Exception ex)
107:         {
108:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[EVENT SERVICE] Error fetching events");
109:             return new List<EventListDto>(); // ✅ Return safe default on unexpected error
110:         }
111:     }
112: 
113:     public async Task<EventDto?> GetEventByIdAsync(Guid eventId)
114:     {
115:         try
116:         {
117:             return await _apiClient.EventGETAsync(eventId);
118:         }
119:         catch (ApiException ex) when (ex.StatusCode == 404) // ✅ Specific handling for 404
120:         {
121:             _logger.LogWarning("[EVENT SERVICE] Event not found: {EventId}", eventId);
122:             return null; // ✅ Return null for not found
123:         }
124:         catch (Exception ex)
125:         {
126:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[EVENT SERVICE] Error fetching event {EventId}", eventId);
127:             return null;
128:         }
129:     }
130: 
131:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> CreateEventAsync(CreateEventDto dto)
132:     {
133:         try
134:         {
135:             _logger.LogInformation("[EVENT SERVICE] Creating event: {Title}", dto.Title);
136:             return await _apiClient.EventPOSTAsync(dto);
137:         }
138:         catch (ApiException ex)
139:         {
140:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[EVENT SERVICE] API error creating event: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
141:             // ✅ Return error response object for command failures
142:             return new BaseCommandResponseOfGuid
143:             {
144:                 Success = false,
145:                 Message = $"API error: {ex.Message}",
146:                 Errors = new List<string> { ex.Response ?? ex.Message }
147:             };
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151:     public async Task<bool> DeleteEventAsync(Guid eventId)
152:     {
153:         try
154:         {
155:             await _apiClient.EventDELETEAsync(eventId);
156:             return true;
157:         }
158:         catch (Exception ex)
159:         {
160:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[EVENT SERVICE] Error deleting event {EventId}", eventId);
161:             return false;
162:         }
163:     }
164: }
165: ```
166: 
167: ### Key Practices
168: 
169: *   **Error Handling**: Use `try-catch` blocks to specifically handle `ApiException` (which NSwag clients throw for HTTP errors) and general `Exception`s.
170: *   **Safe Defaults**: Always return an empty collection (`new List<T>()`) for list methods or `null` for single-item methods on failure, rather than re-throwing exceptions.
171: *   **Logging**: Log API call status, errors, and any specific warnings.
172: *   **Command Responses**: For command-type operations (Create, Update, Delete), return the `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>` object, which explicitly contains `Success`, `Message`, `Id`, and `Errors` properties.
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## 3. Service Registration
177: 
178: Register service interfaces and implementations in the Dependency Injection container. Services that manage state for a user's session should be `Scoped`.
179: 
180: **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs`
181: 
182: ```csharp
183: // Register the NSwag generated API client
184: // This uses HttpClient, configured with message handlers for credentials and 401 redirects
185: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
186: {
187:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(builder.HostEnvironment.BaseAddress);
188: })
189: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler>()
190: .AddHttpMessageHandler<BffUnauthorizedHandler>();
191: 
192: // Register custom services as scoped
193: builder.Services.AddScoped<IEventService, EventService>();
194: builder.Services.AddScoped<ICategoryService, CategoryService>();
195: builder.Services.AddScoped<ITagService, TagService>();
196: // ... other services
197: ```
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: **Related Documentation**:
202: - [bff-configuration.md](bff-configuration.md) - How NSwag clients are configured for BFF.
203: - [auth-state-management.md](auth-state-management.md) - Use of `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler` and `BffUnauthorizedHandler`.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/resources/token-forwarding.md
````markdown
  1: # Token Forwarding
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Token Forwarding Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: >
  7: > **Note**: Code examples use ISLAMU Event (Explore) implementation. Replace with your project names.
  8: 
  9: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 10: 
 11: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 12: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 13: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 14: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server (BFF) project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 15: | `{Entity}` | Main entity | `Event` |
 16: 
 17: ---
 18: 
 19: This document details how access tokens are forwarded from the Blazor BFF (Backend-for-Frontend) to the backend API, especially in the context of Blazor Hybrid rendering.
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## 1. YARP Request Transform (BFF to API)
 24: 
 25: This is the primary mechanism for forwarding the JWT from the user's session cookie to the backend API. It occurs server-side within the BFF.
 26: 
 27: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`
 28: 
 29: ```csharp
 30: builder.Services.AddReverseProxy()
 31:     // ... other YARP configurations
 32:     .AddTransforms(context =>
 33:     {
 34:         context.AddRequestTransform(async transformContext =>
 35:         {
 36:             var httpContext = transformContext.HttpContext;
 37:             // Extract the access token from the secure, HttpOnly cookie
 38:             // This token was saved by the OIDC authentication middleware
 39:             var token = await httpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token");
 40: 
 41:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
 42:             {
 43:                 // Attach the access token as a Bearer header to the proxied request
 44:                 transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization =
 45:                     new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
 46:             }
 47:         });
 48:     });
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: ### Key Points
 52: 
 53: *   **`httpContext.GetTokenAsync("access_token")`**: This extension method from `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication` securely retrieves the access token that was stored in the cookie by the OIDC middleware during login.
 54: *   **`transformContext.ProxyRequest.Headers.Authorization`**: The extracted token is then added to the `Authorization` header of the request being forwarded to the `Explore.API` backend.
 55: *   This transform ensures that the `Explore.API` always receives a standard JWT Bearer token, making it agnostic to the BFF's cookie-based session management.
 56: 
 57: ---
 58: 
 59: ## 2. Token Forwarding for InteractiveServer Components
 60: 
 61: In a Blazor Hybrid application, components running in `InteractiveServer` mode (which use a SignalR circuit) do not have direct access to `HttpContext`. Therefore, a separate mechanism is needed to ensure the access token is available to HTTP clients used by these components.
 62: 
 63: ### `CircuitAccessTokenService` (Scoped Service)
 64: 
 65: This service holds the access token for the duration of a Blazor circuit.
 66: 
 67: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`
 68: 
 69: ```csharp
 70: namespace Explore.Blazor.Services;
 71: 
 72: public interface ICircuitAccessTokenService
 73: {
 74:     void SetAccessToken(string? token);
 75:     string? GetAccessToken();
 76: }
 77: 
 78: public class CircuitAccessTokenService : ICircuitAccessTokenService
 79: {
 80:     private string? _accessToken; // Stores the token for the current circuit
 81: 
 82:     public void SetAccessToken(string? token)
 83:     {
 84:         _accessToken = token;
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     public string? GetAccessToken()
 88:     {
 89:         return _accessToken;
 90:     }
 91: }
 92: ```
 93: 
 94: ### `AccessTokenForwardingHandler` (Delegating Handler)
 95: 
 96: This `DelegatingHandler` attaches the token from `CircuitAccessTokenService` to outgoing HTTP requests.
 97: 
 98: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Services/AccessTokenForwardingHandler.cs`
 99: 
100: ```csharp
101: namespace Explore.Blazor.Services;
102: 
103: using System.Net.Http.Headers;
104: using System.Threading;
105: using System.Threading.Tasks;
106: 
107: public class AccessTokenForwardingHandler : DelegatingHandler
108: {
109:     private readonly ICircuitAccessTokenService _tokenService;
110: 
111:     public AccessTokenForwardingHandler(ICircuitAccessTokenService tokenService)
112:     {
113:         _tokenService = tokenService;
114:     }
115: 
116:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
117:         HttpRequestMessage request, 
118:         CancellationToken cancellationToken)
119:     {
120:         var token = _tokenService.GetAccessToken(); // Get token from the circuit service
121:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
122:         {
123:             // Attach the token as a Bearer header
124:             request.Headers.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
125:         }
126: 
127:         return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
128:     }
129: }
130: ```
131: 
132: ### Registration and Usage
133: 
134: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs`
135: 
136: ```csharp
137: // Register the scoped service for the circuit and the delegating handler
138: builder.Services.AddScoped<ICircuitAccessTokenService, CircuitAccessTokenService>();
139: builder.Services.AddTransient<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>();
140: 
141: // Configure the HTTP client to use the forwarding handler
142: builder.Services.AddHttpClient<IEventApiClient, EventApiClient>(client =>
143: {
144:     client.BaseAddress = new Uri(exploreApiBaseUrl);
145: })
146: .AddHttpMessageHandler<AccessTokenForwardingHandler>(); // Attach the handler
147: ```
148: 
149: **File**: `Explore.Blazor/Components/App.razor` (or a similar root component)
150: 
151: ```razor
152: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor
153: @inject ICircuitAccessTokenService CircuitAccessTokenService // Inject the service
154: 
155: @code {
156:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
157:     {
158:         // Capture token during the initial HTTP request context (before SignalR circuit starts)
159:         var accessToken = await HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.GetTokenAsync("access_token");
160:         // Store it in the scoped service for later use by interactive components
161:         CircuitAccessTokenService.SetAccessToken(accessToken);
162:     }
163: }
164: 
165: @* This cascading value is no longer strictly needed for this pattern, but demonstrates one way to share state if desired *@
166: <CascadingValue Value="accessToken" Name="AccessToken">
167:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
168: </CascadingValue>
169: ```
170: 
171: ---
172: 
173: **Related Documentation**:
174: - [bff-configuration.md](bff-configuration.md) - General YARP configuration.
175: - [auth-state-management.md](auth-state-management.md) - Authentication state serialization for WASM.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: name: blazor-bff-patterns
  2: description: Backend for Frontend (BFF) patterns for Blazor applications. Covers YARP proxy, token forwarding, cookie-based auth, and service layer integration.
  3: type: domain
  4: enforcement: suggest
  5: priority: high
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: # Blazor BFF (Backend for Frontend) Patterns
  9: 
 10: > **Project-Agnostic BFF Patterns for Blazor Hybrid Applications**
 11: >
 12: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).

 28: ## 🎯 Purpose
 29: 
 30: Provides patterns for implementing the BFF architecture in Blazor hybrid applications. Covers YARP reverse proxy, token forwarding, authentication state management, and service layer design.
 31: 
 32: ## ⚡ When This Skill Activates
 33: 
 34: **Triggered by**:
 35: - Keywords: "bff", "backend for frontend", "yarp", "proxy", "token forwarding", "cookie auth", "authentication state"
 36: - File patterns: `**/{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs`, `**/Services/**/*.cs`, `**/Extensions/**/*.cs`
 37: - Content patterns: YARP configuration, authentication handlers, service registration
 38: 
 39: **Note**: Current file triggers are configured for the ISLAMU Event (Explore) implementation. Customize these patterns for your project.

 41: ## 🏗️ BFF Architecture
