163:         <Router AppAssembly="@typeof(App).Assembly">
164:             <Found Context="routeData">
165:                 <RouteView RouteData="@routeData" DefaultLayout="@typeof(MainLayout)" />
166:             </Found>
167:             <NotFound>
168:                 <LayoutView Layout="@typeof(MainLayout)">
169:                     <p role="alert">Sorry, there's nothing at this address.</p>
170:                 </LayoutView>
171:             </NotFound>
172:         </Router>
173:     </CascadingValue>
174: </CascadingAuthenticationState>
175: 
176: @code {
177:     private MudTheme _appTheme = new MudTheme(); // Example theme object
178: }
179: ```
180: 
181: **Consuming in a deeply nested child component**:
182: ```csharp
183: @code {
184:     [CascadingParameter] // For AuthenticationState, no Name needed
185:     public Task<AuthenticationState> AuthenticationState { get; set; } = null!;
186: 
187:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "AppTheme")] // Use Name to specify which value to cascade
188:     public MudTheme Theme { get; set; } = null!;
189: 
190:     private bool _isAuthenticated;
191:     private string _userName = string.Empty;
192: 
193:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
194:     {
195:         var authState = await AuthenticationState;
196:         _isAuthenticated = authState.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
197:         _userName = authState.User.Identity?.Name ?? "Guest";
198:         // Use Theme object
199:     }
200: }
201: ```
202: 
203: ### Theme Management Pattern
204: 
205: The application's dark/light theme setting is cascaded from `App.razor` based on a cookie, then consumed in `MainLayout.razor`.
206: 
207: **`App.razor`**:
208: ```razor
209: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor // Only available in Blazor Server
210: 
211: @code {
212:     private bool _isDarkTheme;
213: 
214:     protected override void OnInitialized()
215:     {
216:         // Read theme preference from cookie for initial render
217:         var themeCookie = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
218:         _isDarkTheme = themeCookie == "dark";
219:     }
220: }
221: 
222: <CascadingValue Value="_isDarkTheme" Name="InitialTheme">
223:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" /> @* Renders root routes *@
224: </CascadingValue>
225: ```
226: 
227: **`MainLayout.razor`**:
228: ```razor
229: @inherits LayoutComponentBase
230: 
231: @code {
232:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
233:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; } // Consumes the cascaded value
234: 
235:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme();
236:     private bool _isDarkMode;
237: 
238:     protected override void OnInitialized()
239:     {
240:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme; // Initialize local state from cascaded value
241:         // Further theme customization if needed
242:     }
243: }
244: 
245: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
246: <MudDialogProvider />
247: <MudSnackbarProvider />
248: 
249: @body
250: ```
251: *For more details on theming, refer to [theming.md](theming.md).*
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 6. Scoped Services - Shared State Across Components
256: 
257: Scoped services are excellent for managing shared, mutable state that needs to persist across multiple components within the same user session (Blazor Server) or application instance (Blazor WebAssembly).
258: 
259: ### Create a State Service
260: 
261: ```csharp
262: // Services/{Entity}StateService.cs
263: using System;
264: using System.Collections.Generic;
265: 
266: public class {Entity}StateService
267: {
268:     private {IdType}? _selected{Entity}Id; // The shared state
269: 
270:     // Event to notify subscribers when state changes
271:     public event Action? OnChange;
272: 
273:     public {IdType}? Selected{Entity}Id
274:     {
275:         get => _selected{Entity}Id;
276:         set
277:         {
278:             if (_selected{Entity}Id != value) // Only update if value changed
279:             {
280:                 _selected{Entity}Id = value;
281:                 NotifyStateChanged(); // Notify subscribers
282:             }
283:         }
284:     }
285: 
286:     private void NotifyStateChanged() => OnChange?.Invoke();
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: ### Register the Service
291: 
292: Register scoped services in `Program.cs` for both `{Project}.Blazor` (Server) and `{Project}.Blazor.Client` (WebAssembly).
293: 
294: **`Program.cs` (Blazor Server or WASM)**:
295: ```csharp
296: builder.Services.AddScoped<{Entity}StateService>();
297: ```
298: 
299: ### Use the Service in Components
300: 
301: **Component A (Sets State)**:
302: ```razor
303: @inject {Entity}StateService {Entity}State // Inject the service
304: 
305: <MudButton OnClick="Select{Entity}">Select This {Entity}</MudButton>
306: 
307: @code {
308:     [Parameter] public {IdType} {Entity}Id { get; set; }
309: 
310:     private void Select{Entity}()
311:     {
312:         {Entity}State.Selected{Entity}Id = {Entity}Id; // Update the shared state
313:     }
314: }
315: ```
316: 
317: **Component B (Reacts to State)**:
318: ```razor
319: @inject {Entity}StateService {Entity}State
320: @implements IDisposable // Implement IDisposable for event cleanup
321: 
322: <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">Currently Selected {Entity}: @{Entity}State.Selected{Entity}Id</MudText>
323: 
324: @code {
325:     protected override void OnInitialized()
326:     {
327:         {Entity}State.OnChange += StateHasChanged; // Subscribe to state changes, force re-render
328:     }
329: 
330:     public void Dispose()
331:     {
332:         {Entity}State.OnChange -= StateHasChanged; // Unsubscribe to prevent memory leaks
333:     }
334: }
335: ```
336: 
337: ### Advanced State Service with `IMediator`
338: 
339: Services can also encapsulate logic for fetching or updating state using `IMediator`.
340: 
341: ```csharp
342: // Services/{ParentEntity}StateService.cs
343: using System;
344: using System.Collections.Generic;
345: using System.Threading.Tasks;
346: using MediatR;
347: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{ParentEntity};
348: using {Project}.Application.Features.{ParentEntities}.Requests.Queries;
349: 
350: public class {ParentEntity}StateService
351: {
352:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
353:     private List<{ParentEntity}Dto> _{parentEntities} = new();
354:     private bool _isLoaded;
355: 
356:     public {ParentEntity}StateService(IMediator mediator)
357:     {
358:         _mediator = mediator;
359:     }
360: 
361:     public event Action? OnChange;
362: 
363:     public IReadOnlyList<{ParentEntity}Dto> {ParentEntities} => _{parentEntities}.AsReadOnly(); // Read-only access
364: 
365:     public async Task Load{ParentEntities}Async()
366:     {
367:         if (_isLoaded) return; // Load only once per session/instance
368: 
369:         var request = new Get{ParentEntity}ListRequest();
370:         _{parentEntities} = await _mediator.Send(request);
371:         _isLoaded = true;
372:         NotifyStateChanged();
373:     }
374: 
375:     public async Task Refresh{ParentEntities}Async()
376:     {
377:         _isLoaded = false; // Force reload
378:         await Load{ParentEntities}Async();
379:     }
380: 
381:     private void NotifyStateChanged() => OnChange?.Invoke();
382: }
383: ```
384: 
385: ---
386: 
387: ## 7. Singleton Services - Global State
388: 
389: Singleton services persist for the entire application lifetime. They are best suited for truly global, immutable data (e.g., application configuration, feature flags). Avoid using them for mutable state unless carefully managed for thread safety, especially in Blazor Server.
390: 
391: ```csharp
392: // Services/ApplicationConfigService.cs
393: public class ApplicationConfigService
394: {
395:     public string AppVersion { get; } = "1.0.0";
396:     public bool FeatureXEnabled { get; } = true;
397:     public DateTime AppStartUpTime { get; } = DateTime.UtcNow;
398: }
399: ```
400: 
401: **Register**:
402: ```csharp
403: builder.Services.AddSingleton<ApplicationConfigService>();
404: ```
405: 
406: **Use**:
407: ```razor
408: @inject ApplicationConfigService Config
409: 
410: <MudText>App Version: @Config.AppVersion</MudText>
411: ```
412: 
413: **Warning**: In Blazor Server, a singleton service is shared across *all users*. Any mutable state in a singleton will be visible and modifiable by every connected user, potentially leading to critical bugs and security vulnerabilities. Use `AddScoped` for per-user state.
414: 
415: ---
416: 
417: ## 8. State Management Patterns Summary
418: 
419: ### Pattern 1: Parent Manages State
420: 
421: The parent component holds the shared state and passes it down to children via parameters. Children use `EventCallback` to inform the parent of changes.
422: 
423: ```razor
424: @* Parent Component *@
425: <{Entity}List {Entities}="@_{entities}" On{Entity}Selected="HandleSelection" />
426: <{Entity}Details {Entity}="@_selected{Entity}" />
427: 
428: @code {
429:     private List<{Entity}ListDto> _{entities} = new();
430:     private {Entity}Dto? _selected{Entity};
431: 
432:     private async Task HandleSelection({IdType} {entity}Id)
433:     {
434:         // Parent fetches details and updates state, which re-renders {Entity}Details
435:         var request = new Get{Entity}DetailRequest { Id = {entity}Id };
436:         _selected{Entity} = await Mediator.Send(request);
437:     }
438: }
439: ```
440: 
441: ### Pattern 2: Service Manages State (Recommended for Unrelated Components)
442: 
443: A scoped service holds the shared state, and components inject the service to read/update the state and subscribe to change notifications.
444: 
445: ```csharp
446: // Component A (Publishes change)
447: @inject {Entity}StateService State
448: 
449: <MudButton OnClick="Select">Select {Entity}</MudButton>
450: 
451: @code {
452:     [Parameter] public {IdType} {Entity}Id { get; set; }
453:     private void Select() => State.Selected{Entity}Id = {Entity}Id;
454: }
455: 
456: // Component B (Subscribes to change)
457: @inject {Entity}StateService State
458: @implements IDisposable
459: 
460: <MudText>Currently Selected {Entity}: @State.Selected{Entity}Id</MudText>
461: 
462: @code {
463:     protected override void OnInitialized() => State.OnChange += StateHasChanged;
464:     public void Dispose() => State.OnChange -= StateHasChanged;
465: }
466: ```
467: 
468: ---
469: 
470: ## 9. Authentication State
471: 
472: Blazor provides robust built-in mechanisms for managing user authentication and authorization state.
473: 
474: ### Accessing Authentication State Declaratively (`AuthorizeView`)
475: 
476: ```razor
477: <CascadingAuthenticationState>
478:     <AuthorizeView>
479:         <Authorized>
480:             <MudText>Welcome, @context.User.Identity?.Name!</MudText>
481:             <MudButton OnClick="Create{Entity}">Create {Entity}</MudButton>
482:         </Authorized>
483:         <NotAuthorized>
484:             <MudButton Href="/login">Login to Create {Entities}</MudButton>
485:         </NotAuthorized>
486:         <Authorizing>
487:             <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" Size="Size.Small" /> Loading authentication...
488:         </Authorizing>
489:     </AuthorizeView>
490: </CascadingAuthenticationState>
491: ```
492: 
493: ### Accessing Authentication State Programmatically
494: 
495: ```razor
496: @inject AuthenticationStateProvider AuthStateProvider
497: 
498: @code {
499:     private UserDto? _currentUser;
500:     private bool _isAuthenticated;
501: 
502:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
503:     {
504:         var authState = await AuthStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
505:         var user = authState.User; // ClaimsPrincipal object
506: 
507:         _isAuthenticated = user.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
508: 
509:         if (_isAuthenticated)
510:         {
511:             _currentUser = new UserDto
512:             {
513:                 Id = {IdType}.TryParse(user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value, out var id) ? id : default,
514:                 Email = user.FindFirst("email")?.Value ?? string.Empty,
515:                 Name = user.Identity.Name ?? string.Empty,
516:                 // Extract other claims as needed
517:             };
518:         }
519:     }
520: }
521: ```
522: 
523: ### Role-Based Authorization
524: 
525: ```razor
526: <AuthorizeView Roles="Admin,{ParentEntity}Manager"> @* Only visible to users with Admin OR {ParentEntity}Manager role *@
527:     <Authorized>
528:         <MudButton>Delete {Entity}</MudButton>
529:     </Authorized>
530:     <NotAuthorized>
531:         <MudText Color="Color.Error">Access Denied: Insufficient Permissions</MudText>
532:     </NotAuthorized>
533: </AuthorizeView>
534: ```
535: 
536: ---
537: 
538: **Related Resources**:
539: - [component-design.md](component-design.md) - Component lifecycle and parameter basics.
540: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication state serialization and token forwarding for hybrid apps.
541: - [`auth-patterns`](../../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - General authentication and authorization rules.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/resources/theming.md
````markdown
  1: # Theming - Consistent UI Styling
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Theming Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document outlines the theming strategy for Blazor applications using MudBlazor, focusing on customizing themes, managing dark/light modes, and ensuring a consistent visual identity.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. MudBlazor Theming Basics
 12: 
 13: MudBlazor uses a theming system that allows customization of colors, typography, shadows, and more. The primary entry point for customization is the `MudThemeProvider` component, typically placed in `MainLayout.razor`.
 14: 
 15: ### `MainLayout.razor` Theme Setup
 16: 
 17: ```razor
 18: @inherits LayoutComponentBase
 19: 
 20: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
 21: <MudDialogProvider />
 22: <MudSnackbarProvider />
 23: 
 24: <MudLayout>
 25:     <MudAppBar Elevation="0">
 26:         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Menu" Color="Color.Inherit" Edge="Edge.Start" OnClick="@((e) => DrawerToggle())" />
 27:         <MudSpacer />
 28:         <MudSwitch @bind-Checked="@_isDarkMode" Color="Color.Primary" Label="Dark Mode" />
 29:         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Custom.Brands.GitHub" Color="Color.Inherit" Link="https://github.com/MudBlazor/MudBlazor" Target="_blank" />
 30:     </MudAppBar>
 31:     <MudDrawer @bind-Open="@_drawerOpen" Elevation="1">
 32:         <MudDrawerHeader>
 33:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">{Project}</MudText>
 34:         </MudDrawerHeader>
 35:         <NavMenu />
 36:     </MudDrawer>
 37:     <MudMainContent>
 38:         <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.Large" Class="my-4 pt-4">
 39:             @Body
 40:         </MudContainer>
 41:     </MudMainContent>
 42: </MudLayout>
 43: 
 44: @code {
 45:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")] // Consumed from App.razor
 46:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; }
 47: 
 48:     private bool _drawerOpen = true;
 49:     private bool _isDarkMode; // Bound to MudThemeProvider and MudSwitch
 50:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme(); // Default theme instance
 51: 
 52:     protected override void OnInitialized()
 53:     {
 54:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme; // Initialize from cascaded value
 55:         _currentTheme = {Project}Theme.CreateTheme(); // Load custom theme
 56:     }
 57: 
 58:     private void DrawerToggle()
 59:     {
 60:         _drawerOpen = !_drawerOpen;
 61:     }
 62: }
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ### Custom `MudTheme` Definition
 66: 
 67: Define your custom theme settings in a static class or a dedicated file (e.g., `Shared/{Project}Theme.cs`).
 68: 
 69: **`Shared/{Project}Theme.cs`**:
 70: ```csharp
 71: using MudBlazor;
 72: 
 73: namespace {Project}.Blazor.Shared;
 74: 
 75: public static class {Project}Theme
 76: {
 77:     public static MudTheme CreateTheme()
 78:     {
 79:         var theme = new MudTheme()
 80:         {
 81:             Palette = new Palette()
 82:             {
 83:                 Primary = "#34685D", // Primary brand color
 84:                 Secondary = "#E0BBE4", // Secondary accent color
 85:                 Tertiary = "#957DAD", // Tertiary color
 86:                 Info = "#2196F3",
 87:                 Success = "#4CAF50",
 88:                 Warning = "#FFC107",
 89:                 Error = "#F44336",
 90:                 Dark = "#27272f",
 91:                 TextPrimary = "#34685D", // Primary text color
 92:                 TextSecondary = "rgba(0,0,0, 0.54)",
 93:                 AppbarBackground = "#34685D", // App bar color
 94:                 AppbarText = Colors.Shades.White,
 95:                 Background = Colors.Grey.Lighten5,
 96:                 DrawerBackground = "#34685D", // Drawer background color
 97:                 DrawerText = Colors.Shades.White,
 98:                 Surface = Colors.Shades.White,
 99:                 // ... more color definitions
100:             },
101:             PaletteDark = new Palette()
102:             {
103:                 Primary = "#58A293", // Lighter primary for dark mode
104:                 Secondary = "#FFD700", // Gold for accent
105:                 Tertiary = "#BB86FC",
106:                 Info = "#90CAF9",
107:                 Success = "#A5D6A7",
108:                 Warning = "#FFEB3B",
109:                 Error = "#EF9A9A",
110:                 Dark = "#27272f",
111:                 TextPrimary = Colors.Shades.White,
112:                 TextSecondary = "rgba(255,255,255, 0.70)",
113:                 AppbarBackground = "#27272f", // Dark app bar
114:                 AppbarText = Colors.Shades.White,
115:                 Background = "#303030", // Dark background
116:                 DrawerBackground = "#212121",
117:                 DrawerText = "rgba(255,255,255, 0.70)",
118:                 Surface = "#424242",
119:                 // ... more dark mode color definitions
120:             },
121:             Typography = new Typography()
122:             {
123:                 Default = new Default() { FontFamily = new[] { "Roboto", "Helvetica", "Arial", "sans-serif" } },
124:                 H1 = new H1() { FontSize = "3rem", FontWeight = 300, LineHeight = 1.167 },
125:                 // ... other typography settings
126:             },
127:             Shadows = new Shadow()
128:             {
129:                 // Custom shadows if needed
130:             },
131:             // ... other theme properties
132:         };
133:         return theme;
134:     }
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 2. Dark/Light Mode Switching
141: 
142: The application supports dynamic dark/light mode switching, with the preference persisted via cookies.
143: 
144: ### `App.razor` Theme Initialization (Server-side)
145: 
146: The `App.razor` component, running on the server initially, reads the theme preference from a cookie and cascades it down to `MainLayout.razor`.
147: 
148: ```razor
149: // File: {Project}.Blazor/App.razor
150: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor // Provides access to HttpContext
151: 
152: @code {
153:     private bool _isDarkTheme;
154: 
155:     protected override void OnInitialized()
156:     {
157:         // Read the 'theme' cookie to determine initial dark mode state
158:         var themeCookie = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
159:         _isDarkTheme = themeCookie == "dark";
160:     }
161: }
162: 
163: <CascadingValue Value="_isDarkTheme" Name="InitialTheme"> @* Cascades the initial theme state *@
164:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" /> @* Renders root routes *@
165: </CascadingValue>
166: ```
167: 
168: ### `MainLayout.razor` Theme Consumption and Persistence
169: 
170: `MainLayout.razor` consumes the cascaded theme value and includes a `MudSwitch` to allow users to toggle dark/light mode. The choice is then saved to a cookie.
171: 
172: ```razor
173: // File: {Project}.Blazor/Shared/MainLayout.razor
174: @inject IJSRuntime JS
175: 
176: @code {
177:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
178:     public bool InitialIsDarkTheme { get; set; } // Consumes the cascaded value
179: 
180:     private bool _isDarkMode; // Bound to MudThemeProvider and MudSwitch
181:     private MudTheme _currentTheme = new MudTheme();
182: 
183:     protected override void OnInitialized()
184:     {
185:         _isDarkMode = InitialIsDarkTheme;
186:         _currentTheme = {Project}Theme.CreateTheme(); // Load custom theme
187:     }
188: 
189:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
190:     {
191:         if (firstRender)
192:         {
193:             // Set up a watcher or initial check from local storage if needed in WASM
194:         }
195:     }
196: 
197:     private async Task OnDarkModeChanged(bool value)
198:     {
199:         // Save the theme preference to a cookie via JavaScript interop
200:         await JS.InvokeVoidAsync("setCookie", "theme", value ? "dark" : "light", 365);
201:         _isDarkMode = value; // Update local state, MudThemeProvider will react
202:         StateHasChanged(); // Force re-render if necessary
203:     }
204: }
205: 
206: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_currentTheme" />
207: <MudDialogProvider />
208: <MudSnackbarProvider />
209: 
210: <MudLayout>
211:     <MudAppBar>
212:         <MudSpacer />
213:         <MudSwitch @bind-Checked="_isDarkMode"
214:                    Color="Color.Primary"
215:                    Label="Dark Mode"
216:                    ValueChanged="OnDarkModeChanged" /> @* Event for persistence *@
217:     </MudAppBar>
218:     @* ... rest of layout ... *@
219: </MudLayout>
220: ```
221: 
222: ### JavaScript for Cookie Management
223: 
224: A simple JavaScript function to set/get cookies.
225: 
226: **`wwwroot/js/site.js`**:
227: ```javascript
228: window.setCookie = (name, value, days) => {
229:     let expires = "";
230:     if (days) {
231:         let date = new Date();
232:         date.setTime(date.getTime() + (days * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
233:         expires = "; expires=" + date.toUTCString();
234:     }
235:     document.cookie = name + "=" + (value || "") + expires + "; path=/; SameSite=Lax";
236: };
237: 
238: window.getCookie = (name) => {
239:     let nameEQ = name + "=";
240:     let ca = document.cookie.split(';');
241:     for(let i=0; i < ca.length; i++) {
242:         let c = ca[i];
243:         while (c.charAt(0) === ' ') c = c.substring(1, c.length);
244:         if (c.indexOf(nameEQ) === 0) return c.substring(nameEQ.length, c.length);
245:     }
246:     return null;
247: };
248: ```
249: 
250: ---
251: 
252: ## 3. Custom CSS Overrides and Variables
253: 
254: For fine-grained control or overrides not possible through the `MudTheme` object, use custom CSS.
255: 
256: ### `wwwroot/css/site.css`
257: 
258: This file is for global styles and overrides.
259: 
260: ```css
261: /* Custom properties for consistency, e.g., for BEM blocks */
262: :root {
263:     --{project}-primary-color: #34685D;
264:     --{project}-secondary-color: #E0BBE4;
265:     --{project}-font-family: 'Roboto', sans-serif;
266: }
267: 
268: /* Override MudBlazor default typography */
269: body {
270:     font-family: var(--{project}-font-family);
271: }
272: 
273: h1.mud-typography-h1 {
274:     color: var(--{project}-primary-color);
275: }
276: 
277: /* Custom styles for components */
278: .{entity}-card {
279:     border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
280:     border-radius: var(--mud-default-border-radius);
281:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-1);
282: }
283: 
284: .{entity}-card__title {
285:     color: var(--{project}-primary-color);
286: }
287: ```
288: 
289: ### `wwwroot/css/variables.css` (Optional, for more granular control)
290: 
291: This file can define CSS variables for colors, spacing, etc., making them easily reusable across the application.
292: 
293: ```css
294: /* Global CSS variables */
295: :root {
296:     /* Colors */
297:     --{project}-color-primary: #34685D;
298:     --{project}-color-secondary: #E0BBE4;
299:     --{project}-color-accent: #FFD700;
300: 
301:     /* Spacing */
302:     --{project}-spacing-unit: 8px;
303:     --{project}-spacing-xs: var(--{project}-spacing-unit);
304:     --{project}-spacing-sm: calc(var(--{project}-spacing-unit) * 2);
305:     /* ... */
306: }
307: 
308: /* Use in other CSS files */
309: .my-component {
310:     padding: var(--{project}-spacing-sm);
311:     background-color: var(--{project}-color-primary);
312: }
313: ```
314: 
315: ---
316: 
317: ## 4. Best Practices for Theming
318: 
319: *   **Centralize `MudTheme`**: Define your primary light and dark themes in a dedicated static class (e.g., `{Project}Theme.cs`).
320: *   **Use CSS Variables**: Leverage MudBlazor's CSS variables (e.g., `var(--mud-palette-primary)`) and define your own (`--{project}-primary-color`) for consistent styling.
321: *   **BEM for Custom CSS**: Combine theming with BEM methodology for maintainable custom component styles.
322: *   **Minimal Global Overrides**: Keep `site.css` lean, focusing on broad overrides and global utilities.
323: *   **Test Dark/Light Mode**: Always test your application thoroughly in both dark and light modes to ensure readability and visual harmony.
324: *   **Accessible Colors**: Ensure sufficient contrast between text and background colors, especially for accessibility.
325: 
326: ---
327: 
328: **Related Resources**:
329: - [mudblazor-usage.md](mudblazor-usage.md) - For how to apply styling to specific MudBlazor components.
330: - [bem-methodology.md](bem-methodology.md) - Guidelines for structured CSS naming.
331: - [state-management.md](state-management.md) - How theme state is managed and cascaded.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: blazor-ui-conventions
  3: description: Comprehensive UI conventions for Blazor applications. Covers MudBlazor usage, BEM methodology, theming, component structure, state management, and render modes.
  4: type: ui
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Blazor UI Conventions & MudBlazor Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic Blazor UI Patterns**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: This skill provides comprehensive guidelines and best practices for developing UI components in Blazor applications. It covers MudBlazor usage, BEM methodology for CSS, theming, component structure, lifecycle, state management, and render modes to ensure consistency, maintainability, and optimal user experience.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "blazor", "component", "razor", "mudblazor", "ui", "page", "dialog", "render", "parameter", "css", "theme", "state", "lifecycle"
 23: - File patterns: `**/*.razor`, `**/*.razor.cs`, `**/*.Client/**/*.cs`, `**/*.css`, `**/*.scss`
 24: - Content patterns: `@page`, `@inject`, `<Mud`, `Parameter`, `EventCallback`, `::deep`, `::part`, `BEM` class names.
 25: 
 26: ## Blazor Hybrid Architecture
 27: 
 28: ```mermaid
 29: graph TD
 30:     subgraph Blazor Hybrid App
 31:         BFF[{Project}.Blazor (Server-side BFF)]
 32:         WASM[{Project}.Blazor.Client (WebAssembly)]
 33:         Router[Router / InteractiveAuto]
 34:     end
 35: 
 36:     subgraph UI Layer
 37:         Components[UI Components (.razor)]
 38:         MudBlazor[MudBlazor Library]
 39:         CSS[BEM-structured CSS]
 40:     end
 41: 
 42:     Router -- Renders on --> BFF
 43:     Router -- Interactivity via --> WASM
 44:     Components -- Built with --> MudBlazor
 45:     Components -- Styled with --> CSS
 46:     WASM -- Communicates with --> BFF
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: ## Resources
 50: 
 51: | Resource | Description |
 52: |----------|-------------|
 53: | [mudblazor-usage.md](resources/mudblazor-usage.md) | Detailed usage of common MudBlazor components (Grid, Buttons, Forms, Dialogs, Tables, Snackbar, Cards). |
 54: | [component-design.md](resources/component-design.md) | Blazor component structure, lifecycle, parameters, `EventCallback`, and best practices for parent-child communication. |
 55: | [state-management.md](resources/state-management.md) | Comprehensive guide to Blazor state management techniques (component state, parameters, cascading values, scoped/singleton services). |
 56: | [render-modes.md](resources/render-modes.md) | Explanation of Blazor render modes (InteractiveAuto, Server, WebAssembly, Static SSR) and their appropriate use cases. |
 57: | [bem-methodology.md](resources/bem-methodology.md) | Guidelines for BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) CSS naming convention for maintainable stylesheets. |
 58: | [theming.md](resources/theming.md) | Customizing MudBlazor themes, dark/light mode switching, and consistent styling. |
 59: | [common-patterns.md](resources/common-patterns.md) | Real-world Blazor implementation patterns for forms, dialogs, tables, navigation, loading states, error handling, search/filter, and infinite scroll. |
 60: 
 61: ## Quick Reference
 62: 
 63: ### 1. BEM Methodology
 64: 
 65: **Rule**: All custom CSS should follow the BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) naming convention.
 66: 
 67: ```css
 68: /* Block: .{entity}-card */
 69: .{entity}-card {
 70:     border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
 71:     border-radius: var(--mud-default-border-radius);
 72:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-1);
 73: }
 74: 
 75: /* Element: .{entity}-card__title */
 76: .{entity}-card__title {
 77:     font-size: var(--mud-typography-h6-size);
 78:     color: var(--mud-palette-primary);
 79: }
 80: 
 81: /* Modifier: .{entity}-card--featured */
 82: .{entity}-card--featured {
 83:     border-color: var(--mud-palette-success);
 84:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-2);
 85: }
 86: ```
 87: *For more details, see [bem-methodology.md](resources/bem-methodology.md).*
 88: 
 89: ### 2. MudBlazor Usage
 90: 
 91: **Rule**: Prefer MudBlazor components over custom HTML for consistent UI and functionality.
 92: 
 93: ```razor
 94: @* Grid Layout *@
 95: <MudGrid Spacing="3">
 96:     <MudItem xs="12" sm="6" md="4" lg="3">
 97:         <MudCard>
 98:             <MudCardMedia Image="@item.CoverImageUrl" Height="200" />
 99:             <MudCardContent>
100:                 <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">@item.Title</MudText>
101:             </MudCardContent>
102:         </MudCard>
103:     </MudItem>
104: </MudGrid>
105: 
106: @* Buttons *@
107: <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled" Color="Color.Primary" StartIcon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Add">
108:     Create {Entity}
109: </MudButton>
110: 
111: @* Forms *@
112: <MudTextField @bind-Value="title" Label="{Entity} Title" Required="true" />
113: <MudSelect @bind-Value="selectedId" Label="{LookupEntity}">
114:     <MudSelectItem Value="1">Option 1</MudSelectItem>
115: </MudSelect>
116: ```
117: *For more details, see [mudblazor-usage.md](resources/mudblazor-usage.md).*
118: 
119: ### 3. Theming
120: 
121: **Rule**: Global styles and theme overrides are managed in `wwwroot/css/StyleGlobal.css` and `wwwroot/css/variables.css`. Dark/Light mode switching is handled via a `CascadingValue`.
122: 
123: ```csharp
124: // App.razor logic for cascading theme
125: @inject IHttpContextAccessor HttpContextAccessor
126: 
127: @code {
128:     var theme = HttpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Cookies["theme"];
129:     var isDark = theme == "dark";
130: }
131: 
132: <CascadingValue Value="isDark" Name="InitialTheme">
133:     <Routes @rendermode="InteractiveAuto" />
134: </CascadingValue>
135: 
136: // MainLayout.razor consuming the theme
137: @code {
138:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
139:     public bool IsDarkMode { get; set; }
140: 
141:     private MudTheme _theme = new();
142:     private bool _isDarkMode;
143: 
144:     protected override void OnInitialized()
145:     {
146:         _isDarkMode = IsDarkMode;
147:     }
148: }
149: 
150: <MudThemeProvider @bind-IsDarkMode="_isDarkMode" Theme="_theme" />
151: ```
152: *For more details, see [theming.md](resources/theming.md).*
153: 
154: ### 4. Component Structure & Lifecycle
155: 
156: **Rule**: Use the code-behind pattern for complex components. Use `OnInitializedAsync` for data fetching, `OnParametersSetAsync` for reacting to parameter changes, and `EventCallback` for child-to-parent communication.
157: 
158: ```razor
159: @* Child Component: {Entity}Card.razor *@
160: <MudCard>
161:     <MudCardActions>
162:         <MudButton OnClick="DeleteClicked">Delete</MudButton>
163:     </MudCardActions>
164: </MudCard>
165: 
166: @code {
167:     [Parameter]
168:     public {Entity}Dto {Entity} { get; set; } = null!;
169: 
170:     [Parameter]
171:     public EventCallback<{IdType}> OnDelete { get; set; }
172: 
173:     private async Task DeleteClicked()
174:     {
175:         await OnDelete.InvokeAsync({Entity}.Id);
176:     }
177: }
178: ```
179: *For more details, see [component-design.md](resources/component-design.md).*
180: 
181: ### 5. State Management
182: 
183: **Rule**: Choose the appropriate state management pattern based on the component relationship and data scope.
184: 
185: -   **Component State**: For isolated component data.
186: -   **Parameters/EventCallback**: For direct parent-child communication.
187: -   **CascadingValue**: For sharing state deep in the component hierarchy (e.g., `AuthenticationState`, theme).
188: -   **Scoped Services**: For sharing state across multiple, unrelated components within the same user session.
189: -   **Singleton Services**: For global, read-only application data.
190: 
191: *For more details, see [state-management.md](resources/state-management.md).*
192: 
193: ### 6. Render Modes
194: 
195: **Rule**: Use `InteractiveAuto` as the default render mode for interactive components. Use `InteractiveServer` for server-only features (e.g., `HttpContext` access) and `InteractiveWebAssembly` for offline-first or highly client-side interactive components.
196: 
197: ```razor
198: @page "/{entities}"
199: @rendermode InteractiveAuto // Default for interactive pages
200: ```
201: *For more details, see [render-modes.md](resources/render-modes.md).*
202: 
203: ### 7. Common Patterns
204: 
205: **Rule**: Implement common UI patterns like forms, dialogs, tables, and loading states consistently across the application.
206: 
207: ```razor
208: @* Confirmation Dialog *@
209: @inject IDialogService DialogService
210: 
211: <MudButton OnClick="Delete{Entity}">Delete</MudButton>
212: 
213: @code {
214:     private async Task Delete{Entity}()
215:     {
216:         var dialog = await DialogService.ShowAsync<ConfirmDialog>("Confirm Delete");
217:         var result = await dialog.Result;
218:         if (!result.Canceled) { /* Perform delete */ }
219:     }
220: }
221: ```
222: *For more details, see [common-patterns.md](resources/common-patterns.md).*
223: 
224: ## Do's
225: 
226: -   **DO** use `@rendermode="InteractiveAuto"` as the default for interactive pages.
227: -   **DO** prefer MudBlazor components over custom HTML for consistency.
228: -   **DO** follow the BEM methodology for all custom CSS classes.
229: -   **DO** use `[Parameter]` for inputs and `EventCallback<T>` for child-to-parent events.
230: -   **DO** load data in `OnInitializedAsync` for initial setup.
231: -   **DO** use `IDialogService` for modals and `ISnackbar` for notifications.
232: -   **DO** implement `IDisposable` for event clean-up in services and components.
233: -   **DO** use scoped services for state management across components within a user session.
234: -   **DO** centralize theme customization in `wwwroot/css/site.css` and `wwwroot/css/variables.css`.
235: 
236: ## Don'ts
237: 
238: -   **DON'T** use raw HTML when a suitable MudBlazor component exists.
239: -   **DON'T** modify `[Parameter]` properties directly from within a child component.
240: -   **DON'T** access `HttpContext` in components rendered with `InteractiveAuto` or `InteractiveWebAssembly` (use `InteractiveServer` or BFF pattern).
241: -   **DON'T** use JavaScript interop for tasks that MudBlazor or Blazor itself can handle.
242: -   **DON'T** call `StateHasChanged()` unnecessarily (can lead to performance issues).
243: -   **DON'T** use static state in Blazor Server apps (can cause data leakage between users).
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: **Related Documentation**:
248: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture, especially Blazor Hybrid.
249: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Details on YARP, token forwarding, and cookie-based auth.
250: - [`auth-patterns`](../auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication and authorization patterns in Blazor.
````

## File: .claude/skills/clean-architecture-rules/resources/dependency-rules.md
````markdown
  1: # Dependency Rules - Complete Reference
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Dependency Rules**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Dependency Matrix
  8: 
  9: | Layer | Can Reference | Cannot Reference | Framework Dependencies Allowed |
 10: |-------|---------------|------------------|-------------------------------|
 11: | **{Project}.Domain** | Nothing | Everything | None (pure C#) |
 12: | **{Project}.Application** | Domain | Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor | MediatR, FluentValidation, AutoMapper |
 13: | **{Project}.Persistence** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | EF Core, Database Provider, PostGIS |
 14: | **{Project}.Infrastructure** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | Any (email, file storage, external APIs) |
 15: | **{Project}.API** | All | None (top layer) | ASP.NET Core, Swashbuckle, Serilog |
 16: | **{Project}.Blazor** | All | None (top layer) | Blazor, MudBlazor, SignalR |
 17: | **{Project}.Blazor.Client** | Shared DTOs | Server components | Blazor WebAssembly, MudBlazor |
 18: 
 19: ## Visual Dependency Flow
 20: 
 21: ```mermaid
 22: graph TD
 23:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 24:         A[{Project}.API]
 25:         B[{Project}.Blazor]
 26:     end
 27: 
 28:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 29:         C[{Project}.Persistence]
 30:         D[{Project}.Infrastructure]
 31:     end
 32: 
 33:     subgraph Application Layer
 34:         E[{Project}.Application]
 35:     end
 36: 
 37:     subgraph Domain Layer
 38:         F[{Project}.Domain]
 39:     end
 40: 
 41:     A --> E
 42:     A --> C
 43:     A --> D
 44: 
 45:     B --> E
 46:     B --> C
 47:     B --> D
 48: 
 49:     C --> E
 50:     C --> F
 51: 
 52:     D --> E
 53:     D --> F
 54: 
 55:     E --> F
 56: 
 57:     style A fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 58:     style B fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 59:     style C fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 60:     style D fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 61:     style E fill:#e5c5fb,stroke:#333
 62:     style F fill:#c5fbc5,stroke:#333
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ## The Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
 66: 
 67: **Core Idea**: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
 68: 
 69: ### Example: Application needs Database Access
 70: 
 71: **❌ WITHOUT Dependency Inversion** (Violation):
 72: ```
 73: Application ──────> Infrastructure
 74: (high-level)        (low-level, concrete)
 75: 
 76: Create{Entity}CommandHandler → {DbContext}
 77: ```
 78: *Problem*: Application layer depends on concrete Infrastructure implementation.
 79: 
 80: **✅ WITH Dependency Inversion** (Correct):
 81: ```
 82: Application ──────> I{Entity}Repository (Interface)
 83:                            ▲
 84:                            │ implements
 85: Infrastructure ────────────┘
 86: {Entity}Repository (implements I{Entity}Repository)
 87: ```
 88: *Solution*: Both depend on abstraction (interface) defined in Application.
 89: 
 90: ## Allowed `using` Statements by Layer
 91: 
 92: ### {Project}.Domain
 93: 
 94: ```csharp
 95: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
 96: namespace {Project}.Domain;
 97: 
 98: // ✅ ALLOWED - Pure C# only
 99: using System;
100: using System.Collections.Generic;
101: using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;
102: 
103: public class {Entity}
104: {
105:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
106: 
107:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
108:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
109:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
110: 
111:     [ForeignKey("{RelatedEntity}")]
112:     public {IdType} {RelatedEntity}Id { get; set; }
113:     public {RelatedEntity} {RelatedEntity} { get; set; }
114: 
115:     // ... more navigation properties
116: }
117: 
118: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED in Domain
119: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
120: using {Project}.Application;                   // Layer above
121: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Layer above
122: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
123: using MediatR;                                 // Application concern
124: ```
125: 
126: ### {Project}.Application
127: 
128: ```csharp
129: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
130: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
131: 
132: // ✅ ALLOWED
133: using System;
134: using System.Collections.Generic;
135: using System.Linq;
136: using System.Threading;
137: using System.Threading.Tasks;
138: using AutoMapper;                                       // Application framework
139: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Same layer
140: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};             // Same layer
141: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;  // Same layer
142: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;  // Same layer
143: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                 // Same layer
144: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
145: using MediatR;                                         // CQRS framework
146: 
147: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
148: using {Project}.Persistence;                   // Infrastructure layer
149: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Infrastructure layer
150: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
151: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
152: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
153: ```
154: 
155: ### {Project}.Persistence
156: 
157: ```csharp
158: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
159: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
160: 
161: // ✅ ALLOWED
162: using System;
163: using System.Collections.Generic;
164: using System.Linq;
165: using System.Threading.Tasks;
166: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Application interfaces
167: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
168: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;                   // ORM framework
169: 
170: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
171: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
172: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
173: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
174: ```
175: 
176: ### {Project}.Infrastructure
177: 
178: ```csharp
179: // File: {Project}.Infrastructure/Email/EmailService.cs
180: namespace {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;
181: 
182: // ✅ ALLOWED
183: using {Project}.Domain;                                   // Domain entities
184: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;     // Application interfaces
185: using SendGrid;                                           // External service
186: using Azure.Storage.Blobs;                                // External service
187: 
188: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
189: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
190: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
191: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
192: ```
193: 
194: ### {Project}.API
195: 
196: ```csharp
197: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
198: namespace {Project}.API.Controllers;
199: 
200: // ✅ ALLOWED (Everything)
201: using System;
202: using System.Collections.Generic;
203: using System.Linq;
204: using System.Security.Claims;
205: using System.Threading.Tasks;
206: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};                          // DTOs
207: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
208: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
209: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                              // Response wrappers
210: using MediatR;                                                      // CQRS
211: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;                           // Auth
212: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;                                    // HTTP context
213: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                                     // Controllers
214: // ... any other dependencies
215: ```
216: 
217: ## Project Reference Rules (.csproj)
218: 
219: ### {Project}.Domain.csproj
220: ```xml
221: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
222:   <PropertyGroup>
223:     <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
224:   </PropertyGroup>
225: 
226:   <!-- ✅ NO PROJECT REFERENCES -->
227:   <ItemGroup>
228:     <!-- Only System.ComponentModel.Annotations for [ForeignKey] -->
229:     <PackageReference Include="System.ComponentModel.Annotations" Version="10.0.0" />
230:   </ItemGroup>
231: </Project>
232: ```
233: 
234: ### {Project}.Application.csproj
235: ```xml
236: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
237:   <ItemGroup>
238:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Reference to Domain -->
239:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
240:   </ItemGroup>
241: 
242:   <ItemGroup>
243:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Framework packages -->
244:     <PackageReference Include="MediatR" Version="12.4.0" />
245:     <PackageReference Include="FluentValidation" Version="11.9.0" />
246:     <PackageReference Include="AutoMapper" Version="13.0.1" />
247:   </ItemGroup>
248: 
249:   <!-- ❌ NOT ALLOWED: References to Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor -->
250: </Project>
251: ```
252: 
253: ### {Project}.Persistence.csproj
254: ```xml
255: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
256:   <ItemGroup>
257:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to Domain and Application -->
258:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
259:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
260:   </ItemGroup>
261: 
262:   <ItemGroup>
263:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: EF Core and database packages -->
264:     <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore" Version="10.0.0" />
265:     <PackageReference Include="Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL" Version="10.0.0" />
266:   </ItemGroup>
267: </Project>
268: ```
269: 
270: ### {Project}.API.csproj
271: ```xml
272: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
273:   <ItemGroup>
274:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to ALL -->
275:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
276:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Infrastructure\{Project}.Infrastructure.csproj" />
277:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Persistence\{Project}.Persistence.csproj" />
278:   </ItemGroup>
279: </Project>
280: ```
281: 
282: ## Verification Commands
283: 
284: ### Check Project References
285: ```bash
286: # Domain should have NO project references
287: dotnet list {Project}.Domain/{Project}.Domain.csproj reference
288: 
289: # Application should ONLY reference Domain
290: dotnet list {Project}.Application/{Project}.Application.csproj reference
291: 
292: # Persistence should reference Domain + Application
293: dotnet list {Project}.Persistence/{Project}.Persistence.csproj reference
294: ```
295: 
296: ### Search for Violations
297: ```bash
298: # Find prohibited using statements in Domain
299: rg "using (Microsoft\.(EntityFrameworkCore|AspNetCore)|{Project}\.(Application|Infrastructure|API|Blazor))" {Project}.Domain/
300: 
301: # Find validation annotations in Domain (except [ForeignKey])
302: rg "\[Required\]|\[MaxLength\]|\[Range\]|\[StringLength\]" {Project}.Domain/
303: ```
304: 
305: ## Common Questions
306: 
307: ### Q: Can Domain use System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations?
308: **A**: LIMITED USE. Only `[ForeignKey]` is acceptable for EF Core relationships. Avoid `[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`, `[Range]` etc.
309: 
310: ```csharp
311: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
312: public class {Entity}
313: {
314:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
315: 
316:     // ✅ OK - Specifies foreign key relationship
317:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
318:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
319:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
320: 
321:     // ❌ NOT OK - Validation annotations
322:     // [Required]
323:     // [MaxLength(200)]
324:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
325: }
326: ```
327: 
328: **Why**: `[ForeignKey]` is metadata for EF Core navigation, not validation. Use FluentValidation in Application layer for validation rules.
329: 
330: ### Q: Can Application use AutoMapper?
331: **A**: ✅ YES. AutoMapper is an Application-layer concern for mapping Domain entities to DTOs.
332: 
333: ```csharp
334: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
335: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
336: {
337:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
338:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
339: 
340:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
341:     {
342:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // Returns List<{Entity}>
343:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});  // ✅ Maps to DTOs
344:     }
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ### Q: Can Application reference EF Core for IQueryable?
349: **A**: ❌ NO. Define repository interfaces that return `Task<List<T>>` instead. Let Infrastructure handle IQueryable.
350: 
351: **Correct Pattern**:
352: ```csharp
353: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
354: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
355: 
356: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
357: {
358:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
359:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // ✅ Returns List<{Entity}>, not IQueryable
360: }
361: 
362: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
363: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
364: {
365:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
366:     {
367:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}  // ✅ EF Core IQueryable handled here
368:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
369:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity})
370:             .ToListAsync();  // ✅ Materializes to List
371:     }
372: }
373: ```
374: 
375: ### Q: Where do I put Email sending logic?
376: **A**:
377: - **Interface**: `{Project}.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IEmailService.cs`
378: - **Implementation**: `{Project}.Infrastructure/Services/EmailService.cs`
379: - **Usage**: Application layer uses `IEmailService`, Infrastructure provides concrete implementation
380: 
381: ### Q: Can Blazor.Client reference Persistence?
382: **A**: ❌ NO. Blazor.Client runs in the browser (WebAssembly) and cannot access databases directly. Use shared DTOs and API calls.
383: 
384: **Correct Pattern**:
385: ```csharp
386: // Shared DTO in {Project}.Application
387: public record {Entity}ListDto
388: {
389:     public {IdType} Id { get; init; }
390:     public string Title { get; init; } = string.Empty;
391:     public string {LookupEntity}Name { get; init; } = string.Empty;
392: }
393: 
394: // API endpoint in {Project}.API
395: [HttpGet]
396: [AllowAnonymous]
397: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
398: {
399:     var {entities} = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest());
400:     return Ok({entities});
401: }
402: 
403: // Blazor.Client calls API
404: @inject HttpClient Http
405: 
406: var {entities} = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<{Entity}ListDto>>("/api/v1/{entity}");
407: ```
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: **Next**: See [violation-examples.md](violation-examples.md) for common mistakes and [fix-patterns.md](fix-patterns.md) for comprehensive fix strategies.
````

## File: .claude/skills/clean-architecture-rules/resources/fix-patterns.md
````markdown
  1: # Fix Patterns - How to Resolve Violations
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Fix Patterns Reference**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Pattern #1: Move Logic to Correct Layer
  8: 
  9: ### Scenario: Business Logic in Controller
 10: 
 11: **❌ Before** (Logic in wrong layer):
 12: ```csharp
 13: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
 14: [HttpPost]
 15: public async Task<ActionResult> Create(Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 16: {
 17:     // ❌ Business logic in controller
 18:     if (dto.Title == null || dto.Title.Length > 500)
 19:         return BadRequest("Title must be between 1 and 500 characters");
 20: 
 21:     if (dto.{LookupEntity}Id <= 0)
 22:         return BadRequest("{LookupEntity} is required");
 23: 
 24:     var {entity} = new {Entity}
 25:     {
 26:         Id = Guid.NewGuid(),
 27:         Title = dto.Title,
 28:         {LookupEntity}Id = dto.{LookupEntity}Id,
 29:         ViewCount = 0
 30:     };
 31: 
 32:     _dbContext.{Entities}.Add({entity});
 33:     await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 34: 
 35:     return Ok({entity}.Id);
 36: }
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: **✅ After** (Logic in correct layers):
 40: ```csharp
 41: // Step 1: Create Command in Application layer
 42: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/Create{Entity}Command.cs
 43: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
 44: 
 45: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
 46: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
 47: using MediatR;
 48: 
 49: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
 50: {
 51:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; } = null!;
 52: }
 53: 
 54: // Step 2: Create Validator in Application layer
 55: // File: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
 56: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
 57: 
 58: using FluentValidation;
 59: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 60: 
 61: public class Create{Entity}DtoValidator : AbstractValidator<Create{Entity}Dto>
 62: {
 63:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity1}Repository _{relatedEntity1}Repository;
 64:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity2}Repository _{relatedEntity2}Repository;
 65:     private readonly I{LookupEntity}Repository _{lookupEntity}Repository;
 66:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity3}Repository _{relatedEntity3}Repository;
 67:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity4}Repository _{relatedEntity4}Repository;
 68: 
 69:     public Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
 70:         I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository,
 71:         I{RelatedEntity2}Repository {relatedEntity2}Repository,
 72:         I{LookupEntity}Repository {lookupEntity}Repository,
 73:         I{RelatedEntity3}Repository {relatedEntity3}Repository,
 74:         I{RelatedEntity4}Repository {relatedEntity4}Repository)
 75:     {
 76:         _{relatedEntity1}Repository = {relatedEntity1}Repository;
 77:         _{relatedEntity2}Repository = {relatedEntity2}Repository;
 78:         _{lookupEntity}Repository = {lookupEntity}Repository;
 79:         _{relatedEntity3}Repository = {relatedEntity3}Repository;
 80:         _{relatedEntity4}Repository = {relatedEntity4}Repository;
 81: 
 82:         RuleFor(x => x.Title)
 83:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("Title is required")
 84:             .MaximumLength(200);
 85: 
 86:         RuleFor(x => x.Description)
 87:             .MaximumLength(5000)
 88:             .When(x => !string.IsNullOrEmpty(x.Description));
 89: 
 90:         RuleFor(x => x.{LookupEntity}Id)
 91:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{LookupEntity} is required")
 92:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
 93:             {
 94:                 var exists = await _{lookupEntity}Repository.Exists(id);
 95:                 return exists;
 96:             })
 97:             .WithMessage("{LookupEntity} not found");
 98: 
 99:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity2}Id)
100:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity2} is required")
101:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
102:             {
103:                 var exists = await _{relatedEntity2}Repository.Exists(id);
104:                 return exists;
105:             })
106:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity2} not found");
107: 
108:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity1}Id)
109:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} is required")
110:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
111:             {
112:                 var exists = await _{relatedEntity1}Repository.Exists(id);
113:                 return exists;
114:             })
115:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} not found");
116: 
117:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity3}Id)
118:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
119:             {
120:                 if (!id.HasValue) return true;
121:                 return await _{relatedEntity3}Repository.Exists(id.Value);
122:             })
123:             .When(x => x.{RelatedEntity3}Id.HasValue)
124:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity3} does not exist.");
125: 
126:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity4}Id)
127:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) =>
128:             {
129:                 if (!id.HasValue) return true;
130:                 return await _{relatedEntity4}Repository.Exists(id.Value);
131:             })
132:             .When(x => x.{RelatedEntity4}Id.HasValue)
133:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity4} does not exist.");
134:     }
135: }
136: 
137: // Step 3: Create Handler in Application layer
138: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
139: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
140: 
141: using System;
142: using System.Linq;
143: using System.Threading;
144: using System.Threading.Tasks;
145: using AutoMapper;
146: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
147: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
148: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
149: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
150: using {Project}.Domain;
151: using MediatR;
152: 
153: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
154: {
155:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
156:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity1}Repository _{relatedEntity1}Repository;
157:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity2}Repository _{relatedEntity2}Repository;
158:     private readonly I{LookupEntity}Repository _{lookupEntity}Repository;
159:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity3}Repository _{relatedEntity3}Repository;
160:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity4}Repository _{relatedEntity4}Repository;
161:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
162: 
163:     public Create{Entity}CommandHandler(
164:         I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository,
165:         I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository,
166:         I{RelatedEntity2}Repository {relatedEntity2}Repository,
167:         I{LookupEntity}Repository {lookupEntity}Repository,
168:         I{RelatedEntity3}Repository {relatedEntity3}Repository,
169:         I{RelatedEntity4}Repository {relatedEntity4}Repository,
170:         IMapper mapper)
171:     {
172:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
173:         _{relatedEntity1}Repository = {relatedEntity1}Repository;
174:         _{relatedEntity2}Repository = {relatedEntity2}Repository;
175:         _{lookupEntity}Repository = {lookupEntity}Repository;
176:         _{relatedEntity3}Repository = {relatedEntity3}Repository;
177:         _{relatedEntity4}Repository = {relatedEntity4}Repository;
178:         _mapper = mapper;
179:     }
180: 
181:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
182:     {
183:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
184: 
185:         // ✅ Validate using FluentValidation - instantiated manually with dependencies
186:         var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
187:             _{relatedEntity1}Repository,
188:             _{relatedEntity2}Repository,
189:             _{lookupEntity}Repository,
190:             _{relatedEntity3}Repository,
191:             _{relatedEntity4}Repository);
192: 
193:         var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto, cancellationToken);
194: 
195:         if (!validationResult.IsValid)
196:         {
197:             response.Success = false;
198:             response.Message = "{Entity} creation failed.";
199:             response.Errors = validationResult.Errors.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToList();
200:             return response;
201:         }
202: 
203:         // ✅ Map DTO to Entity
204:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
205:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0;
206: 
207:         // ✅ Save through repository
208:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
209: 
210:         response.Success = true;
211:         response.Id = {entity}.Id;
212:         response.Message = "{Entity} created successfully.";
213: 
214:         return response;
215:     }
216: }
217: 
218: // Step 4: Thin Controller in API layer
219: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
220: namespace {Project}.API.Controllers;
221: 
222: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
223: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
224: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
225: using MediatR;
226: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
227: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
228: 
229: [Route("api/v1/[controller]")]
230: [ApiController]
231: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
232: {
233:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
234: 
235:     public {Entity}Controller(IMediator mediator) => _mediator = mediator;
236: 
237:     [HttpPost]
238:     [Authorize]
239:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
240:     {
241:         var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto };
242:         var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
243:         return Ok(response);
244:     }
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: **Benefits**:
249: - ✅ Business logic is testable without HTTP
250: - ✅ Validation runs automatically via FluentValidation
251: - ✅ Controller is thin (5 lines)
252: - ✅ Logic can be reused from Blazor, CLI, etc.
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: ## Pattern #2: Use Interfaces for Infrastructure Dependencies
257: 
258: ### Scenario: Application Needs Email Sending
259: 
260: **❌ Before** (Direct dependency):
261: ```csharp
262: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
263: using {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
264: using SendGrid;  // ❌ Infrastructure concern
265: 
266: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
267: {
268:     private readonly SendGridEmailService _emailService;  // ❌ Concrete class
269: 
270:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
271:     {
272:         // ... create {entity}
273: 
274:         await _emailService.SendAsync(email);  // ❌ Tightly coupled
275: 
276:         return response;
277:     }
278: }
279: ```
280: 
281: **✅ After** (Dependency Inversion):
282: ```csharp
283: // Step 1: Define interface in Application layer
284: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IEmailService.cs
285: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
286: 
287: using System;
288: using System.Threading;
289: using System.Threading.Tasks;
290: 
291: public interface IEmailService
292: {
293:     Task Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
294:         {IdType} {entity}Id,
295:         string {entity}Title,
296:         string ownerEmail,
297:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
298: }
299: 
300: // Step 2: Use interface in Application layer
301: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
302: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
303: 
304: using System;
305: using System.Linq;
306: using System.Threading;
307: using System.Threading.Tasks;
308: using AutoMapper;
309: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;  // ✅ Same layer interface
310: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
311: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
312: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
313: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
314: using {Project}.Domain;
315: using MediatR;
316: 
317: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
318: {
319:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
320:     private readonly IEmailService _emailService;  // ✅ Interface
321:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
322:     // ... other dependencies
323: 
324:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
325:     {
326:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
327: 
328:         // Validation...
329:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
330:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0;
331:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
332: 
333:         // ✅ Calls interface, doesn't know about SendGrid
334:         await _emailService.Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
335:             {entity}.Id,
336:             {entity}.Title,
337:             request.{Entity}Dto.OwnerEmail,
338:             cancellationToken);
339: 
340:         return response;
341:     }
342: }
343: 
344: // Step 3: Implement in Infrastructure layer
345: // File: {Project}.Infrastructure/Email/SendGridEmailService.cs
346: namespace {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;
347: 
348: using System;
349: using System.Threading;
350: using System.Threading.Tasks;
351: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;  // ✅ Implements interface
352: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
353: using SendGrid;
354: using SendGrid.Helpers.Mail;
355: 
356: public class SendGridEmailService : IEmailService
357: {
358:     private readonly ISendGridClient _client;
359:     private readonly ILogger<SendGridEmailService> _logger;
360: 
361:     public SendGridEmailService(ISendGridClient client, ILogger<SendGridEmailService> logger)
362:     {
363:         _client = client;
364:         _logger = logger;
365:     }
366: 
367:     public async Task Send{Entity}CreatedNotificationAsync(
368:         {IdType} {entity}Id,
369:         string {entity}Title,
370:         string ownerEmail,
371:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
372:     {
373:         var from = new EmailAddress("noreply@example.com", "Application Name");
374:         var to = new EmailAddress(ownerEmail);
375:         var subject = $"{Entity} Created: {{entity}Title}";
376:         var htmlContent = $"<p>Your {entity} <strong>{{entity}Title}</strong> has been created successfully.</p>";
377: 
378:         var msg = MailHelper.CreateSingleEmail(from, to, subject, null, htmlContent);
379: 
380:         try
381:         {
382:             var response = await _client.SendEmailAsync(msg, cancellationToken);
383:             _logger.LogInformation("Email sent to {Email} for {Entity} {{EntityId}}", ownerEmail, {entity}Id);
384:         }
385:         catch (Exception ex)
386:         {
387:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to send email for {Entity} {{EntityId}}", {entity}Id);
388:             throw;
389:         }
390:     }
391: }
392: 
393: // Step 4: Register in API (Composition Root)
394: // File: {Project}.API/Program.cs
395: builder.Services.AddScoped<IEmailService, SendGridEmailService>();
396: ```
397: 
398: **Benefits**:
399: - ✅ Application doesn't know about SendGrid
400: - ✅ Can easily swap SendGrid for Mailgun, SMTP, or mock for testing
401: - ✅ No breaking changes to Application when Infrastructure changes
402: 
403: ---
404: 
405: ## Pattern #3: Repository Pattern for Data Access
406: 
407: ### Scenario: Application Needs Database Queries
408: 
409: **❌ Before** (Direct DbContext access):
410: ```csharp
411: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
412: using {Project}.Persistence;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
413: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
414: 
415: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
416: {
417:     private readonly {DbContext} _context;  // ❌ Concrete class
418: 
419:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
420:     {
421:         return await _context.{Entities}  // ❌ Direct DbSet access
422:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
423:             .Where(e => e.StatusId == 2)
424:             .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);
425:     }
426: }
427: ```
428: 
429: **✅ After** (Repository pattern):
430: ```csharp
431: // Step 1: Define repository interface in Application layer
432: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
433: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
434: 
435: using System;
436: using System.Collections.Generic;
437: using System.Threading.Tasks;
438: using {Project}.Domain;
439: 
440: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
441: {
442:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
443:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
444:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
445: }
446: 
447: // Step 2: Use interface in Application layer
448: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
449: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Queries;
450: 
451: using System.Collections.Generic;
452: using System.Threading;
453: using System.Threading.Tasks;
454: using AutoMapper;
455: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;  // ✅ Same layer
456: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
457: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
458: using MediatR;
459: 
460: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
461: {
462:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;  // ✅ Abstraction
463:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
464: 
465:     public Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler(I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository, IMapper mapper)
466:     {
467:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
468:         _mapper = mapper;
469:     }
470: 
471:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
472:     {
473:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // ✅ Returns List<{Entity}>
474:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});  // ✅ Maps to DTOs
475:     }
476: }
477: 
478: // Step 3: Implement repository in Persistence layer
479: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
480: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
481: 
482: using System;
483: using System.Collections.Generic;
484: using System.Linq;
485: using System.Threading.Tasks;
486: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;  // ✅ Implements interface
487: using {Project}.Domain;
488: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
489: 
490: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
491: {
492:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
493: 
494:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
495:     {
496:         _dbContext = dbContext;
497:     }
498: 
499:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
500:     {
501:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
502:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
503:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
504:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
505:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
506:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
507:             .Include(e => e.Status)
508:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
509:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
510:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
511:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
512:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity8})
513:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
514:     }
515: 
516:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
517:     {
518:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
519:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
520:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
521:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
522:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
523:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
524:             .Include(e => e.Status)
525:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
526:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
527:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
528:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
529:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity8})
530:             .ToListAsync();
531:     }
532: 
533:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
534:     {
535:         {IdType} userGuid;
536:         var isGuid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userGuid);
537: 
538:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
539:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
540:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
541:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
542:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity3})
543:                 .ThenInclude(r => r.{NestedEntity})
544:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity7})
545:             .Include(e => e.Status)
546:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity4})
547:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity5})
548:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity6})
549:             .AsQueryable();
550: 
551:         if (isGuid)
552:         {
553:             query = query.Where(e =>
554:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userGuid && u.{RelatedEntity3}Id == e.{RelatedEntity3}Id) ||
555:                 _dbContext.{ParentEntity}Members.Any(pm =>
556:                     pm.UserId == userGuid &&
557:                     _dbContext.{ParentEntities}.Any(p => p.Id == pm.{ParentEntity}Id && p.{RelatedEntity3}Id == e.{RelatedEntity3}Id)));
558:         }
559: 
560:         return await query.ToListAsync();
561:     }
562: }
563: 
564: // Step 4: Register in API (Composition Root)
565: // File: {Project}.API/Program.cs
566: builder.Services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
567: ```
568: 
569: **Benefits**:
570: - ✅ Application doesn't know about EF Core
571: - ✅ Can mock repository for unit tests
572: - ✅ Complex queries are encapsulated in Persistence
573: - ✅ Can optimize queries without changing Application
574: 
575: ---
576: 
577: ## Pattern #4: Domain Invariants vs Application Validation
578: 
579: ### Scenario: Ensuring Data Integrity
580: 
581: **Concept**:
582: - **Domain Invariants**: Rules that must ALWAYS be true (enforced in Domain)
583: - **Application Validation**: Input validation that can vary by use case (enforced in Application)
584: 
585: **❌ Before** (Validation in wrong place):
586: ```csharp
587: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
588: using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;  // ❌ VIOLATION!
589: 
590: public class {Entity}
591: {
592:     [Required]  // ❌ Presentation concern
593:     [MaxLength(500)]  // ❌ Database concern
594:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
595: 
596:     [Range(1, 10000)]  // ❌ Arbitrary validation rule
597:     public int? MaxAttendees { get; set; }
598: }
599: ```
600: 
601: **✅ After** (Proper separation):
602: ```csharp
603: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
604: namespace {Project}.Domain;
605: 
606: using System;
607: using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;
608: 
609: public class {Entity}
610: {
611:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
612:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
613:     public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
614:     public decimal? Price { get; set; }
615:     public string CurrencyCode { get; set; } = string.Empty;
616:     public int ViewCount { get; set; }
617: 
618:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
619:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
620:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; } = null!;
621: 
622:     [ForeignKey("{RelatedEntity1}")]
623:     public {LookupIdType} {RelatedEntity1}Id { get; set; }
624:     public {RelatedEntity1} {RelatedEntity1} { get; set; } = null!;
625: 
626:     // ✅ No validation annotations - domain is pure
627: }
628: 
629: // File: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
630: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
631: 
632: using FluentValidation;
633: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
634: 
635: // ✅ INPUT VALIDATION: Can vary by use case
636: public class Create{Entity}DtoValidator : AbstractValidator<Create{Entity}Dto>
637: {
638:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity1}Repository _{relatedEntity1}Repository;
639:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity2}Repository _{relatedEntity2}Repository;
640:     private readonly I{LookupEntity}Repository _{lookupEntity}Repository;
641: 
642:     public Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
643:         I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository,
644:         I{RelatedEntity2}Repository {relatedEntity2}Repository,
645:         I{LookupEntity}Repository {lookupEntity}Repository)
646:     {
647:         _{relatedEntity1}Repository = {relatedEntity1}Repository;
