 38:         builder.Property(e => e.Timezone).HasMaxLength(100);
 39: 
 40:         // Relationships (use Restrict for most FK deletes)
 41:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
 42:             .WithMany()
 43:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
 44:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
 45:     }
 46: }
 47: ```
 48: 
 49: ---
 50: 
 51: ## Common Patterns
 52: 
 53: ### TPT (Table Per Type) Strategy
 54: 
 55: ```csharp
 56: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
 57: {
 58:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
 59:     {
 60:         // ✅ TPT Strategy (project standard)
 61:         builder.UseTptMappingStrategy();
 62: 
 63:         // Each derived type gets its own table
 64:         // Base {Entity} table + derived tables
 65:     }
 66: }
 67: ```
 68: 
 69: **Why TPT?**
 70: - ✅ Normalized data (no discriminator column)
 71: - ✅ No null columns for unused properties
 72: - ✅ Clean separation of types
 73: 
 74: **Alternatives**:
 75: - `UseTphMappingStrategy()` - Table Per Hierarchy (single table with discriminator)
 76: - `UseTpcMappingStrategy()` - Table Per Concrete (one table per concrete type)
 77: 
 78: ### PostgreSQL UUIDv7 Primary Keys
 79: 
 80: ```csharp
 81: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
 82: {
 83:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
 84:     {
 85:         // ✅ PostgreSQL function for UUIDv7
 86:         builder.Property(e => e.Id)
 87:                .HasDefaultValueSql("uuidv7()");
 88:     }
 89: }
 90: ```
 91: 
 92: **Why UUIDv7?**
 93: - ✅ Time-ordered (better index performance than random UUIDs)
 94: - ✅ Globally unique
 95: - ✅ No identity column contention
 96: 
 97: ### Default Values
 98: 
 99: ```csharp
100: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
101: {
102:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
103:     {
104:         // Default value in database
105:         builder.Property(e => e.ViewCount)
106:                .HasDefaultValue(0);
107: 
108:         // Use DB defaults only for stable, cross-cutting values.
109:         // Prefer setting business defaults in Application handlers.
110:     }
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## Property Configuration
117: 
118: ### Required Properties
119: 
120: ```csharp
121: builder.Property(e => e.Title)
122:        .IsRequired()
123:        .HasMaxLength(200);
124: 
125: builder.Property(e => e.Email)
126:        .IsRequired()
127:        .HasMaxLength(255);
128: ```
129: 
130: ### Optional Properties
131: 
132: ```csharp
133: // Nullable reference type (C# 10+)
134: builder.Property(e => e.Description)
135:        .HasMaxLength(2000);  // Optional - no IsRequired()
136: 
137: // Nullable value type
138: builder.Property(e => e.EndDate)
139:        .HasColumnType("timestamp");  // DateTime? is automatically optional
140: ```
141: 
142: ### Max Length
143: 
144: ```csharp
145: builder.Property(e => e.Title).HasMaxLength(200);
146: builder.Property(e => e.ShortDescription).HasMaxLength(500);
147: builder.Property(e => e.Description).HasMaxLength(2000);
148: builder.Property(e => e.Email).HasMaxLength(255);
149: ```
150: 
151: ### Column Types (PostgreSQL)
152: 
153: ```csharp
154: // Text
155: builder.Property(e => e.Description)
156:        .HasColumnType("text");
157: 
158: // Timestamp
159: // If your entity uses DateTimeOffset/DateTime columns:
160: // builder.Property(e => e.CreatedAt)
161: //        .HasColumnType("timestamp with time zone");
162: 
163: // JSON
164: builder.Property(e => e.Metadata)
165:        .HasColumnType("jsonb");
166: 
167: // Decimal with precision
168: builder.Property(e => e.Price)
169:        .HasColumnType("decimal(18,2)");
170: 
171: // Geography (PostGIS)
172: builder.Property(e => e.Location)
173:        .HasColumnType("geography(point)");
174: ```
175: 
176: ---
177: 
178: ## Relationships
179: 
180: ### One-to-Many
181: 
182: ```csharp
183: // {ParentEntity} has many {Entities} (current model: {Entity} references {ParentEntity}, but {ParentEntity} doesn't expose a collection navigation)
184: builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
185:        .WithMany()
186:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
187:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Many-to-One
191: 
192: ```csharp
193: // {Entity} belongs to one Tenant
194: builder.HasOne(e => e.Tenant)
195:        .WithMany()
196:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.TenantId)
197:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
198: ```
199: 
200: ### Many-to-Many
201: 
202: ```csharp
203: // {Entity} <-> Category uses a mapping entity with its own Id
204: public class {Entity}CategoriesConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}Categories>
205: {
206:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}Categories> builder)
207:     {
208:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{Entity})
209:             .WithMany()
210:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{Entity}Id)
211:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade);
212: 
213:         builder.HasOne(e => e.Category)
214:             .WithMany()
215:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.CategoryId)
216:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Cascade);
217: 
218:         builder.HasOne(e => e.Tenant)
219:             .WithMany()
220:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.TenantId)
221:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
222:     }
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### One-to-One
227: 
228: ```csharp
229: // User has one Profile
230: public class UserConfiguration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<User>
231: {
232:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<User> builder)
233:     {
234:         builder.HasOne(u => u.Profile)
235:                .WithOne(p => p.User)
236:                .HasForeignKey<UserProfile>(p => p.UserId);
237:     }
238: }
239: ```
240: 
241: ---
242: 
243: ## Delete Behavior
244: 
245: ```csharp
246: builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
247:        .WithMany()
248:        .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
249:        .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
250: ```
251: 
252: | Behavior | Description |
253: |----------|-------------|
254: | `Cascade` | Delete dependents when principal deleted |
255: | `Restrict` | Prevent delete if dependents exist |
256: | `SetNull` | Set foreign key to null when principal deleted |
257: | `NoAction` | No action (database handles it) |
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## Indexes
262: 
263: ### Simple Index
264: 
265: ```csharp
266: builder.HasIndex(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id);
267: builder.HasIndex(e => e.TenantId);
268: ```
269: 
270: ### Composite Index
271: 
272: ```csharp
273: builder.HasIndex(e => new { e.TenantId, e.{ParentEntity}Id });
274: ```
275: 
276: ### Unique Index
277: 
278: ```csharp
279: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Email).IsUnique();
280: ```
281: 
282: ### Named Index
283: 
284: ```csharp
285: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Title)
286:        .HasDatabaseName("IX_{Entities}_Title");
287: ```
288: 
289: ### Filtered Index (PostgreSQL)
290: 
291: ```csharp
292: builder.HasIndex(e => e.Email)
293:        .IsUnique()
294:        .HasFilter("\"Email\" IS NOT NULL");
295: ```
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## Value Conversions
300: 
301: ### Enum to String
302: 
303: ```csharp
304: builder.Property(e => e.Status)
305:        .HasConversion<string>();  // Store enum as string in database
306: ```
307: 
308: ### JSON Column
309: 
310: ```csharp
311: builder.Property(e => e.Metadata)
312:        .HasConversion(
313:            v => JsonSerializer.Serialize(v, (JsonSerializerOptions)null!),
314:            v => JsonSerializer.Deserialize<Dictionary<string, string>>(v, (JsonSerializerOptions)null!)!)
315:        .HasColumnType("jsonb");
316: ```
317: 
318: ### Custom Value Converter
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: var converter = new ValueConverter<List<string>, string>(
322:     v => string.Join(',', v),
323:     v => v.Split(',', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).ToList());
324: 
325: builder.Property(e => e.Tags)
326:        .HasConversion(converter);
327: ```
328: 
329: ---
330: 
331: ## Owned Types
332: 
333: For value objects that don't have their own identity.
334: 
335: ```csharp
336: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
337: {
338:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
339:     {
340:         // Address is an owned type
341:         builder.OwnsOne(e => e.Address, address =>
342:         {
343:             address.Property(a => a.Street).HasMaxLength(200);
344:             address.Property(a => a.City).HasMaxLength(100);
345:             address.Property(a => a.Country).HasMaxLength(100);
346:         });
347:     }
348: }
349: ```
350: 
351: ---
352: 
353: ## Table Splitting
354: 
355: Multiple entities mapped to same table.
356: 
357: ```csharp
358: // {Entity} and {Entity}Details share same table
359: builder.ToTable("{Entities}");
360: builder.HasOne(e => e.Details)
361:        .WithOne()
362:        .HasForeignKey<{Entity}Details>(d => d.{Entity}Id);
363: 
364: // {Entity}Details configuration
365: builder.ToTable("{Entities}");  // Same table as {Entity}
366: ```
367: 
368: ---
369: 
370: ## Temporal Tables (SQL Server)
371: 
372: ```csharp
373: // Enable temporal table (SQL Server only)
374: builder.ToTable("{Entities}", b => b.IsTemporal(
375:     temporal =>
376:     {
377:         temporal.HasPeriodStart("ValidFrom");
378:         temporal.HasPeriodEnd("ValidTo");
379:         temporal.UseHistoryTable("{Entities}History");
380:     }));
381: ```
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## Best Practices
386: 
387: | Practice | Reason |
388: |----------|--------|
389: | ✅ One configuration class per entity | Separation of concerns |
390: | ✅ Use `HasMaxLength` for strings | Database optimization |
391: | ✅ Specify `IsRequired` explicitly | Clear intent |
392: | ✅ Use `TPT` for inheritance (project standard) | Clean separation |
393: | ✅ Use PostgreSQL functions (`uuidv7()`) | Better performance |
394: | ✅ Configure indexes for foreign keys | Query performance |
395: | ✅ Use `DeleteBehavior.Cascade` carefully | Data integrity |
396: | ❌ Don't configure in OnModelCreating | Use IEntityTypeConfiguration |
397: | ❌ Don't use magic strings for column types | Use HasColumnType |
398: 
399: ---
400: 
401: **Related Resources**:
402: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
403: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
404: - [migrations.md](migrations.md) - Creating migrations
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/migrations.md
````markdown
  1: # Migrations
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Migration Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## What are Migrations?
 10: 
 11: Migrations are version-controlled schema changes that allow you to evolve your database schema over time.
 12: 
 13: ```
 14: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 15: │                       MIGRATION WORKFLOW                            │
 16: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 17: │                                                                     │
 18: │  1. Change Domain Model (Add/Remove/Modify entities)                │
 19: │     ↓                                                               │
 20: │  2. Create Migration (dotnet ef migrations add)                     │
 21: │     ↓                                                               │
 22: │  3. Review Generated SQL                                            │
 23: │     ↓                                                               │
 24: │  4. Apply Migration (dotnet ef database update)                     │
 25: │     ↓                                                               │
 26: │  5. Database Schema Updated                                         │
 27: │                                                                     │
 28: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 29: ```
 30: 
 31: ---
 32: 
 33: ## Creating Migrations
 34: 
 35: ### Add Migration
 36: 
 37: ```bash
 38: # Basic migration
 39: dotnet ef migrations add Add{Entity}Entity --project {Project}.Persistence
 40: ```
 41: 
 42: ### Migration Naming Conventions
 43: 
 44: | Pattern | Example | Use Case |
 45: |---------|---------|----------|
 46: | `Add{Entity}` | `AddEvent` | New entity |
 47: | `Add{Property}To{Entity}` | `AddDescriptionToEvent` | New property |
 48: | `Remove{Property}From{Entity}` | `RemoveOldFieldFromEvent` | Remove property |
 49: | `Update{Entity}{Property}` | `UpdateEventTitleMaxLength` | Modify property |
 50: | `Add{Entity}{Relationship}` | `AddEventOrganizationRelationship` | New relationship |
 51: | `Initial` | `InitialCreate` | First migration |
 52: 
 53: ---
 54: 
 55: ## Migration Structure
 56: 
 57: A migration consists of two methods:
 58: 
 59: ```csharp
 60: public partial class Add{Entity}Entity : Migration
 61: {
 62:     // Applied when migrating up (forward)
 63:     protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
 64:     {
 65:         migrationBuilder.CreateTable(
 66:             name: "{Entities}",
 67:             columns: table => new
 68:             {
 69:                 Id = table.Column<Guid>(type: "uuid", nullable: false, defaultValueSql: "uuidv7()"),
 70:                 Title = table.Column<string>(type: "character varying(200)", maxLength: 200, nullable: false),
 71:                 Description = table.Column<string>(type: "text", nullable: true),
 72:                 StartDate = table.Column<DateTime>(type: "timestamp with time zone", nullable: false),
 73:                 ViewCount = table.Column<int>(type: "integer", nullable: false, defaultValue: 0)
 74:             },
 75:             constraints: table =>
 76:             {
 77:                 table.PrimaryKey("PK_{Entities}", x => x.Id);
 78:             });
 79:     }
 80: 
 81:     // Applied when rolling back (backward)
 82:     protected override void Down(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
 83:     {
 84:         migrationBuilder.DropTable(name: "{Entities}");
 85:     }
 86: }
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ## Applying Migrations
 92: 
 93: ### Update Database
 94: 
 95: ```bash
 96: # Apply all pending migrations
 97: dotnet ef database update --project {Project}.Persistence
 98: 
 99: # Apply to specific migration
100: dotnet ef database update Add{Entity}Entity --project {Project}.Persistence
101: 
102: # Rollback to previous migration
103: dotnet ef database update PreviousMigrationName --project {Project}.Persistence
104: 
105: # Rollback all migrations
106: dotnet ef database update 0 --project {Project}.Persistence
107: ```
108: 
109: ### Generate SQL Script
110: 
111: ```bash
112: # Generate SQL for all migrations
113: dotnet ef migrations script \
114:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
115:   --output migration.sql
116: 
117: # Generate SQL for specific migration
118: dotnet ef migrations script Add{Entity}Entity \
119:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
120:   --output add-{entity}.sql
121: 
122: # Generate SQL from specific migration to another
123: dotnet ef migrations script Migration1 Migration2 \
124:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
125:   --output migration-1-to-2.sql
126: 
127: # Idempotent script (can run multiple times)
128: dotnet ef migrations script \
129:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
130:   --idempotent \
131:   --output migration.sql
132: ```
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## Custom Migration Code
137: 
138: ### Add Custom SQL
139: 
140: ```csharp
141: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
142: {
143:     // Create table
144:     migrationBuilder.CreateTable(/* ... */);
145: 
146:     // ✅ Add custom SQL
147:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
148:         CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION uuidv7() RETURNS uuid AS $$
149:         DECLARE
150:             unix_ts_ms BIGINT;
151:             uuid_bytes BYTEA;
152:         BEGIN
153:             unix_ts_ms = (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CLOCK_TIMESTAMP()) * 1000)::BIGINT;
154:             uuid_bytes = E'\\x' ||
155:                 LPAD(TO_HEX(unix_ts_ms), 12, '0') ||
156:                 GEN_RANDOM_BYTES(10)::TEXT;
157:             RETURN uuid_bytes::UUID;
158:         END;
159:         $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
160:     ");
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: ### Create Index
165: 
166: ```csharp
167: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
168: {
169:     // ✅ Create index
170:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
171:         name: "IX_{Entities}_StartDate",
172:         table: "{Entities}",
173:         column: "StartDate");
174: 
175:     // ✅ Create composite index
176:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
177:         name: "IX_{Entities}_{ParentEntity}Id_StartDate",
178:         table: "{Entities}",
179:         columns: new[] { "{ParentEntity}Id", "StartDate" });
180: 
181:     // ✅ Create unique index
182:     migrationBuilder.CreateIndex(
183:         name: "IX_Users_Email",
184:         table: "Users",
185:         column: "Email",
186:         unique: true);
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Add Column
191: 
192: ```csharp
193: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
194: {
195:     // ✅ Add nullable column (safe)
196:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string>(
197:         name: "Subtitle",
198:         table: "{Entities}",
199:         type: "character varying(200)",
200:         maxLength: 200,
201:         nullable: true);
202: 
203:     // ⚠️ Add non-nullable column (requires default)
204:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<int>(
205:         name: "Priority",
206:         table: "{Entities}",
207:         type: "integer",
208:         nullable: false,
209:         defaultValue: 0);
210: }
211: ```
212: 
213: ### Modify Column
214: 
215: ```csharp
216: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
217: {
218:     // ✅ Change column type
219:     migrationBuilder.AlterColumn<string>(
220:         name: "Title",
221:         table: "{Entities}",
222:         type: "character varying(500)",  // Changed from 200
223:         maxLength: 500,
224:         nullable: false,
225:         oldClrType: typeof(string),
226:         oldType: "character varying(200)",
227:         oldMaxLength: 200);
228: }
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Rename Column/Table
232: 
233: ```csharp
234: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
235: {
236:     // ✅ Rename column
237:     migrationBuilder.RenameColumn(
238:         name: "OldName",
239:         table: "{Entities}",
240:         newName: "NewName");
241: 
242:     // ✅ Rename table
243:     migrationBuilder.RenameTable(
244:         name: "OldTableName",
245:         newName: "NewTableName");
246: }
247: ```
248: 
249: ---
250: 
251: ## Data Migrations
252: 
253: ### Seed Data
254: 
255: ```csharp
256: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
257: {
258:     // ✅ Insert seed data
259:     migrationBuilder.InsertData(
260:         table: "{LookupEntity}s",
261:         columns: new[] { "Id", "FullName", "Description" },
262:         values: new object[,]
263:         {
264:             { 1, "Type A", "Description for Type A" },
265:             { 2, "Type B", "Description for Type B" },
266:             { 3, "Type C", "Description for Type C" }
267:         });
268: }
269: 
270: protected override void Down(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
271: {
272:     // ✅ Remove seed data
273:     migrationBuilder.DeleteData(
274:         table: "{LookupEntity}s",
275:         keyColumn: "Id",
276:         keyValues: new object[] { 1, 2, 3 });
277: }
278: ```
279: 
280: ### Data Transformation
281: 
282: ```csharp
283: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
284: {
285:     // ✅ Transform existing data
286:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
287:         UPDATE ""{Entities}""
288:         SET ""Title"" = UPPER(""Title"")
289:         WHERE ""Title"" IS NOT NULL;
290:     ");
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: ---
295: 
296: ## PostgreSQL-Specific Migrations
297: 
298: ### PostGIS Extension
299: 
300: ```csharp
301: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
302: {
303:     // ✅ Enable PostGIS extension
304:     migrationBuilder.Sql("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;");
305: 
306:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<NetTopologySuite.Geometries.Point>(
307:         name: "Location",
308:         table: "{Entities}",
309:         type: "geography(point)",
310:         nullable: true);
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ### JSONB Column
315: 
316: ```csharp
317: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
318: {
319:     // ✅ Add JSONB column
320:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string>(
321:         name: "Metadata",
322:         table: "{Entities}",
323:         type: "jsonb",
324:         nullable: true);
325: 
326:     // ✅ Create GIN index for JSONB
327:     migrationBuilder.Sql(@"
328:         CREATE INDEX IX_{Entities}_Metadata
329:         ON ""{Entities}"" USING GIN (""Metadata"");
330:     ");
331: }
332: ```
333: 
334: ### Array Column
335: 
336: ```csharp
337: protected override void Up(MigrationBuilder migrationBuilder)
338: {
339:     // ✅ Add array column
340:     migrationBuilder.AddColumn<string[]>(
341:         name: "Tags",
342:         table: "{Entities}",
343:         type: "text[]",
344:         nullable: true);
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: ## Migration Management
351: 
352: ### List Migrations
353: 
354: ```bash
355: # List all migrations
356: dotnet ef migrations list --project {Project}.Persistence
357: ```
358: 
359: ### Remove Last Migration
360: 
361: ```bash
362: # ⚠️ ONLY if not applied to database
363: dotnet ef migrations remove --project {Project}.Persistence
364: 
365: # ❌ DON'T remove if already applied - create a new migration instead
366: ```
367: 
368: ### Check Pending Migrations
369: 
370: ```csharp
371: // In code
372: var pendingMigrations = await _dbContext.Database.GetPendingMigrationsAsync();
373: if (pendingMigrations.Any())
374: {
375:     // Migrations need to be applied
376:     Console.WriteLine($"Pending migrations: {string.Join(", ", pendingMigrations)}");
377: }
378: ```
379: 
380: ### Apply Migrations Programmatically
381: 
382: ```csharp
383: // Program.cs - Apply migrations on startup
384: using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
385: var dbContext = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<{DbContext}>();
386: 
387: // ✅ Apply pending migrations
388: await dbContext.Database.MigrateAsync();
389: ```
390: 
391: ---
392: 
393: ## Best Practices
394: 
395: | Practice | Reason |
396: |----------|--------|
397: | ✅ Review generated SQL before applying | Catch issues early |
398: | ✅ Use descriptive migration names | Easy to understand history |
399: | ✅ Add indexes for foreign keys | Query performance |
400: | ✅ Make nullable columns when adding to existing tables | Avoid data loss |
401: | ✅ Use transactions for data migrations | Data integrity |
402: | ✅ Test migrations on copy of production data | Validate before production |
403: | ✅ Keep migrations small and focused | Easier to review and rollback |
404: | ✅ Generate idempotent SQL scripts for production | Safe deployment |
405: | ❌ Don't remove migrations after applied | Breaks history |
406: | ❌ Don't modify migrations after applied | Use new migration |
407: | ❌ Don't include sensitive data in migrations | Security risk |
408: 
409: ---
410: 
411: ## Troubleshooting
412: 
413: ### Migration Already Applied
414: 
415: ```bash
416: # Error: "The migration '20240101120000_MigrationName' has already been applied to the database."
417: 
418: # ✅ Solution: Create a new migration for changes
419: dotnet ef migrations add UpdateMigration --project {Project}.Persistence
420: ```
421: 
422: ### Conflicting Migrations
423: 
424: ```bash
425: # Error: "Your migrations are out of sync"
426: 
427: # ✅ Solution 1: Pull latest and rebase
428: git pull origin main
429: dotnet ef migrations remove  # If not yet applied
430: 
431: # ✅ Solution 2: Create new migration
432: dotnet ef migrations add ResolveMergeConflict --project {Project}.Persistence
433: ```
434: 
435: ### Connection String Not Found
436: 
437: ```bash
438: # Error: "No connection string named 'DefaultConnection' was found"
439: 
440: # ✅ Solution: Specify connection string
441: dotnet ef database update \
442:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
443:   --connection "Host=localhost;Database={project}_db;Username=postgres;Password=password"
444: ```
445: 
446: ---
447: 
448: ## Production Deployment
449: 
450: ### Generate SQL Script for DBA
451: 
452: ```bash
453: # ✅ Generate idempotent SQL script
454: dotnet ef migrations script \
455:   --project {Project}.Persistence \
456:   --idempotent \
457:   --output migrations/release-1.0.0.sql
458: ```
459: 
460: ### Manual vs Automatic
461: 
462: **Manual (Recommended for Production)**:
463: ```bash
464: # 1. Generate SQL script
465: dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent --output release.sql
466: 
467: # 2. Review script with DBA
468: # 3. DBA applies script to production database
469: ```
470: 
471: **Automatic (Development Only)**:
472: ```csharp
473: // Program.cs
474: if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
475: {
476:     using var scope = app.Services.CreateScope();
477:     var dbContext = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<{DbContext}>();
478:     await dbContext.Database.MigrateAsync();  // ✅ Auto-apply in dev only
479: }
480: ```
481: 
482: ---
483: 
484: **Related Resources**:
485: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
486: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity configuration
487: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/querying-patterns.md
````markdown
  1: # Querying Patterns
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Querying Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Basic Queries
 10: 
 11: ### Get All
 12: 
 13: ```csharp
 14: // ✅ Simple get all
 15: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.ToListAsync();
 16: 
 17: // ✅ With AsNoTracking for read-only
 18: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 19:     .AsNoTracking()
 20:     .ToListAsync();
 21: ```
 22: 
 23: ### Get By ID
 24: 
 25: ```csharp
 26: // ✅ FindAsync (uses primary key)
 27: var {entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.FindAsync({entity}Id);
 28: 
 29: // ✅ FirstOrDefaultAsync with condition
 30: var {entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 31:     .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == {entity}Id);
 32: ```
 33: 
 34: ### Get Single
 35: 
 36: ```csharp
 37: // ✅ SingleOrDefaultAsync (throws if multiple)
 38: var {entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 39:     .SingleOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == {entity}Id);
 40: 
 41: // ⚠️ Use only when expecting exactly 0 or 1 result
 42: ```
 43: 
 44: ---
 45: 
 46: ## Filtering
 47: 
 48: ### Where Clause
 49: 
 50: ```csharp
 51: // Simple filter
 52: var upcoming{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 53:     .Where(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now)
 54:     .ToListAsync();
 55: 
 56: // Multiple conditions
 57: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 58:     .Where(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id == parentId &&
 59:                 e.StartDate > DateTime.Now &&
 60:                 !e.IsCancelled)
 61:     .ToListAsync();
 62: 
 63: // String contains (case-sensitive in PostgreSQL)
 64: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 65:     .Where(e => e.Title.Contains(searchTerm))
 66:     .ToListAsync();
 67: 
 68: // Case-insensitive search (PostgreSQL)
 69: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 70:     .Where(e => EF.Functions.ILike(e.Title, $"%{searchTerm}%"))
 71:     .ToListAsync();
 72: ```
 73: 
 74: ---
 75: 
 76: ## Eager Loading (Include)
 77: 
 78: ### Single Level
 79: 
 80: ```csharp
 81: // ✅ Load {entities} with {parentEntity}
 82: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 83:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
 84:     .ToListAsync();
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: ### Multiple Includes
 88: 
 89: ```csharp
 90: // ✅ Multiple related entities
 91: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 92:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
 93:     .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
 94:     .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
 95:     .Include(e => e.Status)
 96:     .ToListAsync();
 97: ```
 98: 
 99: ### Nested Include (ThenInclude)
100: 
101: ```csharp
102: // ✅ Load {entities} with {parentEntity} and members
103: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
104:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
105:         .ThenInclude(o => o.Members)
106:     .ToListAsync();
107: 
108: // ✅ Multiple levels
109: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
110:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
111:         .ThenInclude(o => o.Members)
112:             .ThenInclude(m => m.User)
113:     .ToListAsync();
114: ```
115: 
116: ### Filtered Include (EF Core 5+)
117: 
118: ```csharp
119: // ✅ Only include approved members
120: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
121:     .Include(o => o.Members.Where(m => m.IsApproved))
122:     .ToListAsync();
123: 
124: // ✅ Only include upcoming {entities}
125: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
126:     .Include(o => o.{Entities}.Where(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now))
127:     .ToListAsync();
128: ```
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## Projection (Select)
133: 
134: ### Project to DTO
135: 
136: ```csharp
137: // ✅ RECOMMENDED: Project directly to DTO
138: var {entity}Dtos = await _dbContext.{Entities}
139:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
140:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
141:     {
142:         Id = e.Id,
143:         Title = e.Title,
144:         Description = e.Description,
145:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName,  // ✅ No N+1 query
146:         StartDate = e.StartDate
147:     })
148:     .ToListAsync();
149: ```
150: 
151: **Benefits**:
152: - ✅ Only selected columns retrieved
153: - ✅ No change tracking
154: - ✅ Faster than loading entire entities
155: 
156: ### Anonymous Type
157: 
158: ```csharp
159: // ✅ Project to anonymous type
160: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
161:     .Select(e => new
162:     {
163:         e.Id,
164:         e.Title,
165:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName
166:     })
167:     .ToListAsync();
168: ```
169: 
170: ### Conditional Projection
171: 
172: ```csharp
173: // ✅ Conditional fields in projection
174: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
175:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
176:     {
177:         Id = e.Id,
178:         Title = e.Title,
179:         IsUpcoming = e.StartDate > DateTime.Now,  // Computed
180:         DaysUntil = (e.StartDate - DateTime.Now).Days  // Computed
181:     })
182:     .ToListAsync();
183: ```
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Sorting
188: 
189: ### OrderBy
190: 
191: ```csharp
192: // ✅ Ascending
193: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
194:     .OrderBy(e => e.StartDate)
195:     .ToListAsync();
196: 
197: // ✅ Descending
198: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
199:     .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
200:     .ToListAsync();
201: 
202: // ✅ Multiple sort criteria
203: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
204:     .OrderBy(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
205:     .ThenByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
206:     .ToListAsync();
207: ```
208: 
209: ### Dynamic Sorting
210: 
211: ```csharp
212: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Get{Entities}(string sortBy, bool descending)
213: {
214:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.AsQueryable();
215: 
216:     query = sortBy switch
217:     {
218:         "title" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.Title) : query.OrderBy(e => e.Title),
219:         "date" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate) : query.OrderBy(e => e.StartDate),
220:         "views" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.ViewCount) : query.OrderBy(e => e.ViewCount),
221:         _ => query.OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)  // Default
222:     };
223: 
224:     return await query
225:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
226:         .ToListAsync();
227: }
228: ```
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## Pagination
233: 
234: ### Skip and Take
235: 
236: ```csharp
237: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Get{Entities}Paginated(int page, int pageSize)
238: {
239:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
240:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
241:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
242:         .Take(pageSize)
243:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
244:         .ToListAsync();
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: ### With Total Count
249: 
250: ```csharp
251: public async Task<(List<{Entity}ListDto> {Entities}, int TotalCount)> Get{Entities}Paginated(
252:     int page,
253:     int pageSize)
254: {
255:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.AsQueryable();
256: 
257:     var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
258: 
259:     var {entities} = await query
260:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
261:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
262:         .Take(pageSize)
263:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
264:         .ToListAsync();
265: 
266:     return ({entities}, totalCount);
267: }
268: ```
269: 
270: ---
271: 
272: ## Aggregation
273: 
274: ### Count
275: 
276: ```csharp
277: // Total count
278: var total{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.CountAsync();
279: 
280: // Conditional count
281: var upcomingCount = await _dbContext.{Entities}
282:     .CountAsync(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now);
283: ```
284: 
285: ### Sum, Average, Min, Max
286: 
287: ```csharp
288: // Sum
289: var totalViews = await _dbContext.{Entities}.SumAsync(e => e.ViewCount);
290: 
291: // Average
292: var avgPrice = await _dbContext.{Entities}.AverageAsync(e => e.Price);
293: 
294: // Min and Max
295: var earliest{Entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.MinAsync(e => e.StartDate);
296: var latest{Entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.MaxAsync(e => e.StartDate);
297: ```
298: 
299: ### GroupBy
300: 
301: ```csharp
302: // Group {entities} by {parentEntity}
303: var {entities}By{ParentEntity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
304:     .GroupBy(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
305:     .Select(g => new
306:     {
307:         {ParentEntity}Id = g.Key,
308:         {Entity}Count = g.Count(),
309:         TotalViews = g.Sum(e => e.ViewCount)
310:     })
311:     .ToListAsync();
312: ```
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: ## Joining
317: 
318: ### Explicit Join
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: var result = await (
322:     from e in _dbContext.{Entities}
323:     join o in _dbContext.{ParentEntities} on e.{ParentEntity}Id equals o.Id
324:     select new {Entity}ListDto
325:     {
326:         Id = e.Id,
327:         Title = e.Title,
328:         {ParentEntity}Name = o.FullName
329:     })
330:     .ToListAsync();
331: ```
332: 
333: ### Include vs Join
334: 
335: ```csharp
336: // ❌ Include (loads entire related entity)
337: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
338:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
339:     .ToListAsync();
340: 
341: // ✅ Select (only needed fields)
342: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
343:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
344:     {
345:         Id = e.Id,
346:         Title = e.Title,
347:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName  // Automatic join
348:     })
349:     .ToListAsync();
350: ```
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## Advanced Patterns
355: 
356: ### AsNoTracking
357: 
358: ```csharp
359: // ✅ Use for read-only queries (faster)
360: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
361:     .AsNoTracking()
362:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
363:     .ToListAsync();
364: ```
365: 
366: ### AsSplitQuery
367: 
368: ```csharp
369: // ✅ Avoid cartesian explosion with multiple Includes
370: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
371:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
372:     .Include(o => o.Members)
373:     .AsSplitQuery()  // Executes as 3 separate SQL queries
374:     .ToListAsync();
375: 
376: // ❌ Single query (can cause performance issues)
377: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
378:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
379:     .Include(o => o.Members)
380:     .ToListAsync();
381: ```
382: 
383: ### FromSqlRaw (Raw SQL)
384: 
385: ```csharp
386: // ✅ Use for complex queries not supported by LINQ
387: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
388:     .FromSqlRaw(@"
389:         SELECT * FROM ""{Entities}""
390:         WHERE ""StartDate"" > {0}
391:         ORDER BY ""ViewCount"" DESC
392:     ", DateTime.Now)
393:     .ToListAsync();
394: 
395: // ⚠️ Use parameters to prevent SQL injection
396: var searchTerm = "conference";
397: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
398:     .FromSqlRaw(@"
399:         SELECT * FROM ""{Entities}""
400:         WHERE ""Title"" ILIKE {0}
401:     ", $"%{searchTerm}%")
402:     .ToListAsync();
403: ```
404: 
405: ### Any / All / Contains
406: 
407: ```csharp
408: // Any: Check if any records exist
409: var hasUpcoming{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
410:     .AnyAsync(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now);
411: 
412: // All: Check if all records match condition
413: var allFree = await _dbContext.{Entities}
414:     .AllAsync(e => e.Price == 0);
415: 
416: // Contains: Check if value in list
417: var {parentEntity}Ids = new[] { guid1, guid2, guid3 };
418: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
419:     .Where(e => {parentEntity}Ids.Contains(e.{ParentEntity}Id))
420:     .ToListAsync();
421: ```
422: 
423: ---
424: 
425: ## Performance Optimization
426: 
427: ### N+1 Query Problem
428: 
429: ```csharp
430: // ❌ N+1 PROBLEM: Loads {parentEntity} for each {entity}
431: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.ToListAsync();
432: foreach (var item in {entities})
433: {
434:     Console.WriteLine(item.{ParentEntity}.FullName);  // ❌ Separate query per item!
435: }
436: 
437: // ✅ FIX 1: Use Include
438: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
439:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
440:     .ToListAsync();
441: 
442: // ✅ FIX 2: Use Select (RECOMMENDED)
443: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
444:     .Select(e => new
445:     {
446:         e.Id,
447:         e.Title,
448:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName  // ✅ Single query
449:     })
450:     .ToListAsync();
451: ```
452: 
453: ### Avoid Loading Entire Entity
454: 
455: ```csharp
456: // ❌ Loads entire entity (all columns)
457: var titles = await _dbContext.{Entities}
458:     .ToListAsync()
459:     .Select(e => e.Title);  // ❌ Executes in memory
460: 
461: // ✅ Project to only needed columns
462: var titles = await _dbContext.{Entities}
463:     .Select(e => e.Title)
464:     .ToListAsync();  // ✅ Only selects Title column
465: ```
466: 
467: ### Compiled Queries
468: 
469: ```csharp
470: // Define compiled query (cached)
471: private static readonly Func<{DbContext}, {IdType}, Task<{Entity}?>> _get{Entity}ById =
472:     EF.CompileAsyncQuery(({DbContext} context, {IdType} id) =>
473:         context.{Entities}.FirstOrDefault(e => e.Id == id));
474: 
475: // Use compiled query
476: var {entity} = await _get{Entity}ById(_dbContext, {entity}Id);
477: ```
478: 
479: ---
480: 
481: ## Best Practices
482: 
483: | Practice | Reason |
484: |----------|--------|
485: | ✅ Use `Select` for projections | Only retrieves needed columns |
486: | ✅ Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only | Faster, no change tracking |
487: | ✅ Use `Include` for related data | Avoid N+1 queries |
488: | ✅ Use `AsSplitQuery()` for multiple includes | Avoid cartesian explosion |
489: | ✅ Filter before sorting/paging | Reduces data processed |
490: | ✅ Use `CountAsync()` instead of `Count()` | Non-blocking |
491: | ✅ Use parameters in raw SQL | Prevent SQL injection |
492: | ❌ Don't use `ToList()` before filtering | Loads all data into memory |
493: | ❌ Don't access navigation properties without Include | Causes N+1 |
494: | ❌ Don't track entities for read-only queries | Unnecessary overhead |
495: 
496: ---
497: 
498: **Related Resources**:
499: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
500: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
501: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity relationships
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/repository-pattern.md
````markdown
  1: # Repository Pattern
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Repository Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Why Repository Pattern?
 10: 
 11: ```
 12: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 13: │                    BENEFITS OF REPOSITORY PATTERN                   │
 14: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 15: │                                                                     │
 16: │  ✅ Abstraction: Application layer doesn't depend on EF Core        │
 17: │  ✅ Testability: Easy to mock repositories for unit tests          │
 18: │  ✅ Clean Architecture: Maintains dependency inversion              │
 19: │  ✅ Centralized Data Access: Common queries in one place            │
 20: │  ✅ Consistent API: Uniform data access across entities             │
 21: │                                                                     │
 22: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 23: ```
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: ## Generic Repository
 28: 
 29: Base repository with common CRUD operations.
 30: 
 31: ### Interface (Application Layer)
 32: 
 33: ```csharp
 34: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/IGenericRepository.cs
 35: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 36: 
 37: public interface IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 38: {
 39:     Task<T> Create(T entity);
 40:     Task<T?> GetById(TKey id);
 41:     Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll();
 42:     Task Update(T entity);
 43:     Task Delete(T entity);
 44:     Task<bool> Exists(TKey id);
 45: }
 46: ```
 47: 
 48: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
 49: 
 50: ```csharp
 51: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/GenericRepository.cs
 52: using System;
 53: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 54: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 55: using Npgsql;
 56: 
 57: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
 58: 
 59: public class GenericRepository<T, TKey> : IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 60: {
 61:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
 62: 
 63:     public GenericRepository({DbContext} dbContext)
 64:     {
 65:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     public async Task<T> Create(T entity)
 69:     {
 70:         try
 71:         {
 72:             await _dbContext.AddAsync(entity);
 73:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 74:             return entity;
 75:         }
 76:         catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (ex.InnerException is PostgresException pgEx && pgEx.SqlState == "23505")
 77:         {
 78:             // Duplicate key violation - detach the entity and rethrow with more context
 79:             _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Detached;
 80:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 81:                 $"A record with the same unique key already exists. Constraint: {pgEx.ConstraintName}. Detail: {pgEx.Detail}",
 82:                 ex);
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     public async Task<T?> GetById(TKey id)
 87:     {
 88:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().FindAsync(id);
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll()
 92:     {
 93:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().ToListAsync();
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     public async Task Update(T entity)
 97:     {
 98:         _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Modified;
 99:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
100:     }
101: 
102:     public async Task Delete(T entity)
103:     {
104:         _dbContext.Set<T>().Remove(entity);
105:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
106:     }
107: 
108:     public async Task<bool> Exists(TKey id)
109:     {
110:         var entity = await GetById(id);
111:         return entity != null;
112:     }
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## Entity-Specific Repository
119: 
120: Inherit from GenericRepository and add custom methods.
121: 
122: ### Interface (Application Layer)
123: 
124: ```csharp
125: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
126: using {Project}.Domain;
127: 
128: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
129: 
130: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
131: {
132:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
133:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
134:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
139: 
140: ```csharp
141: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
142: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
143: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
144: using {Project}.Domain;
145: 
146: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
147: 
148: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
149: {
150:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
151: 
152:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
153:     {
154:         _dbContext = dbContext;
155:     }
156: 
157:     // ✅ REPOSITORIES RETURN ENTITIES, NOT DTOs
158:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
159:     {
160:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
161:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
162:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
163:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
164:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
165:             .Include(e => e.Status)
166:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
167:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
168:             .ToListAsync();
169:     }
170: 
171:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
172:     {
173:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
174:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
175:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
176:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
177:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
178:             .Include(e => e.Status)
179:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
180:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
181:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
182:     }
183: 
184:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
185:     {
186:         {IdType} userIdParsed;
187:         var isValid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userIdParsed);
188: 
189:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
190:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
191:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
192:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
193:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
194:             .Include(e => e.Status)
195:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
196:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
197:             .AsQueryable();
198: 
199:         if (isValid)
200:         {
201:             query = query.Where(e =>
202:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userIdParsed && u.{ParentEntity}Id == e.{ParentEntity}Id));
203:         }
204: 
205:         return await query.ToListAsync();
206:     }
207: 
208:     // NOTE: In the Application layer handler, entities are mapped to DTOs:
209:     //
210:     // public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
211:     // {
212:     //     // Repository returns ENTITIES
213:     //     var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
214:     //
215:     //     // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
216:     //     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
217:     // }
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Repository Registration (DI)
224: 
225: ```csharp
226: // File: {Project}.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs
227: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
228: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
229: using {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
230: 
231: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
232: 
233: public static class PersistenceServicesRegistration
234: {
235:     public static IServiceCollection AddPersistenceServices(
236:         this IServiceCollection services)
237:     {
238:         // Register generic repository
239:         services.AddScoped(typeof(IGenericRepository<,>), typeof(GenericRepository<,>));
240: 
241:         // Register specific repositories
242:         services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
243:         services.AddScoped<I{ParentEntity}Repository, {ParentEntity}Repository>();
244:         services.AddScoped<IUserRepository, UserRepository>();
245:         services.AddScoped<I{LinkEntity}Repository, {LinkEntity}Repository>();
246: 
247:         return services;
248:     }
249: }
250: ```
251: 
252: **Usage in Program.cs**:
253: ```csharp
254: builder.Services.AddPersistenceServices();
255: ```
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## Repository Method Patterns
260: 
261: ### Return Entities (Standard Pattern)
262: 
263: **CRITICAL**: Repositories return ENTITIES, not DTOs. DTO mapping happens in Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
264: 
265: ```csharp
266: // ✅ CORRECT: Repository returns entities
267: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
268: {
269:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
270:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
271:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
272:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
273:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
274:         .ToListAsync();
275: }
276: 
277: // ✅ CORRECT: Handler maps entities to DTOs
278: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
279: {
280:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
281:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
282: 
283:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
284:     {
285:         // Repository returns ENTITIES
286:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
287: 
288:         // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
289:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
290:     }
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: **Benefits**:
295: - ✅ Clean separation of concerns
296: - ✅ Repositories focus on data access only
297: - ✅ Handlers handle DTO mapping with AutoMapper
298: - ✅ Reusable repositories for different DTO shapes
299: 
300: ### AsNoTracking for Read-Only Queries
301: 
302: ```csharp
303: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}ReadOnly()
304: {
305:     // ✅ No change tracking (faster for read-only)
306:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
307:         .AsNoTracking()
308:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
309:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
310:         .ToListAsync();
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: ## Advanced Repository Patterns
317: 
318: ### Specification Pattern
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: // File: Application/Specifications/ISpecification.cs
322: public interface ISpecification<T>
323: {
324:     Expression<Func<T, bool>> Criteria { get; }
325:     List<Expression<Func<T, object>>> Includes { get; }
326: }
327: 
328: // File: Application/Specifications/{Entity}Specification.cs
329: public class {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec : ISpecification<{Entity}>
330: {
331:     public {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec({IdType} {parentEntity}Id)
332:     {
333:         Criteria = e => e.{ParentEntity}Id == {parentEntity}Id;
334:         Includes = new List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>>
335:         {
336:             e => e.{ParentEntity},
337:             e => e.{LookupEntity}
338:         };
339:     }
340: 
341:     public Expression<Func<{Entity}, bool>> Criteria { get; }
342:     public List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>> Includes { get; }
343: }
344: 
345: // Repository method
346: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Find(ISpecification<{Entity}> spec)
347: {
348:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.Where(spec.Criteria);
349: 
350:     query = spec.Includes
351:         .Aggregate(query, (current, include) => current.Include(include));
352: 
353:     return await query.ToListAsync();
354: }
355: ```
356: 
357: ### Pagination
358: 
359: ```csharp
360: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}Paginated(
361:     int page,
362:     int pageSize,
363:     string? searchTerm)
364: {
365:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
366:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
367:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
368:         .AsQueryable();
369: 
370:     if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchTerm))
371:     {
372:         query = query.Where(e =>
373:             e.Title.Contains(searchTerm) ||
374:             e.Description.Contains(searchTerm));
375:     }
376: 
377:     var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
378: 
379:     var items = await query
380:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
381:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
382:         .Take(pageSize)
383:         .ToListAsync();
384: 
385:     return items;
386: }
387: ```
388: 
389: ---
390: 
391: ## Best Practices
392: 
393: | Practice | Reason |
394: |----------|--------|
395: | ✅ Interface in Application, implementation in Persistence | Clean Architecture |
396: | ✅ Inherit from GenericRepository | Code reuse |
397: | ✅ Return entities, not DTOs | Separation of concerns |
398: | ✅ Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only | No unnecessary tracking |
399: | ✅ Include related entities with `Include` | Avoid N+1 queries |
400: | ✅ Register repositories in DI | Dependency injection |
401: | ✅ Use async methods (`Async` suffix) | Non-blocking I/O |
402: | ❌ Don't return IQueryable from repository | Encapsulation |
403: | ❌ Don't inject DbContext in Application layer | Breaks abstraction |
404: | ❌ Don't track entities for read-only queries | Performance overhead |
405: 
406: ---
407: 
408: **Related Resources**:
409: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
410: - [querying-patterns.md](querying-patterns.md) - Query optimization
411: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity configuration
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: dotnet-efcore-guidelines
  3: description: Entity Framework Core best practices for Clean Architecture projects. Covers DbContext, entity configurations, repository pattern, migrations, and PostgreSQL-specific features.
  4: type: domain
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # .NET + Entity Framework Core Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic EF Core Patterns**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: This skill provides comprehensive best practices for using Entity Framework Core with PostgreSQL in Clean Architecture projects. It details conventions for DbContext, entity configurations, repository patterns, migrations, and PostgreSQL-specific features.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "ef core", "entity framework", "dbcontext", "repository", "migration", "database", "postgres", "postgresql"
 23: - File patterns: `**/Persistence/**/*.cs`, `**/Repositories/**/*.cs`, `**/*DbContext.cs`, `**/Configurations/**/*.cs`
 24: 
 25: ## EF Core Architecture
 26: 
 27: The persistence layer (`{Project}.Persistence`) is responsible for data access and storage. It implements interfaces defined in the Application layer, adhering to Clean Architecture principles.
 28: 
 29: ```mermaid
 30: graph TD
 31:     subgraph Application Layer
 32:         A[I{Entity}Repository] --> B[{Entity}]
 33:         B[{Entity}] --> C[Domain Layer]
 34:     end
 35: 
 36:     subgraph Persistence Layer
 37:         D[{DbContext}] --> B
 38:         E[{Entity}Repository] --> D
 39:         E --> A
 40:     end
 41: 
 42:     A -- Implemented by --> E
 43:     C -- Used by --> B
 44:     D -- Configures --> B
 45: ```
 46: 
 47: ## Resources
 48: 
 49: *For more detailed examples, refer to the `resources/` folder within this skill.*
 50: 
 51: | Resource | Description |
 52: |----------|-------------|
 53: | [dbcontext-patterns.md](resources/dbcontext-patterns.md) | DbContext configuration, `SaveChangesAsync` override |
 54: | [entity-configuration.md](resources/entity-configuration.md) | `IEntityTypeConfiguration`, TPT, PostgreSQL functions |
 55: | [repository-pattern.md](resources/repository-pattern.md) | `GenericRepository`, custom repositories |
 56: | [querying-patterns.md](resources/querying-patterns.md) | `Include`, `Select`, projections, performance |
 57: | [migrations.md](resources/migrations.md) | Creating and applying migrations |
 58: 
 59: ## Quick Reference
 60: 
 61: ### 1. DbContext Pattern
 62: 
 63: The `{DbContext}` manages database interactions.
 64: 
 65: ```csharp
 66: // File: {Project}.Persistence/{DbContext}.cs
 67: public class {DbContext} : DbContext
 68: {
 69:     public {DbContext}(DbContextOptions<{DbContext}> options) : base(options) { }
 70: 
 71:     protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
 72:     {
 73:         base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
 74:         // Automatically applies all IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> from the assembly
 75:         modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(typeof({DbContext}).Assembly);
 76:     }
 77: 
 78:     // Override SaveChangesAsync for cross-cutting concerns like auditing or soft deletes
 79:     public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 80:     {
 81:         // Example: Audit logging or automatic timestamp updates
 82:         foreach (var entry in ChangeTracker.Entries())
 83:         {
 84:             // Handle CreatedAt, UpdatedAt logic
 85:         }
 86:         return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
 87:     }
 88: 
 89:     public DbSet<{Entity}> {Entities} { get; set; } = null!;
 90:     public DbSet<{ParentEntity}> {ParentEntities} { get; set; } = null!;
 91:     // ... other DbSets
 92: }
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: *For more details, see [dbcontext-patterns.md](resources/dbcontext-patterns.md).*
 96: 
 97: ### 2. Entity Configuration
 98: 
 99: All entity-specific configurations are done using `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` in separate classes.
100: 
101: ```csharp
102: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Configurations/Entities/{Entity}Configuration.cs
103: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
104: {
105:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
106:     {
107:         // Project Standard: Table Per Type (TPT) inheritance strategy
108:         builder.UseTptMappingStrategy();
109: 
110:         // Project Standard: UUIDv7 primary keys for main entities
111:         builder.Property(e => e.Id).HasDefaultValueSql("uuidv7()");
112: 
113:         // Database-level defaults are acceptable here, not in domain entities
114:         builder.Property(e => e.ViewCount).HasDefaultValue(0);
115: 
116:         builder.Property(e => e.Title).HasMaxLength(200).IsRequired();
117:         builder.Property(e => e.Description).HasMaxLength(5000);
118: 
119:         // Example relationship configuration
120:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
121:             .WithMany()
122:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
123:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
124:     }
125: }
126: ```
127: 
128: *For more details, see [entity-configuration.md](resources/entity-configuration.md).*
129: 
130: ### 3. Repository Pattern
131: 
132: Repositories abstract data access. Interfaces reside in the Application layer, and implementations are in the Persistence layer.
133: 
134: **CRITICAL RULE**: Repositories **MUST** return **DOMAIN ENTITIES**, not DTOs. DTO mapping always happens in the Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
135: 
136: ```csharp
137: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs (Application Layer)
138: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
139: {
140:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails(); // Returns List<{Entity}>
141:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id); // Returns {Entity}?
142: }
143: 
144: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs (Persistence Layer)
145: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
146: {
147:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
148: 
149:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext) => _dbContext = dbContext;
150: 
151:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
152:     {
153:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
154:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
155:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
156:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
157:             .ToListAsync(); // Returns entities
158:     }
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: *For more details, see [repository-pattern.md](resources/repository-pattern.md).*
163: 
164: ### 4. Querying Patterns
165: 
166: Efficient querying is crucial for performance. Avoid N+1 issues by using eager loading (`Include`) and projections (`Select`).
167: 
168: ```csharp
169: // Example: Query with eager loading and projection to DTO (in Application Layer Handler)
170: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
171: {
172:     var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails(); // Repository returns entities
173:     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities}); // Handler maps to DTOs
174: }
175: 
176: // Example: Using AsNoTracking for read-only queries (in Repository)
177: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}ReadOnly()
178: {
179:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
180:         .AsNoTracking() // Disables change tracking for performance
181:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
182:         .ToListAsync();
183: }
184: ```
185: 
186: *For more details, see [querying-patterns.md](resources/querying-patterns.md).*
187: 
188: ### 5. Migrations
189: 
190: Database schema changes are managed through EF Core migrations.
191: 
192: ```powershell
193: # Create a new migration for schema changes
194: dotnet ef migrations add AddNewFieldTo{Entity} --project {Project}.Persistence
195: 
196: # Apply pending migrations to the database
197: dotnet ef database update --project {Project}.Persistence
198: 
199: # Generate SQL script for production deployment
200: dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent --output migrations/release.sql --project {Project}.Persistence
201: ```
202: 
203: *For more details, see [migrations.md](resources/migrations.md).*
204: 
205: ## Key Principles & Conventions
206: 
207: *   **IDs**: All primary keys are `Guid` (or `{IdType}`), except for lookup tables which use `int` (or `{LookupIdType}`).
208: *   **Numeric Types**: Use `int` instead of `long` unless explicitly required for large values (e.g., file sizes, pagination cursors).
209: *   **Default Values**: **DO NOT** add default values in domain entity property initializers (e.g., `public int ViewCount { get; set; } = 0;`). Set defaults in application handlers or use database-level defaults via `IEntityTypeConfiguration`.
210: *   **Link Tables**: Navigation properties on link/mapping tables are **readonly for queries only**. Writes must go through the link table's repository directly.
211: *   **PostgreSQL Features**: Leverage PostgreSQL-specific features like `UUIDv7` for primary keys and PostGIS for spatial data handling.
212: 
213: ---
214: 
215: **Related Documentation**:
216: - [`docs/DOMAIN.md`](../../../docs/DOMAIN.md) - Conceptual domain model.
217: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture.
218: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Dependency enforcement.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/api-exception-handling.md
````markdown
  1: # Centralized API Exception Handling
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Exception Handling Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This pattern ensures that all unhandled exceptions occurring within the API are caught centrally, logged, and presented to the client in a standardized, RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` format. This avoids repetitive `try-catch` blocks in every controller action and provides a consistent error experience.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. Configuration in `Program.cs`
 12: 
 13: The primary setup for centralized exception handling in ASP.NET Core involves `UseExceptionHandler` and `AddProblemDetails` in the `Program.cs` file of the `{Project}.API` project.
 14: 
 15: **File**: `{Project}.API/Program.cs`
 16: 
 17: ```csharp
 18: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics;
 19: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
 20: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
 21: 
 22: // Add ProblemDetails services to the DI container
 23: builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
 24: 
 25: // Configure the exception handling middleware
 26: app.UseExceptionHandler(exceptionHandlerApp =>
 27: {
 28:     exceptionHandlerApp.Run(async context =>
 29:     {
 30:         // Set the HTTP status code to 500 Internal Server Error
 31:         context.Response.StatusCode = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError;
 32:         // Set the Content-Type header to indicate a ProblemDetails response
 33:         context.Response.ContentType = "application/problem+json";
 34: 
 35:         // Retrieve the IExceptionHandlerFeature, which contains the unhandled exception
 36:         var exceptionHandlerFeature = context.Features.Get<IExceptionHandlerFeature>();
 37:         // Retrieve the ProblemDetails service from the request services
 38:         var problemDetailsService = context.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<IProblemDetailsService>();
 39: 
 40:         // Log the exception (ILogger would be used here)
 41:         var logger = context.RequestServices.GetRequiredService<ILogger<Program>>();
 42:         logger.LogError(exceptionHandlerFeature?.Error, "An unhandled exception occurred during request processing.");
 43: 
 44:         // Construct and write the ProblemDetails response to the client
 45:         await problemDetailsService.WriteAsync(new ProblemDetailsContext
 46:         {
 47:             HttpContext = context,
 48:             ProblemDetails = new ProblemDetails
 49:             {
 50:                 Title = "An unexpected error occurred.",
 51:                 Detail = "Please try again later. If the problem persists, contact support.",
 52:                 Status = StatusCodes.Status500InternalServerError,
 53:                 Instance = context.Request.Path
 54:             }
 55:         });
 56:     });
 57: });
 58: ```
 59: 
 60: ---
 61: 
 62: ## 2. Benefits of Centralized Handling
 63: 
 64: *   **Consistency**: All unhandled API errors return a standard `ProblemDetails` response, making client-side error handling predictable.
 65: *   **Reduced Boilerplate**: Eliminates the need for `try-catch` blocks in every controller action, keeping controllers clean and focused on business logic.
 66: *   **Security**: Prevents sensitive exception details from being directly exposed to API consumers by default, while still allowing for internal logging.
 67: *   **Observability**: Provides a single point where all unhandled exceptions can be logged, monitored, and potentially sent to external error tracking services like Sentry.
 68: 
 69: ---
 70: 
 71: ## 3. `ProblemDetails` Format (RFC 7807)
 72: 
 73: The `ProblemDetails` object conforms to RFC 7807, providing a structured way to convey API errors.
 74: 
 75: ```json
 76: {
 77:   "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.6.1",
 78:   "title": "An unexpected error occurred.",
 79:   "status": 500,
 80:   "detail": "Please try again later. If the problem persists, contact support.",
 81:   "instance": "/api/v1/{entity}/some-failing-endpoint"
 82: }
 83: ```
 84: 
 85: ---
 86: 
 87: ## 4. Interaction with Other Error Handling
 88: 
 89: *   **Explicit Error Returns**: For business validation errors (e.g., FluentValidation failing), use `BadRequest(response)` to return a specific `BaseCommandResponse` or `ProblemDetails` with status `400 Bad Request`. These are *handled* errors and won't be caught by `UseExceptionHandler`.
 90: *   **Sentry Integration**: If Sentry is enabled, the centralized exception handler is the ideal place to capture the `exceptionHandlerFeature.Error` using `SentrySdk.CaptureException()`, ensuring all crashes are reported.
 91: 
 92: ---
 93: 
 94: ## 5. Middleware Order
 95: 
 96: The order of middleware in `Program.cs` is crucial:
 97: *   `app.UseExceptionHandler()` should typically be placed early in the pipeline to catch exceptions from subsequent middleware.
 98: *   `app.UseDeveloperExceptionPage()` (if used for development) must be placed *before* `UseExceptionHandler`.
 99: 
100: ```csharp
101: // Example middleware pipeline order
102: if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
103: {
104:     app.UseDeveloperExceptionPage();
105: }
106: else
107: {
108:     app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error");
109: }
110: 
111: app.UseHsts();
112: app.UseHttpsRedirection();
113: app.UseStaticFiles();
114: app.UseRouting();
115: 
116: // Sentry tracing middleware (if integrated) should be here
117: // app.UseSentryTracing();
118: 
119: app.UseAuthentication();
120: app.UseAuthorization();
121: 
122: app.MapControllers();
123: ```
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/blazor-error-boundary.md
````markdown
  1: # Blazor Error Boundary
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Error Boundary Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: The `ErrorBoundary` component in Blazor is a powerful tool for gracefully handling unhandled exceptions that occur during the rendering or lifecycle of its child components. Instead of crashing the entire UI, it allows you to display a fallback UI and optionally log the error.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. `ErrorBoundary` Usage
 12: 
 13: Wrap any potentially error-prone content with an `ErrorBoundary` component. It provides two `RenderFragment` properties: `ChildContent` (the content to protect) and `ErrorContent` (the UI to display if an error occurs).
 14: 
 15: **File**: `{Project}.Blazor/Components/Pages/{Entities}.razor`
 16: 
 17: ```razor
 18: @page "/{entities}"
 19: @inject ILogger<{Entities}> _logger
 20: 
 21: <MudText Typo="Typo.h4" Class="mb-4">{Entities} Overview</MudText>
 22: 
 23: @* Wrap the component that fetches and displays {entity} data *@
 24: <ErrorBoundary>
 25:     <ChildContent>
 26:         @if (_{entities} == null)
 27:         {
 28:             <MudProgressCircular Indeterminate="true" Color="Color.Primary" />
 29:             <MudText Class="ml-2">Loading {entities}...</MudText>
 30:         }
 31:         else if (_{entities}.Any())
 32:         {
 33:             <MudGrid Spacing="3">
 34:                 @foreach (var item in _{entities})
 35:                 {
 36:                     <MudItem xs="12" sm="6" md="4" lg="3">
 37:                         <{Entity}Card {Entity}="@item" />
 38:                     </MudItem>
 39:                 }
 40:             </MudGrid>
 41:         }
 42:         else
 43:         {
 44:             <MudText>No {entities} found. Try creating one!</MudText>
 45:         }
 46:     </ChildContent>
 47:     <ErrorContent Context="exception">
 48:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Error" Variant="Variant.Filled" Class="mt-4">
 49:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">An unexpected error occurred!</MudText>
 50:             <MudText>We're sorry, but we couldn't load the {entity} data right now.</MudText>
 51:             <MudText Class="mt-2">Error details: <i>@exception.Message</i></MudText>
 52:             <MudButton OnClick="@(() => _errorBoundary?.Recover())" Color="Color.Warning" Class="mt-3">
 53:                 Try Reloading
 54:             </MudButton>
 55:         </MudAlert>
 56:         @code {
 57:             // ✅ Log the exception to your logging provider (e.g., Application Insights, Sentry)
 58:             protected override void OnInitialized()
 59:             {
 60:                 _logger.LogError(exception, "An unhandled UI error occurred in {Entity}List component.");
 61:             }
 62:         }
 63:     </ErrorContent>
 64: </ErrorBoundary>
 65: 
 66: @code {
 67:     private List<{Entity}ListDto>? _{entities};
 68:     private ErrorBoundary? _errorBoundary;
 69: 
 70:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 71:     {
 72:         try
 73:         {
 74:             _{entities} = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<{Entity}ListDto>>("api/v1/{entity}");
 75:         }
 76:         catch (Exception ex)
 77:         {
 78:             // ✅ Log the exception here, but then re-throw it to let the ErrorBoundary catch it
 79:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to load {entities} in OnInitializedAsync.");
 80:             throw; // IMPORTANT: Re-throw to propagate to the ErrorBoundary
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: }
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: ---
 87: 
 88: ## 2. Global Error Handling with `ErrorBoundary`
 89: 
 90: You can place an `ErrorBoundary` at a higher level, such as in `App.razor` or `MainLayout.razor`, to catch errors from a larger portion of your application.
 91: 
 92: **File**: `{Project}.Blazor/Components/App.razor`
 93: 
 94: ```razor
 95: <ErrorBoundary @ref="_errorBoundary">
 96:     <ChildContent>
 97:         <CascadingAuthenticationState>
 98:             <Router AppAssembly="@typeof(App).Assembly">
 99:                 <Found Context="routeData">
100:                     <RouteView RouteData="@routeData" DefaultLayout="@typeof(MainLayout)" />
101:                     <FocusOnNavigate RouteData="@routeData" Selector="h1" />
102:                 </Found>
103:                 <NotFound>
104:                     <PageTitle>Not found</PageTitle>
105:                     <LayoutView Layout="@typeof(MainLayout)">
106:                         <p role="alert">Sorry, there's nothing at this address.</p>
107:                     </LayoutView>
108:                 </NotFound>
109:             </Router>
110:         </CascadingAuthenticationState>
111:     </ChildContent>
112:     <ErrorContent Context="exception">
113:         <MudContainer MaxWidth="MaxWidth.ExtraLarge" Class="mud-theme-error pa-4 ma-2 rounded-lg">
114:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h5" Class="mb-2">Application Error</MudText>
115:             <MudText Class="mb-3">
116:                 An unexpected error occurred. Please try refreshing the page or contact support.
117:             </MudText>
118:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Dark" Class="mb-4">
119:                 Error ID: @Guid.NewGuid().ToString() <br />
120:                 Message: @exception.Message
121:             </MudText>
122:             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled" Color="Color.Warning" OnClick="@(() => _errorBoundary?.Recover())">
123:                 Reload Page
124:             </MudButton>
125:         </MudContainer>
126:     </ErrorContent>
127: </ErrorBoundary>
128: 
129: @code {
130:     private ErrorBoundary? _errorBoundary;
131: }
132: ```
133: 
134: ---
135: 
136: ## 3. Best Practices for `ErrorBoundary`
137: 
138: *   **Strategic Placement**: Place `ErrorBoundary` components at logical boundaries in your UI where you want to gracefully handle failures without affecting the entire application.
139: *   **Log Errors**: Always log the `exception` caught by the `ErrorContent` to your logging provider (`ILogger`, Sentry, Application Insights) to track and resolve issues.
140: *   **User-Friendly Messages**: Provide clear, concise, and helpful messages in the `ErrorContent` to the user, instructing them on possible next steps (e.g., "try again," "contact support"). Avoid exposing raw exception details to end-users.
141: *   **Recovery Option**: Offer a "Try Again" or "Reload" button that calls `ErrorBoundary.Recover()` to reset the boundary and re-render its `ChildContent`.
142: *   **Avoid Nested `ErrorBoundary`**: Do not nest `ErrorBoundary` components too deeply, as it can make debugging more complex.
143: *   **Propagate Exceptions**: If an error occurs during data fetching (`OnInitializedAsync`, `OnParametersSetAsync`), ensure you `throw` the exception after logging it so that the `ErrorBoundary` can catch it. If you `catch` and *don't* `throw`, the `ErrorBoundary` won't activate.
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: **Related Resources**:
148: - [api-exception-handling.md](api-exception-handling.md) - How API errors are handled.
149: - [mediatr-logging-behavior.md](mediatr-logging-behavior.md) - Logging errors in MediatR pipeline.
150: - [`blazor-ui-conventions`](../../blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md) - General Blazor UI guidelines.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/db-performance-monitoring.md
````markdown
  1: # Database Performance Monitoring
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Performance Monitoring Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: Effective database performance monitoring is crucial for identifying and resolving bottlenecks in your application. This document outlines patterns for tracking database query performance, leveraging .NET's `ActivitySource` for OpenTelemetry compatibility.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. Using `ActivitySource` for Tracing
 12: 
 13: `ActivitySource` is part of `System.Diagnostics` and is the recommended way to create custom traces that can be integrated with OpenTelemetry. These traces are visible in tools like the Aspire dashboard, making it easy to visualize performance.
 14: 
 15: ### `ActivitySource` Setup
 16: 
 17: You typically define a static `ActivitySource` instance per logical component (e.g., your Persistence layer).
 18: 
 19: **File**: `{Project}.Persistence/ActivitySourceProvider.cs` (New File)
 20: 
 21: ```csharp
 22: using System.Diagnostics;
 23: 
 24: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
 25: 
 26: /// <summary>
 27: /// Provides a centralized ActivitySource for tracing operations within the Persistence layer.
 28: /// This enables custom spans for database interactions to be captured by OpenTelemetry.
 29: /// </summary>
 30: public static class ActivitySourceProvider
 31: {
 32:     // Define an ActivitySource instance for the Persistence layer.
 33:     // The name should be unique and descriptive.
