## File: Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs
````csharp
  1: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication;
  2: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.Circuits;
  3: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
  4: using System.Collections.Concurrent;
  5: using System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt;
  6: 
  7: namespace Explore.Blazor.Services;
  8: 
  9: public interface ICircuitAccessTokenService
 10: {
 11:     string? AccessToken { get; }
 12:     void SetToken(string? token);
 13: }
 14: 
 15: 
 16: 
 17: 
 18: 
 19: 
 20: public class CircuitAccessTokenService : ICircuitAccessTokenService
 21: {
 22: 
 23: 
 24:     private static readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, TokenEntry> _tokenStore = new();
 25: 
 26: 
 27:     private static TokenEntry? _latestToken;
 28:     private static readonly object _latestTokenLock = new();
 29: 
 30:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 31:     private readonly ILogger<CircuitAccessTokenService>? _logger;
 32:     private string? _localToken;
 33:     private string? _userId;
 34: 
 35:     public CircuitAccessTokenService(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, ILogger<CircuitAccessTokenService>? logger = null)
 36:     {
 37:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 38:         _logger = logger;
 39:     }
 40: 
 41:     public string? AccessToken => _localToken ?? GetStoredToken();
 42: 
 43:     public void SetToken(string? token)
 44:     {
 45:         _localToken = token;
 46: 
 47:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
 48:         {
 49:             _logger?.LogWarning("[CircuitAccessTokenService] SetToken called with null/empty token");
 50:             return;
 51:         }
 52: 
 53: 
 54:         var userId = ExtractUserIdFromToken(token) ?? GetUserIdFromHttpContext();
 55: 
 56:         _logger?.LogInformation("[CircuitAccessTokenService] SetToken called. Token length: {TokenLen}, UserId: {UserId}",
 57:             token.Length, userId ?? "(null)");
 58: 
 59: 
 60:         lock (_latestTokenLock)
 61:         {
 62:             _latestToken = new TokenEntry(token, DateTime.UtcNow);
 63:         }
 64:         Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] Stored as latest token (length: {token.Length})");
 65: 
 66:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 67:         {
 68:             _userId = userId;
 69:             _tokenStore[userId] = new TokenEntry(token, DateTime.UtcNow);
 70:             _logger?.LogInformation("[CircuitAccessTokenService] ✓ Token stored in static store for userId: {UserId}. Total tokens in store: {Count}",
 71:                 userId, _tokenStore.Count);
 72:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] ✓ Token stored for userId: {userId}. Store has {_tokenStore.Count} entries");
 73:             CleanupOldTokens();
 74:         }
 75:         else
 76:         {
 77:             _logger?.LogWarning("[CircuitAccessTokenService] Could not extract userId from token - stored as latest only");
 78:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] ✗ Could not extract userId - stored as latest only");
 79:         }
 80:     }
 81: 
 82: 
 83: 
 84: 
 85: 
 86:     private static string? ExtractUserIdFromToken(string token)
 87:     {
 88:         try
 89:         {
 90:             var handler = new JwtSecurityTokenHandler();
 91:             if (handler.CanReadToken(token))
 92:             {
 93:                 var jwtToken = handler.ReadJwtToken(token);
 94:                 var sub = jwtToken.Claims.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Type == "sub")?.Value;
 95:                 Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] Extracted userId from JWT: {sub ?? "(null)"}");
 96:                 return sub;
 97:             }
 98:         }
 99:         catch (Exception ex)
100:         {
101:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] Failed to parse JWT: {ex.Message}");
102:         }
103:         return null;
104:     }
105: 
106:     private string? GetUserIdFromHttpContext()
107:     {
108:         var user = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User;
109:         var userId = user?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
110:             ?? user?.FindFirst(System.Security.Claims.ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value;
111:         Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService] GetUserIdFromHttpContext: {userId ?? "(null)"}");
112:         return userId;
113:     }
114: 
115:     private string? GetStoredToken()
116:     {
117:         var userId = _userId ?? GetUserIdFromHttpContext();
118:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId) && _tokenStore.TryGetValue(userId, out var entry))
119:         {
120: 
121:             if (entry.CreatedAt > DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(-1))
122:             {
123:                 return entry.Token;
124:             }
125:         }
126:         return null;
127:     }
128: 
129: 
130: 
131: 
132: 
133:     public static string? GetAnyValidToken()
134:     {
135:         var cutoff = DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(-1);
136:         var validEntries = _tokenStore.Values.Where(e => e.CreatedAt > cutoff).ToList();
137:         Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetAnyValidToken] Total store entries: {_tokenStore.Count}, Valid entries: {validEntries.Count}");
138: 
139:         var entry = validEntries.FirstOrDefault();
140:         if (entry != null)
141:         {
142:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetAnyValidToken] Found valid token from store (length: {entry.Token.Length})");
143:             return entry.Token;
144:         }
145: 
146: 
147:         lock (_latestTokenLock)
148:         {
149:             if (_latestToken != null && _latestToken.CreatedAt > cutoff)
150:             {
151:                 Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetAnyValidToken] Found valid latest token (length: {_latestToken.Token.Length})");
152:                 return _latestToken.Token;
153:             }
154:         }
155: 
156:         Console.WriteLine("[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetAnyValidToken] No valid tokens found anywhere");
157:         return null;
158:     }
159: 
160: 
161: 
162: 
163:     public static string? GetTokenForUser(string userId)
164:     {
165:         Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetTokenForUser] Looking for userId: {userId}, Store has {_tokenStore.Count} entries, Keys: [{string.Join(", ", _tokenStore.Keys)}]");
166:         if (_tokenStore.TryGetValue(userId, out var entry))
167:         {
168:             if (entry.CreatedAt > DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(-1))
169:             {
170:                 Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetTokenForUser] Found valid token for {userId} (length: {entry.Token.Length})");
171:                 return entry.Token;
172:             }
173:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetTokenForUser] Token for {userId} is expired");
174:         }
175:         else
176:         {
177:             Console.WriteLine($"[CircuitAccessTokenService.GetTokenForUser] No entry found for userId: {userId}");
178:         }
179:         return null;
180:     }
181: 
182:     private static void CleanupOldTokens()
183:     {
184:         var cutoff = DateTime.UtcNow.AddHours(-2);
185:         var oldKeys = _tokenStore.Where(kvp => kvp.Value.CreatedAt < cutoff).Select(kvp => kvp.Key).ToList();
186:         foreach (var key in oldKeys)
187:         {
188:             _tokenStore.TryRemove(key, out _);
189:         }
190:     }
191: 
192:     private record TokenEntry(string Token, DateTime CreatedAt);
193: }
194: 
195: 
196: 
197: 
198: 
199: public class AccessTokenForwardingHandler : DelegatingHandler
200: {
201:     private const string TenantIdHeaderName = "X-Tenant-Id";
202: 
203: 
204: 
205: 
206: 
207: 
208:     private static readonly Guid DefaultTenantId = Guid.Parse("018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001");
209: 
210:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
211:     private readonly ILogger<AccessTokenForwardingHandler> _logger;
212: 
213:     public AccessTokenForwardingHandler(
214:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
215:         ILogger<AccessTokenForwardingHandler> logger)
216:     {
217:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
218:         _logger = logger;
219:     }
220: 
221:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(
222:         HttpRequestMessage request,
223:         CancellationToken cancellationToken)
224:     {
225:         _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Processing request to {Path}", request.RequestUri?.PathAndQuery);
226: 
227:         string? token = null;
228:         string source = "none";
229: 
230: 
231:         var httpContext = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
232:         var isAuthenticated = httpContext?.User?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true;
233:         _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] HttpContext available: {HasContext}, User authenticated: {IsAuth}",
234:             httpContext != null, isAuthenticated);
235: 
236:         if (isAuthenticated)
237:         {
238:             try
239:             {
240:                 token = await httpContext!.GetTokenAsync("access_token");
241:                 if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
242:                 {
243:                     source = "HttpContext";
244:                     _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Got token from HttpContext (length: {Len})", token.Length);
245: 
246: 
247:                     try
248:                     {
249:                         var handler = new System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt.JwtSecurityTokenHandler();
250:                         if (handler.CanReadToken(token))
251:                         {
252:                             var jwt = handler.ReadJwtToken(token);
253:                             var aud = jwt.Audiences?.ToList() ?? new List<string>();
254:                             var azp = jwt.Claims.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Type == "azp")?.Value;
255:                             var iss = jwt.Issuer;
256:                             var exp = jwt.ValidTo;
257:                             var sub = jwt.Claims.FirstOrDefault(c => c.Type == "sub")?.Value;
258: 
259:                             _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Token details - Issuer: {Issuer}, Audiences: [{Audiences}], Azp: {Azp}, Sub: {Sub}, Expires: {Exp}",
260:                                 iss, string.Join(", ", aud), azp ?? "(null)", sub ?? "(null)", exp);
261:                         }
262:                         else
263:                         {
264:                             _logger.LogWarning("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Token is NOT a valid JWT! First 50 chars: {Preview}",
265:                                 token.Length > 50 ? token.Substring(0, 50) + "..." : token);
266:                         }
267:                     }
268:                     catch (Exception ex)
269:                     {
270:                         _logger.LogWarning("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Could not parse token: {Error}", ex.Message);
271:                     }
272:                 }
273:                 else
274:                 {
275:                     _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] HttpContext.GetTokenAsync returned null/empty");
276:                 }
277:             }
278:             catch (Exception ex)
279:             {
280:                 _logger.LogWarning(ex, "[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Could not get token from HttpContext: {Message}", ex.Message);
281:             }
282:         }
283: 
284: 
285:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
286:         {
287:             var userId = httpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
288:                 ?? httpContext?.User?.FindFirst(System.Security.Claims.ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value;
289: 
290:             _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Strategy 2: UserId from claims = {UserId}", userId ?? "(null)");
291: 
292:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
293:             {
294:                 token = CircuitAccessTokenService.GetTokenForUser(userId);
295:                 if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
296:                 {
297:                     source = "StaticStore(userId)";
298:                     _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Got token from static store by userId (length: {Len})", token.Length);
299:                 }
300:                 else
301:                 {
302:                     _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] No token in static store for userId: {UserId}", userId);
303:                 }
304:             }
305:         }
306: 
307: 
308:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
309:         {
310:             token = CircuitAccessTokenService.GetAnyValidToken();
311:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
312:             {
313:                 source = "StaticStore(any)";
314:                 _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Got token from static store (any valid token, length: {Len})", token.Length);
315:             }
316:             else
317:             {
318:                 _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] No valid tokens in static store at all");
319:             }
320:         }
321: 
322: 
323:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(token) && !request.Headers.Contains("Authorization"))
324:         {
325:             request.Headers.Authorization = new System.Net.Http.Headers.AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", token);
326:             _logger.LogInformation("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] ✓ Added Bearer token from {Source} to {Path}", source, request.RequestUri?.PathAndQuery);
327:         }
328:         else if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(token))
329:         {
330:             _logger.LogWarning("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] ✗ NO TOKEN AVAILABLE for {Path} - request will likely fail with 401", request.RequestUri?.PathAndQuery);
331:         }
332: 
333: 
334: 
335:         if (!request.Headers.Contains(TenantIdHeaderName))
336:         {
337:             request.Headers.Add(TenantIdHeaderName, DefaultTenantId.ToString());
338:             _logger.LogDebug("[AccessTokenForwardingHandler] Added {Header}: {TenantId} to {Path}",
339:                 TenantIdHeaderName, DefaultTenantId, request.RequestUri?.PathAndQuery);
340:         }
341: 
342:         return await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
343:     }
344: }

  1: using System.Text.Json;
  2: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
  3: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
  4: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
  5: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
  6: using Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks;
  7: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  8: using Microsoft.Extensions.ServiceDiscovery;
  9: using OpenTelemetry;
 10: using OpenTelemetry.Metrics;
 11: using OpenTelemetry.Trace;
 12: 
 13: namespace Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
 14: 
 15: 
 16: 
 17: 
 18: public static class Extensions
 19: {
 20:     private const string HealthEndpointPath = "/health";
 21:     private const string AlivenessEndpointPath = "/alive";
 22: 
 23:     public static TBuilder AddServiceDefaults<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 24:     {
 25:         builder.ConfigureOpenTelemetry();
 26: 
 27:         builder.AddDefaultHealthChecks();
 28: 
 29:         builder.Services.AddServiceDiscovery();
 30: 
 31:         builder.Services.ConfigureHttpClientDefaults(http =>
 32:         {
 33: 
 34:             http.AddStandardResilienceHandler();
 35: 
 36: 
 37:             http.AddServiceDiscovery();
 38:         });
 39: 
 40: 
 41: 
 42: 
 43: 
 44: 
 45: 
 46:         return builder;
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     public static TBuilder ConfigureOpenTelemetry<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 50:     {
 51:         builder.Logging.AddOpenTelemetry(logging =>
 52:         {
 53:             logging.IncludeFormattedMessage = true;
 54:             logging.IncludeScopes = true;
 55:         });
 56: 
 57:         builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
 58:             .WithMetrics(metrics =>
 59:             {
 60:                 metrics.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
 61:                     .AddHttpClientInstrumentation()
 62:                     .AddRuntimeInstrumentation();
 63:             })
 64:             .WithTracing(tracing =>
 65:             {
 66:                 tracing.AddSource(builder.Environment.ApplicationName)
 67:                     .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation(tracing =>
 68: 
 69:                         tracing.Filter = context =>
 70:                             !context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments(HealthEndpointPath)
 71:                             && !context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments(AlivenessEndpointPath)
 72:                     )
 73: 
 74: 
 75:                     .AddHttpClientInstrumentation();
 76:             });
 77: 
 78:         builder.AddOpenTelemetryExporters();
 79: 
 80:         return builder;
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     private static TBuilder AddOpenTelemetryExporters<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
 84:     {
 85:         var useOtlpExporter = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(builder.Configuration["OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT"]);
 86: 
 87:         if (useOtlpExporter)
 88:         {
 89:             builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().UseOtlpExporter();
 90:         }
 91: 
 92: 
 93: 
 94: 
 95: 
 96: 
 97: 
 98: 
 99:         return builder;
100:     }
101: 
102:     public static TBuilder AddDefaultHealthChecks<TBuilder>(this TBuilder builder) where TBuilder : IHostApplicationBuilder
103:     {
104:         builder.Services.AddHealthChecks()
105: 
106:             .AddCheck("self", () => HealthCheckResult.Healthy(), ["live"]);
107: 
108:         return builder;
109:     }
110: 
111:     public static WebApplication MapDefaultEndpoints(this WebApplication app)
112:     {
113: 
114: 
115: 
116: 
117:         var healthCheckOptions = new HealthCheckOptions
118:         {
119:             ResponseWriter = WriteHealthCheckResponse,
120:             ResultStatusCodes =
121:             {
122:                 [HealthStatus.Healthy] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
123:                 [HealthStatus.Degraded] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
124:                 [HealthStatus.Unhealthy] = StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable
125:             }
126:         };
127: 
128: 
129:         app.MapHealthChecks(HealthEndpointPath, healthCheckOptions);
130: 
131: 
132:         app.MapHealthChecks(AlivenessEndpointPath, new HealthCheckOptions
133:         {
134:             Predicate = r => r.Tags.Contains("live"),
135:             ResponseWriter = WriteHealthCheckResponse,
136:             ResultStatusCodes =
137:             {
138:                 [HealthStatus.Healthy] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
139:                 [HealthStatus.Degraded] = StatusCodes.Status200OK,
140:                 [HealthStatus.Unhealthy] = StatusCodes.Status503ServiceUnavailable
141:             }
142:         });
143: 
144:         return app;
145:     }
146: 
147:     private static async Task WriteHealthCheckResponse(HttpContext context, HealthReport report)
148:     {
149: 
150:         context.Response.ContentType = "application/json; charset=utf-8";
151:         context.Response.Headers["Connection"] = "close";
152:         context.Response.Headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = "*";
153:         context.Response.Headers["X-Health-Status"] = report.Status.ToString();
154:         context.Response.Headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate";
155:         context.Response.Headers["Pragma"] = "no-cache";
156: 
157:         var response = new
158:         {
159:             status = report.Status.ToString(),
160:             message = report.Status switch
161:             {
162:                 HealthStatus.Healthy => "Ok",
163:                 HealthStatus.Degraded => "Degraded",
164:                 HealthStatus.Unhealthy => "Service Unavailable",
165:                 _ => "Unknown"
166:             },
167:             totalDuration = report.TotalDuration.TotalMilliseconds,
168:             checks = report.Entries.Select(e => new
169:             {
170:                 name = e.Key,
171:                 status = e.Value.Status.ToString(),
172:                 description = e.Value.Description,
173:                 duration = e.Value.Duration.TotalMilliseconds,
174:                 error = e.Value.Exception?.Message,
175:                 data = e.Value.Data.Count > 0 ? e.Value.Data : null
176:             })
177:         };
178: 
179:         var jsonOptions = new JsonSerializerOptions
180:         {
181:             WriteIndented = true,
182:             PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase,
183:             DefaultIgnoreCondition = System.Text.Json.Serialization.JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull
184:         };
185: 
186:         await context.Response.WriteAsync(JsonSerializer.Serialize(response, jsonOptions));
187:     }
188: }
````

## File: CLAUDE.md
````markdown
  1: # CLAUDE.md — ISLAMU Event Project Reference
  2: 
  3: > **Source of Truth for AI Agents and Team Collaboration**
  4: >
  5: > This document provides comprehensive context for working with the ISLAMU Event codebase.
  6: > This file is the entrypoint. Detailed docs are imported from `docs/`.
  7: > Last Updated: January 2026
  8: 
  9: You are an experienced, pragmatic software engineer. You don’t over-engineer a solution when a simple one works.
 10: 
 11: 
 12: ## Documentation Template System
 13: 
 14: This project uses **project-agnostic documentation** with placeholder syntax `{Placeholder}`.
 15: **Template Glossary**: [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md) - Defines all placeholders
 16: 
 17: 
 18: **Documentation Coverage**:
 19: - ✅ Core Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md, API.md, BLAZOR.md, GOVERNANCE.md, QUICK_REFERENCE.md
 20: - ✅ Operations: CONTRIBUTING.md, OPERATIONS.md, CONFIGURATION.md, TROUBLESHOOTING.md
 21: - ✅ Domain Reference: DOMAIN.md (project-specific with generic patterns)
 22: - ✅ Skills: blazor-bff-patterns (SKILL.md + 4 resources), and 7 other skills
 23: - ✅ All use "Generic Template + Concrete Example" pattern
 24: 
 25: ## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - Quick Reference
 26: 
 27: **MUST READ**: Never violate them.
 28: 
 29: 
 30: > ⚠️ **Rule #1:** Never assume an exception. Get explicit permission from me before breaking or bending any rule.
 31: 
 32: - Only write inside this repo project folder, never in users folder (not in C:\Users\*\.claude\ or anywhere outside this project folder)
 33: - When getting build errors, stop building! Get the errors, fix them, skip building until fixed. Limited retry attempts, then fix without building until confident.
 34: - NEVER run rm -rf commands or delete files/folders unless explicitly instructed - instead report files that should be deleted
 35: - Never read .mcp.json file
 36: 
 37: **Some Technical API Rules**:
 38: 1. **Repositories Return ENTITIES, Never DTOs** - Map to DTOs in handlers
 39: 2. **Validators Use Manual Instantiation (NOT DI)** - `var validator = new CreateEventDtoValidator(_repo1, _repo2);`
 40: 3. **Navigation Properties Are Readonly** - Use repository for writes: `_memberRepository.Create(member)`
 41: 4. **Use int Instead of long** - Except size/cursor fields or absolutely necessary
 42: 5. **No Default Values in Domain Entities** - Set in handler: `@event.TotalViews = 0;`
 43: 6. **Commands Return BaseCommandResponse<Guid>** - Not just `Guid`
 44: 7. **GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize, Admin = Roles** - Public read, protected write, role-based for admin operations
 45: 8. **Extract UserId with Fallback** - `sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`
 46: 9. **File-Scoped Namespaces** - `namespace Explore.Application.Features.Events;`
 47: 10. **Entities Include Auditing Fields** - CreatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedAt, UpdatedBy, IsDeleted (soft delete)
 48: 11. **Use Named Query Filters for Soft Delete** - EF Core 10+ `.HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", predicate: e => !e.IsDeleted)`
 49: **Full Details**: [@docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md](docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md)
 50: 
 51: ---
 52: 
 53: ## 🧱 Foundational Rules
 54: 
 55: - Doing it right is better than doing it fast. You are not in a rush.
 56: - Never skip steps or take shortcuts.
 57: - Tedious, systematic work is often the correct solution. Don't abandon an approach because it's repetitive—only if it's wrong.
 58: - **One question at a time** - When gathering requirements or clarifying design, ask questions individually. Wait for each answer before proceeding to the next question.
 59: - Honesty is a core value. If you're not fully truthful, our collaboration can't continue.
 60: 
 61: ---
 62: 
 63: ## 🤝 Our Relationship
 64: 
 65: - We are colleagues — equals working toward the same goal.
 66: - Speak up immediately when you don’t know something or are over your head.
 67: - Call out bad ideas, mistakes, or unreasonable expectations. I highly depends on this.
 68: - Never agree just to be nice. Honest disagreement is better than fake consensus.
 69: - If you disagree, cite technical reasons. If it’s intuition, say so.
 70: - You have unreliable memory. Use your **journal** to record important facts, insights, and preferences before you forget.
 71: - Search your journal before repeating research or reasoning.
 72: - Discuss all **Important decisions** (refactors...) before implementation **or** before finalizing requirements that assume a particular approach.
 73: - When something is identified as "a major decision" elevate its priority immediately.
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ## 🔧 Starting Work (Critical First Steps)
 78: 
 79: **Before starting ANY task, always run tests:**
 80: 
 81: 1. **Check test status**: `dotnet test` (or equivalent)
 82: 2. **If tests are failing:**
 83:    - **STOP your planned work**
 84:    - Fix the failing tests FIRST
 85:    - Document what was broken and how you fixed it
 86:    - Then resume your planned work
 87: 3. **If tests are passing:**
 88:    - Proceed with your work
 89:    - Run tests frequently during development
 90: 
 91: **Why this matters:**
 92: - Broken tests indicate the codebase is in an unknown state
 93: - Your changes built on broken tests compound the problem
 94: - It's unclear if YOUR changes break things or if they were already broken
 95: - Fixing tests first establishes a known-good baseline
 96: 
 97: **Example workflow:**
 98: ```bash
 99: # Start of session
100: dotnet test
101: # ❌ 3 tests failing
102: 
103: # DO NOT proceed with work yet
104: # Fix the 3 failing tests
105: 
106: # Now tests pass - safe to proceed
107: dotnet test
108: # ✅ All tests passing
109: 
110: # Now continue on your work
111: ```
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 🚀 Proactiveness
116: 
117: When assigned a task, **do it completely**, including obvious follow-ups. However, distinguish between:
118: 
119: **Implementation tasks** (be proactive):
120: - "Fix this bug"
121: - "Add this feature"
122: - "Write tests for X"
123: - "Refactor this code"
124: 
125: **Design/planning tasks** (be systematic, not proactive):
126: - "Let's discuss architecture"
127: - "Help me design X"
128: - "What are the requirements for Y?"
129: - "Let's talk about..."
130: 
131: For design/planning: Pause and ask questions one at a time. Don't create implementations, templates, or code until explicitly requested or requirements are finalized.
132: 
133: Follow the prd skill at .claude/skills/prd/SKILL.md when planning
134: 
135: Pause to ask for confirmation when:
136: - Multiple valid approaches exist and the choice matters.
137: - The action deletes or restructures existing code.
138: - You genuinely don't understand the task.
139: - explicitly asked "how should I approach X?" — answer the question, don't start coding.
140: - You're in **requirements gathering mode** - always wait for explicit direction.
141: 
142: Act autonomously for clear, low-risk tasks. Stop and ask when changes affect architecture, data integrity, or long-term behavior.
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## 📝 Requirements Gathering
147: 
148: When designing new features or systems:
149: 
150: - **One question at a time** - Never batch multiple questions. Wait for answer before proceeding.
151: - **Document as you go** - Capture decisions in real-time in a dedicated requirements document.
152: - **Don't get ahead of yourself** - Resist the urge to implement or create templates before requirements are complete.
153: - **Systematic over ad-hoc** - Work through structured questionnaires methodically.
154: - **I may enhance your options** - Be open to improving or adding to the options you propose.
155: - **Requirements before implementation** - Complete and review all requirements before any coding begins.
156: 
157: ---
158: 
159: ## 🧩 Designing Software
160: 
161: - **YAGNI** – "You Ain't Gonna Need It." The best code is no code.
162: - When possible, architect for **extensibility and flexibility**, but never preemptively.
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## ✅ Test-Driven Development (TDD)
167: 
168: For every new feature or bugfix:
169: 
170: 1. Write a failing test validating the desired behavior.  
171: 2. Run it to confirm failure.  
172: 3. Write *only* enough code to make the test pass.  
173: 4. Run tests to confirm success.  
174: 5. Refactor if needed while keeping tests green.
175: 
176: You may skip TDD only with given explicit permission.
177: 
178: ---
179: 
180: ## 💻 Writing Code
181: 
182: - Verify you have followed **all rules** before submitting work.
183: - Make the **smallest reasonable changes** to achieve the desired result.
184: - Prefer simple, clean, maintainable code over clever or complex solutions.
185: - **Eliminate duplication aggressively:**
186:   - Never copy-paste code - extract and import instead
187:   - If the same logic appears twice, prepare to extract on third usage
188:   - Before creating a new file with similar purpose, refactor the existing file
189:   - Search codebase thoroughly before implementing functionality that might already exist
190: - Never throw away or rewrite code without permission (except trivial cleanup or bugfixes).
191: - Get approval before implementing **backward compatibility**.
192: - Match the surrounding code style. Local consistency beats external style guides.
193: - Don't manually adjust whitespace unless necessary; use a formatter instead: `dotnet format`.
194: - Fix broken things immediately when you find them.
195: 
196: **Error handling:** Code must fail fast, log clearly, and handle expected errors gracefully.
197: 
198: ---
199: 
200: ## 🗂️ File Management & Organization
201: 
202: ### Before Creating a New File
203: 
204: **STOP and ask these questions:**
205: 
206: 1. **Does a similar file already exist?**
207:    - Search the codebase thoroughly: `grep -r "class ClassName"`, `find . -name "*keyword*"`
208:    - If similar file exists, **extend it** rather than duplicate
209: 
210: 2. **Will this create duplication?**
211:    - If implementing similar functionality to an existing file, **refactor the existing file** instead
212:    - Never create `FileV2.cs`, `FileEnhanced.cs`, `FileNew.cs` - these indicate you should be editing the original
213:    - Bad: Creating both `WordPressClient.cs` and `WordPressEnhanced.cs`
214:    - Good: Enhancing the existing `WordPressClient.cs`
215: 
216: 3. **Is this a test file?**
217:    - **Ad-hoc test scripts → NO**: Put in proper test project
218:    - **Integration/manual tests → MAYBE**: Only if truly cannot be automated
219:    - **Never** create scripts for unit tests
220: 
221: 4. **Is this a backup or temporary file?**
222:    - Use git branches and history, not backup files
223:    - Add patterns to `.gitignore` immediately
224: 
225: ### When Replacing/Deprecating Files
226: 
227: If creating a replacement file (e.g., `new-cli.cs` replacing `old-script.cs`):
228: 
229: 1. **Delete the old file in the same PR** - Don't leave both
230: 2. **Update all imports** that referenced the old file
231: 4. **Update documentation** to reference only the new file
232: 5. **Add migration notes** to git commit message
233: 
234: ### Duplication Detection Checklist
235: 
236: Before submitting code, check for these duplication patterns:
237: 
238: - [ ] **Complete file duplication** - Same class name in two files
239: - [ ] **Logic duplication** - Same algorithm copied between files (>20 lines)
240: - [ ] **Constant duplication** - Same constants defined in multiple files
241: 
242: **Rule of Three**: If the same code appears **3 times**, extract it to a shared utility following asp.net core conventions and clean architecture and this repo' convention. If it appears **twice** and you're adding a third, extract **before** adding.
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## 📦 Shared Logic & Abstraction
247: 
248: ### Mandatory Extraction Scenarios
249: 
250: Extract shared logic when:
251: 
252: 1. **Same logic in 2+ files AND you're adding a 3rd usage**
253:    - Extract **before** adding the third copy
254:    - Example: `chunkArray` used in 3 places
255: 
256: 2. **Same class structure in 2+ files** (>100 lines shared)
257:    - Create abstract base class with shared logic
258:    - Example: LocalWhisper + MLXWhisper both traverse directories identically
259: 
260: 3. **Same algorithm repeated** (>20 lines)
261:    - Extract to shared function
262:    - Example: Retry logic, error handling patterns
263: 
264: 4. **Same constants/config in 2+ files**
265:    - Extract to shared file
266:    - Example: `FILE_STATUS` constants, supported file extensions
267: 
268: ### Abstraction Guidelines
269: 
270: - **Base classes** for shared **implementation** (template method pattern)
271: - **Interfaces** for shared **contracts** (dependency inversion)
272: - **Utility functions** for shared **algorithms** (pure functions)
273: - **Never** copy-paste similar code - refactor to share instead
274: 
275: ### Red Flags - Stop and Refactor
276: 
277: If you're writing code and notice:
278: 
279: - ⚠️  "This is similar to what `FileX.cs` does..."
280: - ⚠️  "I'll just copy this logic from here..."
281: - ⚠️  "There's probably already a function for this..."
282: - ⚠️  "This feels like I've written it before..."
283: 
284: **STOP** - Search the codebase first, then extract shared logic.
285: 
286: ---
287: 
288: ## 🧠 Naming
289: 
290: - Names must express **what** code does, not **how** it works or its history.
291: - Don’t reference implementation details unless essential to meaning.
292: - Avoid temporal or comparative names (“NewController”, “LegacyHandler”, “EnhancedService”).
293: - Avoid pattern names unless they improve clarity.
294: 
295: ---
296: 
297: ## 💬 Code Comments
298: 
299: Comments explain **what** or **why**, never **how it changed** or **what used to be**.
300: 
301: - Don’t reference prior implementations (“refactored from…”, “used x instead of…”).
302: - Don’t add meta-comments like “improved”, “better”, “new”, or “enhanced.”
303: - Don’t leave instructional comments (“use this pattern”).
304: - Remove outdated comments only when they describe behavior that no longer exists.
305: - Don’t add temporal context (“recently refactored”, “moved”, “new”).
306: - All files must start with a **two-line summary** beginning with `ABOUTME:` describing what the file does.
307: 
308: **Examples:**
309: ```csharp
310: // BAD: This uses FluentValidator for validation instead of manual checking
311: // BAD: Refactored from old validation system
312: // GOOD: Executes tools with validated arguments
313: ```
314: 
315: If you find yourself writing “new”, “old”, “legacy”, “wrapper”, “unified”, or “enhanced”, stop and find a better description.
316: 
317: ---
318: 
319: ## 🧰 Version Control
320: 
321: - Ask how to handle uncommitted or untracked files before starting work.
322: - If no branch exists for your task, create a **WIP** branch.
323: - Track all non-trivial changes in git.
324: - Commit frequently and atomically, with meaningful messages describing intent.
325: - Never skip or disable pre-commit hooks.
326: - Never use `git add -A` without first running `git status`.
327: - **Never commit backup or temporary files:**
328:   - Use `.gitignore` to prevent accidental commits
329:   - If you see these in git, delete them immediately
330: - **Clean up deprecated code in the same commit:**
331:   - When adding a replacement file, delete the old one in the same PR
332:   - Update all references to point to new implementation
333:   - Remove old exports from barrel files
334: - Commit your **journal** entries too.
335: 
336: ---
337: 
338: ## 🧪 Testing
339: 
340: ### Testing Standards
341: 
342: **CRITICAL RULE: Never commit or push with broken tests**
343: 
344: - **All test failures are YOUR responsibility**, even if you didn't cause them
345: - If tests are broken when you start work, fix them FIRST before proceeding
346: - If you break tests during your work, fix them IMMEDIATELY
347: - If tests break during your work for unrelated reasons, fix them before committing
348: - **Never** commit with the intention of "fixing tests in the next commit"
349: - **Never** push broken tests to any branch (including WIP branches)
350: 
351: **Test Quality Standards:**
352: 
353: - Never delete failing tests — raise the issue with me.
354: - Tests must cover all functionality comprehensively.
355: - Never test mocked behavior; test real logic.
356: - Never mock in end-to-end tests — use real APIs and data.
357: - Never ignore logs or output — they often reveal the issue.
358: - Test output must be **pristine** (no unexpected warnings or stack traces).
359: - Intermittent failures count as full failures until proven otherwise.
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 📋 Issue Tracking
364: 
365: ### GitHub Issues for Work Items
366: 
367: **Use GitHub Issues for all significant work:**
368: 
369: - Create issues for features, bugs, refactors, and technical debt
370: - **Break down to smallest complete unit of work** - each issue should be:
371:   - Completable in a single PR
372:   - Independently testable
373:   - Deployable without dependencies (when possible)
374:   - Estimated at 4 hours or less of work
375: - If a task is larger than 4 hours, break it into multiple issues
376: - Link related issues together (e.g., "Part 1 of 3: Delete duplicate files")
377: 
378: **Good issue breakdown:**
379: - ✅ "Delete duplicate client implementation"
380: - ✅ "Update imports after client deletion"
381: - ✅ "Remove client from barrel exports" (15 min)
382: 
383: **Bad issue breakdown:**
384: - ❌ "Fix all architectural issues" (too large, not specific)
385: - ❌ "Refactor transcribers and fix tests and update docs" (multiple units of work)
386: 
387: 
388: ## 🔍 Systematic Debugging Process
389: 
390: Always find the **root cause** — never patch symptoms or add workarounds.
391: 
392: ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
393: - Read error messages carefully.
394: - Reproduce consistently.
395: - Check recent changes (`git diff`, commits).
396: 
397: ### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis
398: - Find similar working examples.
399: - Compare against reference code.
400: - Identify differences.
401: - Understand dependencies.
402: 
403: ### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing
404: 1. Form one hypothesis at a time.  
405: 2. Make the smallest possible change to test it.  
406: 3. Verify results before continuing.  
407: 4. If you don’t know, say “I don’t understand X.”
408: 
409: ### Phase 4: Implementation
410: - Always have a minimal failing test case.  
411: - Never add multiple fixes at once.  
412: - Never claim to follow a pattern without reading it fully.  
413: - Test after every change.  
414: - If the first fix fails, re-analyze instead of stacking patches.
415: 
416: ---
417: 
418: ## 🧾 Learning and Memory Management
419: 
420: Use your journal (`dev/active/journal.md`) to capture insights, failures, and patterns.
421: 
422: **For major architectural decisions or requirements**, create dedicated documents:
423: - `docs/REQUIREMENTS_DECISIONS.md` - Structured Q&A format for feature design
424: - `docs/ARCHITECTURAL_DECISIONS.md` - Major system design choices
425: - `docs/journal.md` - General insights, patterns, failures
426: 
427: **Journal format** (`dev/active/journal.md`):
428: 
429: ```md
430: ## Technical Insights
431: - [Date] Learned how to optimize Zapier webhook retries for Xero sync.
432: 
433: ## Failed Approaches
434: - [Date] Tried parsing PDFs with Regex—too brittle, switched to x solution.
435: 
436: ## Architectural Decisions
437: - [Date] Chose x structure for y due to compliance flexibility.
438: 
439: ## User Feedback Patterns
440: - [Date] customers confused by variant naming—need clearer labels.
441: 
442: ## Deferred Fixes
443: - [Date] sync bug with atproto login—log for future fix.
444: ```
445: 
446: - Each entry must be timestamped and formatted as above.
447: - Review your journal weekly.
448: - Search it before starting complex tasks.
449: - Document architectural decisions and user feedback trends.
450: - Record issues for later rather than fixing unrelated bugs mid-task.
451: - Before starting complex tasks:
452:   - Search the journal for relevant past experiences.
453:   - Document architectural decisions and their outcomes.
454:   - Track recurring user feedback or collaboration patterns.
455:   - When you find something unrelated but worth fixing, log it instead of fixing it immediately.
456:   - Review the journal weekly to reinforce learning and memory.
457: 
458: ---
459: 
460: ## 🔬 Research and Recommendations
461: 
462: When researching tools, technologies, or approaches:
463: 
464: - **Document comprehensively** - Create dedicated markdown files with findings.
465: - **Provide context** - Executive summary tailored to CJ's specific workflow and preferences.
466: - **Compare systematically** - Use tables/matrices for clear comparison.
467: - **Recommendation clarity** - Be explicit about what you recommend and why.
468: - **Ask clarifying questions** - End research with specific questions to guide next steps.
469: - **Don't assume CJ's workflow** - Ask about primary tools and preferences before making assumptions.
470: 
471: ---
472: 
473: ## 🗄️ Code Archeology & Cleanup
474: 
475: ### When Making Changes, Look for Obsolete Code
476: 
477: While working in a file, actively search for:
478: 
479: 1. **Unused imports** - Remove immediately
480: 2. **Commented-out code** - Delete (it's in git history)
481: 3. **Dead functions** - Delete if no references found
482: 4. **Backup files** - Never commit
483: 5. **TODO comments older than 3 months** - Convert to GitHub issues or delete
484: 6. **Deprecated patterns** - Refactor to current standards
485: 
486: ### Spotting Obsolete Code Patterns
487: 
488: These patterns indicate obsolete code to delete:
489: 
490: - Files with "old", "legacy", "deprecated" in name
491: - Commented-out imports or functions
492: - Duplicate implementations of same interface
493: - Multiple files exporting the same class name
494: 
495: ### Regular Maintenance (Requested)
496: 
497: Periodically ask to run architectural reviews:
498: 
499: > "Would you like me to scan for duplicate code and obsolete files?"
500: 
501: This prevents accumulation of technical debt.
502: 
503: ---
504: 
505: ## 🏗️ Architectural Hygiene
506: 
507: ### Pre-Implementation Checklist
508: 
509: Before implementing a new feature or significant change:
510: 
511: - [ ] **Search for existing implementations**: `grep -r "class Name"`, `find . -name "*keyword*"`
512: - [ ] **Review similar features**: Understand patterns already in use
513: - [ ] **Identify shared logic**: Will this duplicate any existing functionality?
514: - [ ] **Plan for reuse**: How can this be designed to avoid future duplication?
515: 
516: ### Post-Implementation Checklist
517: 
518: After implementing a feature:
519: 
520: - [ ] **Delete obsolete code**: If replacing functionality, delete old implementation
521: - [ ] **Update all references**: Ensure no dangling imports to deleted code
522: - [ ] **Extract duplicates**: If logic is similar to existing code, refactor to share
523: - [ ] **Clean up test scaffolding**: Delete ad-hoc test scripts if proper tests exist
524: - [ ] **Update documentation**: Remove references to deleted/obsolete files
525: - [ ] **Verify exports**: Remove deleted files from `index.ts` barrel exports
526: 
527: ### Red Flags - Request Architectural Review
528: 
529: If you notice any of these, suggest an architectural review:
530: 
531: - Multiple files with same/similar class names
532: - Same schema/type defined in 2+ places
533: - 3+ test testing similar functionality
534: - Logic duplicated across files (>50 lines)
535: 
536: **Phrase to use:**
537: > "I noticed [pattern]. Would you like me to do an architectural review to identify duplication and suggest consolidation?"
538: 
539: ---

````markdown
  1: # Contribution Workflow
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Contribution Guidelines**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `{Project}.API` |
 13: | `{Project}.AppHost` | Aspire AppHost | `{Project}.AppHost` |
 14: | `{Project}ApiClient` | Generated API client | `{Project}ApiClient` |
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Branch Strategy
 19: 
 20: ```
 21: main                    # Default branch
 22: ├── feature/xxx         # New features
 23: ├── bugfix/xxx          # Bug fixes
 24: └── refactor/xxx        # Code improvements
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: ## Commit Convention
 28: 
 29: ```
 30: type(scope): subject
 31: 
 32: body (optional)
 33: 
 34: footer (optional)
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
 38: 
 39: **Examples**:
 40: ```
 41: feat(events): add prayer-relative scheduling
 42: fix(federation): correct HTTP signature validation
 43: docs(api): update endpoint documentation
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ## Pull Request Process
 47: 
 48: 1. Create a branch from `main`
 49: 2. Implement changes with tests
 50: 3. Ensure all tests pass: `dotnet test`
 51: 4. Ensure code formatting: `dotnet format`
 52: 5. Create PR with description and linked issue
 53: 6. Request review from maintainers
 54: 7. Address feedback
 55: 8. Squash and merge when approved
 56: 
 57: ## Issue Templates
 58: 
 59: - **Bug Report**: Describe bug, steps to reproduce, expected behavior
 60: - **Feature Request**: Describe need, proposed solution, alternatives
 61: - **Task**: Technical work without user-facing change
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## DTO Change Workflow (API → Blazor Client)
 66: 
 67: When making changes to DTOs in the API project, follow this specific workflow to ensure the Blazor client is properly updated.
 68: 
 69: ### Why This Workflow Matters
 70: 
 71: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for orchestration, which:
 72: 1. Fetches secrets from Infisical and injects them as environment variables
 73: 2. Starts all projects in the correct order
 74: 3. **Triggers OpenAPI schema regeneration** in the API project on startup
 75: 4. **NSwag watches for schema changes** and automatically regenerates the Blazor API client
 76: 
 77: **Key Point**: You must run Aspire to regenerate the client. Building alone won't update the generated client code.
 78: 
 79: ### The Vicious Cycle Problem
 80: 
 81: Understanding **why** this workflow exists prevents frustrating debugging sessions.
 82: 
 83: #### The Problem: Build Errors Block Client Regeneration
 84: 
 85: When you change DTOs in the API and then try to build the **full solution**, you enter a vicious cycle:
 86: 
 87: ```
 88: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 89: │                    ❌ THE VICIOUS CYCLE                              │
 90: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 91: │                                                                     │
 92: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
 93: │     ↓                                                               │
 94: │  2. You try to build the FULL SOLUTION                              │
 95: │     ↓                                                               │
 96: │  3. ❌ BUILD FAILS - Blazor references the OLD generated client     │
 97: │     │   (The generated client doesn't have the new property yet)    │
 98: │     ↓                                                               │
 99: │  4. ❌ ASP.NET API won't run (solution didn't build)                │
100: │     ↓                                                               │
101: │  5. ❌ swagger.json can't regenerate (API isn't running)            │
102: │     ↓                                                               │
103: │  6. ❌ NSwag can't update the client (no new schema)                │
104: │     ↓                                                               │
105: │  7. ❌ Generated client stays outdated                              │
106: │     ↓                                                               │
107: │  8. ❌ Build errors persist → BACK TO STEP 3                        │
108: │                                                                     │
109: │  💀 YOU ARE STUCK IN AN INFINITE LOOP                               │
110: │                                                                     │
111: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
112: ```
113: 
114: #### The Solution: Build API Separately First
115: 
116: By building **only the API project** first, you break the cycle:
117: 
118: ```
119: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
120: │                    ✅ THE CORRECT WORKFLOW                           │
121: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
122: │                                                                     │
123: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
124: │     ↓                                                               │
125: │  2. Build ONLY the API project: `dotnet build {Project}.API`          │
126: │     ↓                                                               │
127: │  3. ✅ API builds successfully (no Blazor dependency issues)        │
128: │     ↓                                                               │
129: │  4. Run Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`              │
130: │     ↓                                                               │
131: │  5. ✅ API starts and generates new swagger.json                    │
132: │     ↓                                                               │
133: │  6. ✅ NSwag detects changes, regenerates client                    │
134: │     ↓                                                               │
135: │  7. ✅ Generated client now has the new property                    │
136: │     ↓                                                               │
137: │  8. NOW update Blazor services/components                           │
138: │     ↓                                                               │
139: │  9. ✅ Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`              │
140: │                                                                     │
141: │  🎉 SUCCESS - No build errors!                                      │
142: │                                                                     │
143: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
144: ```
145: 
146: #### Common Trap: Updating Blazor Services Too Early
147: 
148: A particularly frustrating mistake is updating **Blazor services that interact with the generated API client** before the client is regenerated:
149: 
150: ```
151: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
152: │              ❌ THE SERVICE UPDATE TRAP                              │
153: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
154: │                                                                     │
155: │  Scenario: You add `Description` property to `EventDto`             │
156: │                                                                     │
157: │  1. You update EventDto in API (✅ correct)                         │
158: │     ↓                                                               │
159: │  2. You update EventService in Blazor to use `.Description`         │
160: │     ↓                                                               │
161: │  3. ❌ ERROR: 'EventDto' does not contain 'Description'             │
162: │     │                                                               │
163: │     │   WHY? The generated client ({Project}ApiClient.cs) still       │
164: │     │   has the OLD EventDto without Description!                   │
165: │     │                                                               │
166: │     │   Your service references: Generated.EventDto (OLD)           │
167: │     │   You expect:              Generated.EventDto.Description     │
168: │     │   Reality:                 Property doesn't exist yet         │
169: │     ↓                                                               │
170: │  4. Build fails on BOTH sides:                                      │
171: │     • API side: Works fine (your DTO has the property)              │
172: │     • Blazor side: Fails (generated client is outdated)             │
173: │                                                                     │
174: │  💡 The generated client is OUT OF SYNC with the API!               │
175: │                                                                     │
176: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
177: ```
178: 
179: **Rule of Thumb**:
180: - **API-only changes** → Build API only, run Aspire, then update Blazor
181: - **UI-only changes** (no DTO changes) → Can work directly in Blazor
182: - **Both API + Blazor changes** → Follow the full checklist, API first
183: 
184: ### Standard Workflow
185: 
186: ```
187: API Changes → Build API → Run Aspire → Client Regenerates → Update Blazor UI
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Process Checklist for DTO Changes
191: 
192: Follow this checklist whenever you add/modify DTO properties:
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: ## DTO Change Checklist
196: 
197: ### 1. Application Layer Changes
198: - [ ] Add/update properties in `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/` files
199: - [ ] Update `{Entity}Dto.cs` (full details)
200: - [ ] Update `{Entity}ListDto.cs` (list view) if applicable
201: - [ ] Update `Create{Entity}Dto.cs` / `Update{Entity}Dto.cs` if applicable
202: 
203: ### 2. Mapping & Data Access
204: - [ ] Update `MappingProfile.cs` if new navigation properties
205: - [ ] Update Repository `.Include()` statements if loading related data
206: - [ ] Update Handler if new processing logic needed
207: 
208: ### 3. Build & Regenerate
209: - [ ] Build API project only: `dotnet build {Project}.API`
210: - [ ] Start Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`
211: - [ ] Wait for swagger.json to regenerate (automatic on API startup)
212: - [ ] NSwag regenerates client automatically (watches schema file)
213: 
214: ### 4. Blazor UI Updates
215: - [ ] NOW update Blazor components to use new properties
216: - [ ] Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`
217: - [ ] Test the changes in browser
218: ```
219: 
220: ### Quick Fix: If You Forgot the Workflow
221: 
222: If you already updated Blazor UI before running Aspire and the generated client is missing properties:
223: 
224: **Option 1: Proper Fix (Recommended)**
225: ```powershell
226: # Stop any running instances
227: # Run Aspire to regenerate everything
228: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
229: ```
230: 
231: **Option 2: Manual Fix (Quick Workaround)**
232: Manually add the missing properties to the generated client file as a temporary fix, then run Aspire later to properly regenerate.
233: 
234: ### Architecture Diagram
235: 
236: ```
237: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
238: │                         .NET Aspire Orchestration                    │
239: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
240: │                                                                     │
241: │  1. Aspire Starts                                                   │
242: │     └── Fetches secrets from Infisical                              │
243: │     └── Injects environment variables to all projects               │
244: │                                                                     │
245: │  2. API Project Starts                                              │
246: │     └── Generates swagger.json (OpenAPI schema)                     │
247: │     └── Schema reflects current DTO structure                       │
248: │                                                                     │
249: │  3. Blazor Project Watches                                          │
250: │     └── NSwag detects swagger.json changes                          │
251: │     └── Regenerates API client ({Project}ApiClient.cs)                │
252: │                                                                     │
253: │  4. Blazor Components                                               │
254: │     └── Use the regenerated client with new properties              │
255: │                                                                     │
256: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
257: ```
258: 
259: ### Common Mistakes
260: 
261: | Mistake | Why It Fails | Fix |
262: |---------|--------------|-----|
263: | Build solution without running Aspire | swagger.json not regenerated | Run Aspire first |
264: | Update Blazor before API | Generated client missing new properties | Follow the checklist order |
265: | Manually edit generated files | Changes overwritten on next regeneration | Add to source DTOs, regenerate |
266: | Skip the MappingProfile update | AutoMapper doesn't map new properties | Always update profile |
267:

272: - [BLAZOR.md](BLAZOR.md) - Blazor client architecture
273: - [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) - DTO patterns and conventions
````
